### Weapon art — the descriptive section as it stood through roster-r12


**Landed state (read this first; the history below is record):** the full-roster redesign + sigil commission landed 2026-10-25 through the artist-kit route (returns #1–#2 in `deliveries/`, promotion chain `e9662ebf…` → `59b87b17…` → `dccb4892…` → `3bc1fbee…` → stamp `d09ffc12…`): 22 weapon blocks in canonical `build([...])` grammar pre-scale, 19 coverings rebaked by `.qa/bake-rows.mjs`, chain segs re-mapped, sigils realized one-KC-per-weapon, nine shot kinds in `SHOTS_ART` with the affinity locals, the knives volley and the tome trio rotation in the sim, copy-kind throws at centroid pivots. The grammar described below (flat fills, locked palette + locals, legibility lock, shaft doctrine, prescriptive handheld spec, lead/headLead taxonomy) is now PRESCRIPTIVE from the landed art; the close draft ratifies it item by item. `ingest.mjs` stands dormant/superseded. What follows is the section as it stood through the landing, kept as record.

What follows **describes current practice**; none of it is prescribed. The 2026-10-18 locked convention (palette of five, shaft doctrine, per-family proportions, supplier/selector process, squash test) is preserved verbatim in the archive — its amber `#c9a227` no longer appears in any merged art, and the v1.0 batch did not go through its process.

**What the art currently does.** Flat fills; one uniform ink outline (`#2e2b22`); no gradients, no texture, no glow. Colors in use: wood `#7a4a2a`, dark wood `#4f3220`, steel `#8fa3b5`, near-white `#eaf6ff` (cutting/striking faces — and PAPER: the tome's pages, owner-named extension), and light blue `#9fe0ff` (the orb body, the tome gem, the scroll sparkles). **Gold is RETIRED from art (sweep-r15, owner option B, 2026-10-27): every former gold shape — 21 `KG`-tagged plus 7 ingest-era hexes — now wears dark wood `#4f3220`; `KG` survives only as the carrier-less sigil fallback constant.** Circular elements are cut as 32-gons (roundness class, same day: nine true circles recut to 32; elongated wraps are exempt by the aspect gate and keep their authored contours). The scroll (2026-10-23) adds the first PER-WEAPON owner-reference extension: KT `#ecd5a3` parchment, KTS `#c9a35a`, KR `#b8352c` ribbon, KRD `#8f2a24` — declared scroll-local inside its INGR zone, the six shared consts untouched; **the convention close must ratify (or veto) the per-weapon reference-color class.** Squint-test-at-120px and minimum-feature-15/1000 were the old legibility rules; nobody has re-checked the v1.0 batch against them.

**Owner additions 2026-10-21 — PRESCRIPTIVE for every future batch and every new weapon (the rest of this section stays descriptive until the convention itself locks): the generic handheld weapon spec.** (1) **Length ceiling:** no weapon spine is longer than `LT` — the shared heavy-four length (the mace's tip, ≈113.4 pre-scale, ≈147.5px as played). Owner: "a max length of weapons, where a weapon can not be longer than this, per default … its about the lenght of spear,axe hammer … it looks good for the eye". Skills that grow length later are a mechanics topic, never an exception to the authored rest length. The crossbow was the one spine past the ceiling (len 116) and was rescaled to LT the same day at owner word ("fix the crossbow") — uniform downscale, proportions untouched (sim-data change; **Measured facts**). (2) **One shaft size:** generic handheld weapons share the shaft doctrine's universal width (~11.5u full width, ~15 as played); a deviation is only a named, disclosed owner pick for a very specific design — the exception mechanism already exists as practice (axe2-D's 13.5u haft, chosen on the true-scale sheet, "owner taste overrides the doctrine default"). (3) **Plain butt:** the handle bottom the bot wields is the handle brown `#7a4a2a` with no patterns and no other colors — this settles the 2026-10-18 palette's dark-wood "butts, grips" assignment against merged practice (every merged butt is wood; the axe's gold pommel/collar left at v0.8.4). Owner: "the bottom of the handle where the weapon is wielded by the bot should just be brown color as we are using in most of the handles right now, with no patterns/design other colors". (4) **Flat butt cut:** the shaft bottom is cut flat, not round — the tuck clip hides it in play anyway ("the bottom of the shaft should not be round, as it is going under the bots body anyyways, so nobody will see it"); the two places it IS visible (VS poster, contact sheets — neither tuck-clips) read a flat cut as a normal handle end. The v1.0 builder batch was already flat; the three ingested veterans (hammer, dagger, axe) keep their rounded caps until their next art touch — grandfathered, not re-authored for this rule. (5) **Directional asymmetry declares `lead`** (owner decision 2026-10-22 — the katana "appears to spin backwards" observation): art with a directional reading — a chisel blade, a hook, a curve whose **business contour** (the cutting edge of a blade, the BEAK of a hook) looks to one side of the spine — declares `lead: ±1` on its WEAPONS row (the spine-local side that contour bears), and the placement layer mirrors art+hitbox together on spin sign so the contour leads the motion at both spin directions and through every parry flip. Katana and scythe are both −1, the reference implementations of the two contour classes — **for hooks the owner's playtest is the ruling doctrine: shipped mouth-forward (+1), it read as "spinning the wrong way from the beginning"; the beak must lead, the mouth scoops behind.** **Radial asymmetry never declares it** — art whose off-axis mass faces away from the body (the bow/crossbow bellies, the knives' outward blades) would mirror inward, wrong at both signs; symmetric art declares nothing; chain weapons are forbidden it by boot throw (mirror × tie unproven until a real case). Artists author in the canonical orientation — edge on the declared side — and the engine flips; `.qa/leadproof.mjs` extends (PROBES/CELLS) for every new flagged weapon. *

(5b) **Along-chord asymmetry declares `headLead`** (owner decision 2026-10-22 — "i think the javelin should also flip around like scythe and katana"): a weapon whose BUSINESS END sits at one chord extreme (a spear head) declares `headLead: ±1` (the d-end bearing the head; the javelin's is the d = len end, +1), and the placement layer d-mirrors art+hitbox about the **centred rim grip** — the chord midpoint, the mirror's fixed point, which is why the trait is tangential-hold-ONLY (a radial grip at d 0 would slide off the body; boot throw) — so the head always points the way the grip travels (kinematics: v·d̂ = bodyR·spin). One flip factor drives one declared axis: `lead` XOR `headLead`, never both, never on chains (boot throws). The javelin rider's "bilaterally symmetric, no lead" guidance stays true — its asymmetry is along the chord, not across it, which is exactly the case `lead` cannot fix and `headLead` exists for. (6) **The sigil — one carrier-colored element per weapon** (owner decision 2026-10-23, his words: "i dont want it to be like all weapons have the same dot or similar, i want it to make sense for the weapons … dont just invent something on the sword just for the sake of givinig it a color, like put a string or something stupid on the sword, which doesnt make sense"): exactly ONE diegetic element per weapon renders in the wielding fighter's cast color via the `KC` tag (recolor an existing plausible element first — band, gem, hub, binding, seal; add the smallest plausible ownership element only where none exists, interior-ink preferred; never on KP; owner-reference colors like the scroll's KR ribbon are not sigil material). The mark map lives in `roster-redesign-brief.md`; the mechanism is the `drawWeapon`/`drawWeaponChain` swap (renderer-only, gold fallback for carrier-less renders). Sigil = the vocabulary word (SPEC's "mark" stays reserved for body identity).

**Two art paths coexist — RESOLVED at roster-r12 (close item 2a): the in-file poly builder via the artist-kit route IS the canonical path; `ingest.mjs` stands dormant/superseded. (2026-10-25 alignment note; the subsection below is the record as it stood.)**

**Two art paths coexist (undecided which is canonical):**
1. **`ingest.mjs` — the SVG merge gate:** validate → normalize → cover (0.5u grid, ink inflated 1.5u = the drawn outline counted as body, RMIN 2.0, ε disclosed) → combat gauntlet on a temp copy → merge only on PASS. Produced `INGR_HAMMER`, `INGR_DAGGER`, `INGR_AXE` (all with gauntlet records in the archive) and `INGR_BOW` (blob shape matches; **no gauntlet record**). Its merge template hardcodes the melee ability (+0.7 DMG) — a launcher candidate needs a post-merge edit. Its orientation rule: an end tapering to ~zero width is the tip; only when neither end tapers does the thinner blunt end read as the grip.
2. **The in-file `build()` poly builder (v1.0 batch):** weapons authored as plain polygons in spine-local (d, l) units; covering circles generated from the same polygons (1.5u sample grid, silhouette inflated **1.2u**, min r **4**, dedupe 0.72) — different parameters from ingest, **no ε disclosure, no gauntlet** for any of the nine. Drawing and hitbox still cannot drift (same source polys), but uncovered-sliver depth is unmeasured.

**Undecided (open question):** palette (**settled at owner word 2026-10-27: gold retired from art (sweep to KD, sweep-r15), blue IN, amber long retired — convention-close item 1a carries the amended lock**), the process (batches + contact sheets + owner-picks, or direct authoring?), whether the builder path must pass the ingest gate retroactively, per-family proportions beyond the decided ceiling and shaft size (head shares, guard treatment — see the archive grammar). The owner decides; until then new art follows whichever path the owner's next pick implies, inside the prescriptive spec above.

**Edge-leading mirror — katana + scythe (2026-10-22, owner observation and decision: "most weapon looks the same spinning left and right, which is fine, but i just noticed katana, since it has a sharp side on its blade, the weapon appears to spin backwards … i was thinking if we could flip the weapon when its turn, to prevent this, and also for future weapons"; built as the opt-in per-weapon `lead` trait after the proposal consultation — owner: "go". Kinematic ground (proven at birth, 64 angles × both signs):
`wAngle += spin·dt` makes the local **+l side lead when spin > 0**. **Mechanism, one source:** `leadFlip(wId, spin)` beside `spineFrame`, exported on `geom` — consumed by the sim's collision (parryGap pose objects gained `fp`; bladeVsBody, the resolver's D0/D1 and the swat check pass `leadFlip(w, spin)` from the live substep spin), the renderer (`polyPath`/`drawWeapon`/`drawWeaponOn`/`drawWeaponOf` carry the factor; `view[i].flip` is binary from the LATEST tick's spin — never blended; the pop-in centre POPC mirrors with the art), the stills (latch stores `fp: leadFlip(e.aW, e.aSp)`, the view override consumes it) and every harness recompute. **Events carry the flip truth:** conditional `aSp` on hits, `aSp`/`bSp` on parries (ENTRY signed spins, captured pre-resolver/pre-flip beside the entry angles — the audit recomputes the mirror the blades had when they touched, not the recoil's), `fSp` on swats — flagged weapons ONLY, so unflagged event JSON stays byte-identical and the delta stays surgical. **Boot guards:** `lead` must be ±1 (loud throw); **chain weapons are forbidden the flag** (mirror × tie/articulation unproven until a real case — loud throw).

## gates a pasted block is measured against (no silent fixes)

1. `KC` count === 1 — exactly one diegetic sigil, never on `KP`.
2. radial weapons: art `maxD` ≤ LT = 113.44 (pre-scale units).
3. mace: `maxD` must equal LT — it is the sentinel every `len: LT` row inherits.
4. keepers (`cls K`): drawn-union mask must stay pixel-identical, else the row ghosts and the
   ledger + landing list move (that is information, not a failure — the owner may want it).
5. scale is **detected**: the audit divides `maxD` by `S` (and by `KX` for the crossbow), so a
   pre-scale INGR block lands as-is; if the extent matches the canonical `len` under neither
   reading the paste is ambiguous → ask, never guess.
6. launch anchors stay where they shipped (bow off 26, crossbow off 34, knives off 38, tome
   off 10, scroll off 11, staff/wand `fire: 'tip'`, chain joint distances).
7. canonical `spinclash-preview.html` md5 before === after (read-only proof).

### `scratch/claude-design-prompt.md` (verbatim, as purged)

# SPINCLASH — weapon artist commission v2 (kit route, one weapon per message)

> v1 (2026-10-25 era) pasted the 244 KB canonical `spinclash-preview.html` into
> the session. Superseded 2026-10-24 at owner vote: the base is now the small
> self-contained **artist kit** (`scratch/artist-kit.html`, ~39 KB) — same
> medium, same conventions, paste-able. The kit is generated from the live
> proposal set; its blocks are canonical `build([...])` grammar in draw units.

You are the weapon artist for SPINCLASH, a dependency-free browser physics
auto-battler. Fighters are discs (bodyR 64) that spin a weapon around
themselves; the art is read at a glance, in motion, at roughly 60–150 px.

The owner pastes into this conversation: **this prompt + the complete artist
kit**. The kit is the single source of truth for the medium: conventions
header, helpers (`rect` / `star` / `build`), the 22 `INGR_*` blocks, the
`IDENTITY` table, and a self-viewer. Read it before designing. If anything
below disagrees with the kit, the kit wins — say so.

## The loop

1. On receiving this prompt, reply in **3 lines or fewer**: acknowledge the
   rules and ask which weapon. Do not design anything yet. The roster (22):
   `bow, hammer, dagger, axe, sword, spear, mace, shield, staff, wand,
   crossbow, boomerang, shuriken, flail, nunchaku, scythe, katana, knives,
   javelin, tome, scroll, orb`.
2. The owner names **one** weapon. You design that weapon only — never others,
   never the roster in bulk. He iterates in-session ("fatter head", "sigil
   elsewhere"); the owner IS the question loop.
3. You reply with the 3-part delivery: **note** (what the look does, one
   paragraph) → **code** (the complete `const INGR_<ID> = build([...])` block,
   draw units, drop-in replacement for that weapon's kit block) → **audit
   line** (measured, not claimed): `KC ×1 · reach <n> vs LT 147.47 · anchors
   kept/moved-with-note · traits kept/flipped-with-note · chain coherent/n-a`.
4. In-session revisions may emit only the changed block + fresh audit. The
   **final delivery is the COMPLETE kit file** with every accepted change in
   place — the owner hands that file to the implementer whole.

## Rules (the kit header carries the full doctrine; these are the hard edges)

- **Edit only the 22 `INGR_*` blocks and their `observed:` header lines.**
  Conventions, helpers, `IDENTITY`, viewer, palette consts: frozen context.
  No reformatting of untouched blocks — the implementer diff-audits your
  return against the pristine base, and formatting noise hides real deltas.
- **Geometry is yours.** Silhouettes may change freely (that is the point of
  the pass). Hitboxes are NOT yours: never author covering circles; a changed
  silhouette ghosts until the implementer rebakes it — designed cost, not a
  defect. `IDENTITY` (len / hold / fire anchor / lead / headLead) is shipped
  truth: row values change only at the owner's in-session word, and a moved
  business contour flips its `lead`/`headLead` sign WITH the art plus an
  `observed:` note (katana edge −1, scythe beak −1, javelin head +1).
- **Sigil doctrine:** exactly ONE diegetic element per weapon wears `KC` —
  never on a `KP` face, never a sticker, recolor-first. The seeded block's
  header names the current sigil; keep the doctrine when art moves around it.
- **Caps:** d-axis extent (reach) ≤ LT = 147.47 draw units, every weapon; the
  mace envelope is the sentinel — its reach EQUALS LT, never move it.
  Launchers keep their declared exit (bow off 33.8, crossbow 44.2, knives 49.4,
  tome 13, scroll 14.3, staff/wand `fire:'tip'`); tangential grips stay at the
  chord middle. Chain weapons: segment shape-ranges + joint d's stay coherent
  with any re-authored shapes; counts and hinge order never change.
- **Medium:** flat fills, locked palette, no gradients/texture/glow/opacity;
  the renderer adds the only ink (3px round-join around every shape); 4–14
  shapes; nothing solid thinner than ~1.5 draw units (thinner = paint, third
  element `1`); curves as generously-sampled polylines; hand-made, not
  generated (tapers, asymmetry, material logic).
- **The `chain:` header line is MACHINE-READ** (flail, nunchaku): the owner's
  arena page and the implementer's splice parse segs + joints from it, so keep
  the kit's exact format — `chain: segs shapes a-b / c / …, joints at d x / y
  / z` — and update it in the same breath as any re-counted shape list. The
  arena then re-maps segments live and swings your new art; a *moved joint*
  is sim data: the arena refuses it (kept staged) and the implementer
  reconciles it at landing.
- **Never generate, request or reference images.** You design blind from
  coordinates and the doctrine; the owner's eyes live on the kit's self-viewer
  and the implementer's in-game arena page.
- **No questions in the final delivery.** Judgment calls that survive get
  one-line `observed: …` notes in that weapon's header.
- Determinism: no `Math.random` / `Date.now` / `performance.now` anywhere.
  `WEAPON_IDS` frozen: same 22, same order.

## Why the file you return is safe to hand over

The implementer splices your blocks verbatim into the game's staging set,
runs the seven gates (KC ×1 · radial reach ≤ LT · mace sentinel · keeper-union
pixel identity · scale detection · launch anchors · canonical md5 unchanged),
re-renders the review sheet and the in-game arena page, re-bakes every ghosted
covering, and lands the roster in one batch after the owner's playtest. Your
blocks are canonical grammar, so nothing is re-authored downstream — what you
emit is what ships.

## Shots — the flying art (owner rulings 2026-10-24, scope: all kinds)

The kit's SHOTS zone lists every kind with its launcher, hitbox `r` and speed,
plus today's look. Rules beyond the weapon doctrine:

- **Shot-local grammar:** origin = projectile centre, +x = flight direction,
  DRAW units, `build([...])`. Spinning kinds (spark, spell) spin in code.
- **Accent doctrine (owner vote):** exactly ONE diegetic accent element per
  kind wears `KC` — dyed fletching, cord wrap, glyph core. Never the whole
  body, never on a KP edge. The shot must still read as *what* it is.
- **Stay inside `r`** (the halo disc inks the true hitbox; visible-contact-
  first applies in flight). Art that must exceed it: disclose the whiff band
  in the header, measured.
- **Copy kinds are NOT yours:** star, boom, javelin fly as the wielder's own
  weapon polys by engine rule — redesigning the weapon redesigns its throw.
  Never author SHOT_STAR / SHOT_BOOM / SHOT_JAVELIN.
- **knife is a new kind** (splits off bolt): ONE knife, the exact look of one
  of the weapon's three knives. (The owner is considering a 3-knife volley —
  one per fan direction — as a mechanics ruling; design the single knife so a
  volley of three reads clean.)
- **spell is shared** by tome AND scroll: one flat rune-glyph visual, no glow,
  no gradient. The old page sheet and parchment roll are retired by it.
- Deliver shot blocks as `const SHOT_<KIND> = build([...])` inside the SHOTS
  zone, header line per block: `/* shot <kind> · r <n> · accent: <element> ·
  observed: … */`. Audit line adds: `r-fit ok/disclosed`.
- **Paint flag for shots (lever 2):** third element `1` = no-ink paint. Glow
  layers = simplified silhouette offsets of the head region behind the body
  (array-first), mid KB / outer KP, fixed tints, never carrier-mixed, never
  gradient/opacity. Weapon blocks must not use the flag. Muzzle flash and
  speed-stretch are implementer-side — never author them.
- **Animation contract (owner 2026-10-25, levers 1+2):** third-element flags on
  shots: `1` = glow paint (no ink) · `2` = alternate frame of the preceding
  shape, no ink · `3` = alternate frame, inked. Alt pairs swap every 4 ticks
  (two-frame flicker). Flicker scope: glow layers and the OUTER tongue only —
  inner structure stays stable so the silhouette never mushes. Implementer
  dials (glow pulse, tail sway, speed-stretch) apply themselves: never author
  them. DOCTRINE: animate the tail and the glow, NEVER the head — the head
  carries the hitbox disc and the eye anchors contact truth on it.

Meanwhile `grow()` feeds two separate accumulators, `spinGain = sk.spin + ab.spin` and `dmgGain = sk.dmg + ab.dmg`. Cross that with the roster, verified weapon by weapon including the check that **orb is melee, not a launcher**:
**the 10 projectile weapons are exactly the 10 weapons carrying `{spin: 0.70, dmg: 0}`, and the 12 melee weapons are exactly the 12 carrying `{spin: 0, dmg: 0.7}`** — a perfect 1:1. Consequence: Speedy (+0.30 spin) holding any projectile weapon has `dmgGain = 0 + 0 = 0`, so **its shots do base damage for the entire battle, forever**, while Heavy (+0.9 dmg) holding the same weapon grows +0.9 per hit. Melee splits +0.7 versus +1.6 per hit. *(4) The fair test of the two skills — like-for-like, shield cells excluded, 384 cells / 6,355 rounds.* Speedy melee vs Heavy melee: **34.4% Speedy** (108 cells, 2,073 rounds). Speedy projectile vs Heavy projectile: **24.9%** (86 cells, 1,125 rounds). Those two diagonals are the only rows that compare the skills with the weapon class held constant, and both favour Heavy — **65.6% of melee mirrors and 75.1% of projectile mirrors**. So the answer to the question the cast entry owed to this run is measured: **+0.30 spin is not equal in value to +0.9 damage, and the two are not even parallel axes** — damage reaches both offence paths, spin reaches neither.
Off-diagonal for scale: Speedy melee vs Heavy projectile 82.7% Speedy; Speedy projectile vs Heavy melee **2.4%**. Weapon class outweighs fighter class by roughly 30 points. *(5) Per-weapon, Speedy's win rate holding the weapon:* scythe 72.2, hammer 69.0, axe 68.4, mace 60.5, nunchaku 60.3, katana 56.0, flail 55.1, sword 54.2, boomerang 48.7, dagger 43.1, orb 39.0, staff 17.8, javelin 14.3, scroll 10.6, bow 9.4, crossbow 6.8, knives 5.6, wand 4.7, tome 4.4 (shield, spear and shuriken arrive with Part 5). Group gap: **melee 55.7% versus projectile 12.0%, 43.3 points**. Boomerang is the one projectile exception. The cause is in the shot ledger — Part 1 alone threw 415,580 shots, landed 38,300 and lost 243,208 to the rim, so **about 9% of shots ever reach a body**. *(6) The shield cannot win a round, and its trait is inert.* Its own player-facing `line` reads `'parries only · no projectile'` and the sim gates it to knock-only contact ("projectile spines, the shield … deals NO spine damage, whatever its hold"), so this is deliberate design rather than a defect. Measured consequence: **Heavy holding the shield won 0 of 229 rounds.** And because `grow()` fires only on a damaging hit, the shield's `trait: { spin: 0.0, dmg: 0.7 }` **can never activate** — it is inert data, as is its wielder's fighter skill.
This is also the mechanism behind open question 1's `shield+shield` non-termination: neither side is capable of a KO, so the cell can only ever exhaust the budget. Open question 4 ("what is a weapon that cannot damage *for*?") now carries that number. *(7) The two live reds at matrix scale.* **Law 3's band class** — overlaps NOT explained by the mirror mechanism — measured 14.673 / 20.754 / 14.488 / 17.604 / 15.745px worst across the five landed slices **[COMPLETED 2026-10-28: Part 5 adds 13.956px, so all six slices are red — worst 20.754px, 3.5× the disclosed limit]**, against a disclosed band of <6px and a 22.83px floor measured with the resolver disabled. It appears in every slice including Part 6, which contains no chain weapon at all, so the "the mirror test is too narrow for chain flips" reading does not cover it; frequency stays trivial (2,877 visible overlaps in 72.8M fight-ticks, 0.006-0.01% per slice), so this is a tail-depth question, not a rate question. It re-opens the katana+shuriken rework item's dilemma at 2.4-3.5x the numbers: either the band's 6px line moves with a recorded justification, or the resolver does. **Projectile law 4s** printed `double departures 3`, confined to Part 1 — zero across the 811,998 shots of Parts 2, 3, 4 and 6. **[SUPERSEDED 2026-10-28 when Part 5 landed: they are NOT confined to Part 1. Part 5 carries 2 more, for 5 across the complete baseline — 1 in ~296,475 of 1,482,374 shots thrown — with Parts 2, 3, 4 and 6 still at zero. Part 6 threw 310,411 shots and found none, so shot volume does not predict them.]**
The label is wrong: the counter is `shotDeathDup` and it conflates `addGone()` firing twice for one sid (line 372) with a shot marked gone yet still in flight at battle end (line 769); neither is a departure. Shot ids are provably battle-unique (`++G.shotSid`, and the sim's own comment "sids never repeat"), so id reuse is ruled out; the leading hypothesis is same-tick ordering — a rim/land/swat death landing in the same tick as a round roll's `clearedSids` sweep, or as the battle end. Damage-side laws are spotless, so no gameplay effect is indicated. *(8) Both reds are un-attributed, and that is the owed next step.* The harness reports counts and worst values but never says where: no cell, no seed, no tick. Localising either needs an attribution edit — cell/seed/tick for the band-class worst overlap, and cell/seed/tick plus which of the two mechanisms for each `shotDeathDup` — applied after the baseline so all seven parts come from one instrument version, then a re-run of only the implicated slices. *(9) Integrity, and the caveat.* Across **3,224 battles · 6,935 rounds · 193,523 hits · 151,527 parries · 72,801,424 rendered fight-ticks · 1,363,242,755 substep poses** (403 of 484 cells, 83.3%):
phantom hits 0/193,523, phantom shot hits 0/97,073, swats without touch 0/74,006, parries without touch 0/151,527, substep-budget violations 0, off-point launches 0, melee hits by projectile weapons 0, **missing chain poses 0** — so every law recompute used the sim's own stored poses and none silently degraded to the rigid spine. All of it is measured at base damage 1 against 100 hp, which the owner called "just a test": absolute win rates will move when those constants move, but the structural facts will not — spin feeds no damage path, the projectile half of the roster inherits only its fighter's dmg, and the shield's trait can never fire. Part files and md5s: `scratch/m-01.txt` `4e0e06f4b938ab5d9a97f4688a55635f`, `m-02.txt` `b4334de39118bf4227bb6c31af41f7e0`, `m-03.txt` `80d2dc1ea508f305cb53a0db1e77110e`, `m-04.txt` `129bd14e419b51b06f39667eb4df8323`, `m-06.txt` `fc35bf31ae3e65ec68026d867fd2af51`, plus the owner's calibration capture `scratch/measure-quick-20261028-owner.txt` `0295f2030ee2ed896cf1d24724253b4b` **[file RETIRED in the 2026-10-28 pre-skills cleanup, owner go — the md5 above and its conclusion, that his Windows machine reproduced the sandbox number-for-number, are the surviving record; the artifact is not]**; Part 5 (`m-05.txt`) was in flight at the time of writing. **[ALL SIX part files RETIRED from the workspace later on 2026-10-28, owner go — he holds local copies. ### Retired from GAMES.md L444 (2026-10-28)

*Why it was retired: a pre-build cost estimate, superseded by the canonical's own `TRAIT / SKILL REGISTRY` block and by three measured landings (`skill-r29`, `seam-r30`, `pair-r31`); its spin-headroom paragraph survives in the dedicated `omegaCap` entry.*

**Skills-prep cost map — what a per-weapon skill actually has to touch, measured before any of it is built (2026-10-28, pre-skills cleanup; analysis only, no code changed, no plumbing added).** Written so the skills pass budgets correctly instead of discovering the expensive axis mid-design. **The growth site is already per-weapon.** `grow()` is the single place growth happens: it reads `FIGHTERS[idx].skill` and `WEAPONS[weapon].ability` ({spin, dmg}) and applies both on every damaging hit. Per-weapon skills are therefore a KEYING change, not a rewrite. **What a NEW axis costs** (the checklist, derived from the two that exist): a fighter field plus its per-round reset; the consumer site that reads it at hit or launch time; the legend/poster SPD-DMG boxes, which are a fixed three-channel display, so a fourth channel is a layout change; the `G.maxDmg` / `maxSpin` ridiculousness trackers; the fingerprint's hashed fields; and harness coverage — a new axis needs its own probe the way `lead` needed leadproof, or it ships unproven (the facing pass's vacuous-unextended-run trap is the precedent: a harness that passes without covering the new flag proves nothing).
**Cheap axes — launch-snapshotted.** Shot `r`, `speed`, `turn`, `bounce` and `len` are each copied onto the projectile at birth exactly like `dmg: f.dmg`, so a per-fighter multiplier is one line per axis with no boot-time consequence and no geometry rebuild. Knock is one hit-time read of a per-fighter field (today a global `CFG.hitKnock` 130). *[Corrected 2026-10-28: this entry originally named the field `CFG.knock` — the identifier was wrong, and the two skills-model entries that quoted it were wrong the same way; the value (130) and the analysis are unchanged. Measured while grounding the skill list: `CFG.hitKnock` is read at exactly two sites, `bladeVsBody` and `shotHitBody`, so knock is live on all 22 weapons.]* Any of these can be a skill without touching the bake. **Expensive axis — length growth, which the owner ruled 2026-10-28 IS in the skill vision.** `W.len` is consumed at BOOT to build SPAN, REACH, the scaled polys and the baked covering circles, so runtime growth needs a per-fighter length scale threaded through `spineFrame`, `bladeCircles` and the renderer, and it invalidates two boot-derived bounds: REACH (the parryGap prune bound) and MINR (the adaptive-substep budget), both computed once from authored len. The boot LEN_MIN/LT gate would NOT catch runtime growth, so the ceiling has to live inside the growth rule itself. Scoped, deliberately not built: the rule's shape (per hit? per round? capped where?) decides the plumbing, so nothing is threaded until the skill list exists.
This is the axis the owner's spectacle example named — "lets imagine spear geting longer each hit, suddenly it is hilariously long" — and it is the only one needing engineering rather than data. **Spin headroom (the ceiling the owner asked about).** `omegaCap: 140` is a sim-stability clamp, not a gameplay cap. Observed maximum across 30 naturals is 103.5 rad/s = base 3.5 + exactly 100 damaging hits × 1.0/hit (ability 0.70 + Speedy 0.30), so the clamp bites at 136.5 hits on that axis: **36.5 hits of headroom, and it clamps silently** — no readout, no event, the fighter just stops accelerating. Four options were put to the owner (leave it silent and record the headroom / measure the true stability limit read-only / raise it, which is a sim change owing its own kept pair / promote it to a visible gameplay cap); **the owner picked the measurement, and it superseded the framing above: the clamp is dormant, the binding ceiling is hp ÷ damage, and the stability limit is ω ≈ 258 at the worst pair — see the spin-ceiling measurement entry. The constant is no longer folklore.** **Launcher readiness.** After this landing the per-weapon shot surface is `revs` / `volley` / `cycle` / `copy` plus r/speed/turn/bounce/len/kind, all on the row: a skill that changes shot behaviour edits data or snapshots a per-fighter multiplier at launch, never the launcher.
**Owed before skills — SUPERSEDED 2026-10-28 by the no-balancing ruling: this now runs at the END of the skills pass, not before it.** The sanctioned `measure.mjs` run on the owner's machine (its 19 forced cells miss the dagger and the staff, and its expected counts predate both damage 1 and the facing pass) and the kit-route rebuild, which must carry the placement/reach rules and WDEF.

### Retired from GAMES.md L505 (2026-10-28)

*Why it was retired: a ruling that closed with no code change (+0.7 DMG was already the shipped value), so no mechanism is left to describe; its discharge notes live in Open design questions 6 and the roster row.*

**The dagger's growth axis ruled — +0.7 DMG stands, and the ruling changed no code (2026-10-28, owner go verbatim: "ok go", on the recommendation "+0.7 DMG". Of the two owner decisions the completed baseline was waiting on, this is the one that needed no compute.)** *(1) What the question actually was.* Not a magnitude — a **binary axis choice**, carried by the roster table's ⚠ since 2026-10-19. The dagger's trait was +0.7 **SPIN** in the owner-locked v0.7 growth-identity decision; the undocumented era flipped it to +0.7 DMG with no recorded reason, and the owner's 2026-10-28 pre-skills ruling was explicitly *neither ratify nor revert* — the skills pass decides. Under M2 a trait is weapon data, so either value is one number and no plumbing. The two branches: **+0.7 DMG** makes the dagger a Heavy-synergy weapon (Heavy's +0.9 → **1.6 per damaging hit** together) and leaves the roster split at **12 +DMG / 10 +SPIN**; **+0.7 SPIN** restores its v0.7 identity, makes it a Speedy-synergy weapon (+0.30 → **1.00/hit**, the cell that produced the measured ω 103.5 maximum) and moves the split to **11/11**.
*(2) The ruling, and the datum read honestly.* **+0.7 DMG stands.** The datum the deferral was waiting on: the dagger ranks **13th of 22** at a **53.8%** holder win rate — dead average, and the last weapon above the cliff (orb 53.9 · dagger 53.8 · then javelin 27.6). Dead average *under the DMG axis* says the axis is not what mis-tunes the dagger; its rank is better explained by reach (`len: 78`, the shortest melee blade in the roster) than by its growth family. And the revert would have paired it with the fighter that loses **61%** of rounds and with the family whose group holder win% is **29.3** against melee's **69.0** — so the data argues *against* +0.7 SPIN rather than merely failing to argue for +0.7 DMG. *(3) NO SIM CHANGE — and the correction that matters.* The dagger row already ships `trait: { spin: 0.0, dmg: 0.7 }`, byte-identical to the other eleven +DMG weapons (all twelve carry that exact pair). Ratifying the shipped value therefore moves nothing: **canonical md5 `e401e3e33c3133b03ec192f7e5fe0199` unchanged, 3,093 lines, no fingerprint movement, no re-baseline, no stamp bump.** This entry also corrects the framing the ruling was granted under, which described +0.7 DMG as a data-table edit that would move the fingerprints and need them re-baselined.
It would not, because it is the current value; only the **+0.7 SPIN** branch was a behaviour change. The deferral closes in the docs alone: the roster-table ⚠ is marked CLOSED with the ruling and the no-change fact, and the discharged "Next"/"Owed"/"synergy question" claims in the four entries that carried it are bracketed in place with the date, per the house pattern for a paid obligation. *(4) Reversibility, recorded so the alternative stays recoverable.* One number in one row, no plumbing. Had the owner picked SPIN — or picks it later — `dagger.trait` becomes `{ spin: 0.70, dmg: 0.0 }`, and that IS a sanctioned sim change: fingerprints re-baselined to a new `.qa/fp-<stamp>.json`, stamp bumped, roster split 11/11. *(5) What is still owed.* The other decision does need the owner's machine: the attribution re-runs (Part 2 then Part 1, commands in `scratch/measure-parts.md`), and after them the **band-vs-resolver** ruling for law 3. Then the skills pass itself, starting with the length-growth rule's shape — design, not code, since under M2 the hook machinery is not built until a special skill exists to hang on it.

### Retired from GAMES.md — the "Standing baseline:" annotation chain (2026-10-28)

FILE: combine.js

const fs = require("fs");
const path = require("path");

const outputFile = "project_dump.txt";
let finalText = "";

function traverseDir(dir) {
  const files = fs.readdirSync(dir);

  files.forEach((file) => {
    const filePath = path.join(dir, file);
    const stat = fs.statSync(filePath);

    // 1. Skip folders we don't care about, and the output file itself
    if (
      file === "node_modules" ||
      file === ".git" ||
      file === outputFile ||
      file === ".env"
    )
      return;

    if (stat.isDirectory()) {
      // If it's a folder, go inside it
      traverseDir(filePath);
    } else {
      // 2. Only grab text-based web files (ignores images, binaries, etc.)
      if (/\.(js|ts|jsx|tsx|html|css|json|md|txt)$/.test(file)) {
        const content = fs.readFileSync(filePath, "utf8");

        // 3. Add nice headers so the AI knows which file is which
        finalText += `\n\n========================================\n`;
        finalText += `FILE: ${filePath}\n`;
        finalText += `========================================\n\n`;
        finalText += content;
      }
    }
  });
}

try {
  console.log("Scanning your project...");
  traverseDir("./"); // Start scanning the current folder

  fs.writeFileSync(outputFile, finalText, "utf8");
  console.log(`✅ Success! All your code has been combined into ${outputFile}`);
  console.log("You can now upload this file to our chat.");
} catch (err) {
  console.error("Oops, something went wrong:", err);
}

FILE: CONTRACT.md
========================================

# ARENA ENGINE — Game Contract

The interface a game implements. The platform knows nothing about any specific game: **zero `gameId` conditionals in platform code, ever.** If you find yourself adding one, the contract is wrong — fix the contract.

---

## A game is a folder

```
games/<id>/
├─ index.ts      # default-exports the GameModule
├─ sim.ts        # pure simulation
├─ render.ts     # frame drawing
├─ config.ts     # Zod schema
└─ README.md     # what it is, what the knobs do
```

Discovery is convention-based: the registry imports every `games/*/index.ts` at boot, validates the export, and rejects malformed modules with a readable error surfaced in the UI. No registration file, no platform edits.

---

## The interface

```ts
export interface GameModule<C = unknown, S = unknown> {
  meta: {
    id: string;                 // kebab-case, unique, stable forever
    name: string;
    tagline: string;
    category: 'race' | 'elimination' | 'competition' | 'accumulation'
            | 'prediction' | 'spectacle' | 'other';
    tags: string[];
    targets: ExportTargetId[];  // 'vertical' | 'vertical-30' | 'horizontal'
    version: string;            // bump on any output-affecting change
  };

  /** Single source of truth for every knob. Drives the UI panel,
   *  CLI flags, validation and defaults. */
  configSchema: z.ZodType<C>;

  /** The platform asks the game how long it is — never the reverse. */
  getDuration(config: C): number;   // seconds

  /** Pure: no drawing, no I/O, no globals. */
  createGame(config: C, svc: SimServices): GameInstance<S>;

  /** Draw one frame. May not mutate sim state. */
  render(ctx: Surface, snap: S, t: number, svc: RenderServices): void;
}

export interface GameInstance<S> {
  step(dt: number): void;       // advance exactly one fixed tick (1/120)
  snapshot(): S;                // serializable state at the current tick
  events(): GameEvent[];        // events since the last call
  finished(): boolean;
  result(): ResultSummary;      // valid once finished()
}
```

Five required members, nothing optional. Every extra hook is a promise the platform keeps forever — add nothing until a real game needs it.

`getDuration` is a function because length usually depends on config. `createGame` returns a stepping instance, not a whole timeline, so memory stays bounded. `snapshot()` must be plain serializable data — it's stored at keyframes. `render` gets a snapshot rather than the instance, which makes the sim/render split physical: the renderer cannot advance the game.

---

## Injected services

A game touches **only** its own module and these.

### `SimServices` (in `createGame`)

| | |
|---|---|
| `rng` | `.next()` `.range(a,b)` `.int(a,b)` `.pick(arr)` `.weighted(entries)` `.shuffle(arr)` `.fork(label)` |
| `config` | Validated, frozen config object |
| `clock` | `{ tick, ticksPerSec, time }` — the only permitted time source |
| `emit(event)` | Record a discrete event. Use the core vocabulary where it applies; custom kinds are permitted and ignored by the platform. |
| `say(text, style, window)` | On-screen text as part of the game's graphics — a callout, caption bar, status line. **Not** a subtitle system; produces no caption file. |
| `sfx(name, at?, gain?)` | Queue an audio cue against a timeline time |

`rng.fork(label)` gives each subsystem its own deterministic stream, so adding a random call in one place doesn't shift every later outcome.

### `RenderServices` (in `render`)

| | |
|---|---|
| `gfx` | `bar` `chip` `badge` `meter` `countdown` `leaderboard` `bracket` `swoosh` `flash` `vignette` `grid` `body(player, opts)`, plus camera moves `zoom()` `pan()`. No `particles`, no `confetti`, no `shake` — the locked frame punctuates with flash and type only (house style). |
| `type` | `display()` `ui()` `mono()` at the house scale; `fit(text, maxWidth)` `wrap()` `measure()` |
| `palette` | Tokens, semantic colors, and per-match player color assignment |
| `layout` | Canvas dims, **`arena`** (the fixed play-area rectangle, identical in every game), `safe.titleBox` / `safe.scoreBox` / `safe.captionBox`, column and row grids |
| `anim` | `tween(from, to, t, ease)` `stagger(i, n, offset)` `spring()`, the house easing set |
| `beat(ms)` | The 3-beat helper: anticipation → strike → settle, synced to an event time |
| `theme` | This render's accent color and package settings |

### `Surface`

A ~40-method interface over `CanvasRenderingContext2D`. Games draw against `Surface`, never a concrete canvas — that's what lets the same render code run on Node's Skia and in a browser `OffscreenCanvas`.

---

## Players

A player is one participant in a match — always a single named thing, never a crowd. Matches are 1v1 or a four-way free-for-all, so at most four appear at once.

```ts
type Player = {
  id: string;              // stable forever, used by the sim
  name: string;            // what the audience reads
  color: string;             // permanent and unique — the same in every game
  mark?: Mark;             // glyph, flag, or image. Optional.
};
```

**Players live in data files, not in code.** A pool is a JSON file of players — `assets/pools/characters.json`, and others as needed. A game declares which pool it draws from, or supplies its own list. Adding player #41 is a one-line data change; the platform never learns their name.

**Color is permanent.** Speedy is green in every game, forever — that's what makes them recognisable, and it's worth more than any other visual consistency. `mark` is the detailed identity drawn on the body: a glyph for a character, a flag for a nation. Color is what the *system* uses (bar, chip, territory fill); the mark is what the *body* wears. They're separate because a flag can't fill a progress bar.

### Colors never collide

**No two players in a pool share a color.** It's a constraint on the data, checked at load — not something resolved at runtime. There is no priority order, no reassignment, no per-match logic. A player's color is simply theirs.

This is easy because the numbers are small. A match shows at most four players, so only four colors ever need to be separable *at the same time* — and they're backed by names, marks and scoreboard positions, so color is reinforcement rather than the sole identifier. The palette only needs to be at least as large as the pool.

The palette is **~24 colors**, differing in lightness as well as hue so they survive grayscale and red-green color vision deficiency (~8% of men). The practical ceiling on pool size is not color availability but memory: past roughly 24–30 named players, a cast stops being something an audience can hold in its head. Choose colors you can *name* — "green" and "red" are characters people discuss in comments; "chartreuse" and "olive" are not.

### What the platform provides

- `palette` exposes the player colors for this match.
- `gfx.body(player, opts)` draws a default body — a colored form carrying the mark and name — which a game may override where its subject demands.
- The scoreboard, leaderboard and result summary refer to players by `id`.

Nothing else. The platform has no concept of a cast, a character, or a nation.

---

## Skills — how players differ

A player's identity (name, color, mark) never changes. What makes them behave differently is their **skill**, and a skill is a set of **hooks** into one game's mechanics.

The split is strict:

- **Player data holds no behaviour.** Just `id`, `name`, `color`, optional `mark`.
- **Behaviour lives only in hooks**, defined inside each game.
- **Identity is global; skill is local.** The same player is reinterpreted per game — the identity stays recognisable, the mechanical effect does not have to be identical.

**One skill per player per game.** A player has exactly one skill in each game they appear in, and that skill may be expressed through one hook or several. Not zero, not two.

### Rules for a hook

1. It **reads** the player and a small context, and **returns a modified value**. It never mutates state.
2. It is **optional**. Where a game calls a hook a player doesn't implement, the base value passes through unchanged — so adding a hook never means editing every player that doesn't use it.

   Optionality is a **safety net, not a design choice**. Because of it, a player can appear in a game *before* their skill is authored — they simply run on base values and the game still works. Adding player #12 therefore doesn't block on writing twelve skills; they can appear immediately and get theirs later.
3. It **never depends on another player's hook.**
4. It **modifies an existing mechanic**; it never introduces a new one.
5. It may consume the game's seeded RNG, but must **never create or seed one.**
6. Anything time-dependent — a cycle, a timer, a cooldown — is advanced by the game's own per-tick logic. The hook only reads whatever has already been decided.

A game may bind its hooks tighter than these six rules. SPINCLASH's standing ruling (owner, 2026-10-31, recorded in its `GAMES.md`): a player **skill** and an equipment **trait** may stack **only by addition on a shared axis** — neither may reach into the other's mechanic, and no unique player×equipment combinations may exist.

### Hook names belong to the game

Each game defines its own hook interface. Names are local to it, never shared between games, and **the platform never learns any of them.** It supplies only the generic shape of a hook — a context in, a value out — and nothing more.

That's what keeps rule 6 true: adding a game never edits the platform, and adding a player never edits a game they don't appear in.

A consequence worth stating, because it settles a question we'd deferred: **there is no platform-level skill system, no archetype taxonomy, and no ability registry.** The platform provides the shape; games provide the content.

An earlier design had six archetypes as buckets implying behaviour. They were dropped: **a well-chosen name does the same job and is visible to the audience.** "Heavy" tells a viewer what to expect; `front-runner` never would. See SPEC.md for the naming rules.

---

## Event vocabulary

`emit()` takes a `kind`. Seven kinds are **core** — the platform reacts to these with shared visuals and audio, so every game punctuates moments the same way:

| Kind | Platform reaction |
|---|---|
| `win` | Outro, result card |
| `eliminated` | Desaturate the player, strike it from the scoreboard, impact sound |
| `lead` | Position swoosh, scoreboard reorder |
| `nearMiss` | Brief tension beat |
| `impact` | Shake + impact sound |
| `milestone` | Callout |
| `phaseChange` | Transition wipe |

**Games use only the kinds that apply.** Most will use two or three, and that's expected — nothing requires a game to emit all seven.

Games may also emit **custom kinds** for their own rendering. The platform ignores any kind it doesn't recognise, and never branches on `gameId` to work one out.

---

## Matchup config

Every game is *X versus Y*, so every game needs to know which players from the pool are competing. One standard config helper does this:

```ts
const config = z.object({
  matchup: MatchupSchema,   // { mode: 'headToHead' | 'freeForAll' | 'random', ids?: string[] }
  // ...the game's own options
});
```

The platform resolves `matchup` into a list of player ids and hands them to the game. The studio renders `MatchupSchema` as the same control in every game — a grid of the available players you tick, plus a "random" option — so the picker looks and behaves identically everywhere and no game writes matchup UI. Display names come from the game.

---

## A game may **not**

Enforced by ESLint and CI:

- Import `node:*`, `fs`, `path`, `child_process`, or anything from `packages/render` / `packages/server`
- Reference `window`, `document`, `process`, or mutate `globalThis`
- Call `Math.random`, `Date.now`, `performance.now`, `new Date()` without an argument
- Perform I/O, network calls, or dynamic `import()`
- Mutate state inside `render`
- Hardcode a resolution, framerate, safe zone, font or color — those come from services
- Define its own easing curves
- Draw action outside `layout.arena`, or restyle the platform-injected frame overlay
- Exceed its declared duration, or emit events after `finished()`

---

## Timeline

Produced by the platform from a completed simulation. Games never construct it.

```ts
type Timeline<S> = {
  meta: { gameId: string; gameVersion: string; seed: number; config: C;
          durationSec: number; ticksPerSec: number };
  keyframes: { tick: number; snap: S }[];   // every 0.5s → enables re-entry
  events: GameEvent[];
  audio: AudioCue[];                        // { at, sound, gain }
  result: ResultSummary;
};

type GameEvent = {
  tick: number;
  kind: string;                             // game-defined, e.g. 'overtake'
  subjectId: string;
  otherId?: string;
  data?: Record<string, string | number>;
  label?: string;                           // human-readable, may be shown on screen
};

type ResultSummary = {
  standings: { id: string; place: number; value?: number }[];   // required
  winnerId: string;                                             // required
  margin?: number;                          // game-defined units
  leadChanges?: number;
  biggestComeback?: { id: string; from: number; to: number };
  records?: string[];                       // e.g. "fastest final"
  highlights?: { tick: number; label: string }[];
};
```

Keyframes every 0.5s, not every tick — 7,200 full snapshots for a 60s match would be hundreds of megabytes. Sparse keyframes let the renderer re-enter cheaply, which is what makes a second aspect ratio a re-encode rather than a fresh simulation.

`ResultSummary` feeds exactly three things: the outcome panel, the per-render stats breakdown, and `render.json` (which is where per-game aggregate stats come from). The platform displays these facts and does not interpret them. **There is no drama score** — an earlier weighted composite was removed; invented weights presented as measurement, when the underlying facts are more useful.

---

## Fixed timestep

- Simulation: **120 Hz**, `dt = 1/120`, never variable.
- Output: 30 or 60 fps per target; the renderer interpolates between ticks.
- The platform drives the loop. `step()` must be safe to call exactly `duration × 120` times, and `finished()` must be true at or before that point.

---

## Contract validation suite

One Vitest file loops over every registered game and runs these eight. A game isn't done until all pass.

1. **Purity lint** — no forbidden imports or globals.
2. **Schema check** — config parses, defaults valid, every field has UI metadata.
3. **Determinism** — simulate twice with one seed → identical timeline hash.
4. **Duration** — sim finishes within 2% of `getDuration()`.
5. **Snapshot serializability** — `structuredClone` round-trip.
6. **Safe zones and arena** — render 20 sampled frames; no meaningful ink outside the safe boxes, and no action outside `layout.arena`.
7. **Output completeness** — a 5-second render produces a valid MP4 at every declared target plus `render.json`, and nothing else.
8. **Golden frame** — one committed reference PNG hash per game per version.

---

## The two probes

The contract must be validated by two mechanically unrelated games before any real game is built. Both stay in the repo as compliance fixtures; neither is content.

- **`_probe` A** — the simplest thing that exercises the whole pipe: N players advancing to a finish line. Continuous motion.
- **`_probe` B** — deliberately the opposite: discrete rounds, phases, elimination, a bracket graphic, no continuous motion.

If B fits without contract changes, the contract is real. If it needs a special case, fix the contract then — before ten games depend on it.

---

## Reserved for later

Only one speculative extension is worth leaving room for, because it affects the timeline format:

- **`interactive` mode** — an optional flag plus an `input` event stream. A local player plays the game; the input is recorded as a deterministic log and replayed through the same pipeline into a video. Cheap to allow for now, expensive to retrofit.

Also possible later with no contract change: in-browser sim preview (needs only a `Surface` shim over `OffscreenCanvas`), and thumbnails (just "encode one chosen frame").

The **hook machinery is still not built**, per the cast ruling that it waits for the first genuinely contextual special skill; a weapon-row *rate* is data under M2 and needs no hook. ## Game #1 — SPINCLASH

Engine id `spinclash` — kebab-case, frozen at naming (CONTRACT). Named 2026-10-15 under SPEC.md "Game naming rules". Tagline: *"Blades clash. Bots snowball."*

A physics auto-battler: two bots drop into a circular arena (inscribed in the platform's fixed square bounds) under heavy gravity, each swinging an orbiting weapon. Genre reference: earclacks (cosmicoptima) — **inspiration only**; the rules, code and visuals here are original (the reference file was purged at owner word 2026-10-22 — the lessons remain; note the v1.0 roster leans on familiar archetypes — see open question on prior-art wording).

- **Battle = best of 3 rounds**, first to 2 round wins. Video target: 1min+ of battle (platform intro/outro add to it).
- **Per-round dice roll.** Before every round, the seeded roll assigns each fighter a weapon from the roster; **duplicates allowed** (mirror duels are deliberate comedy). Fixed draw order (2 weapon draws + 1 opening-spin-direction draw + 2 launch draws — one angle per fighter — per round), so `(seed)` fully determines a battle. The direction draw opens every round **counter-rotating** — mechanism, owner decision and rationale in Core contact law rule 6.
- **Stats reset every round** — each round is a fresh snowball; escalation is carried by the series situation (ROUND 3 = DECIDER banner, scorebug always visible), not by stat carry-over.
- **Rounds end on K.O. only** — no timer, by owner decision; the harness watches stalls and non-termination and the decision is revisited only if they prove real (they currently do — open question 1).
- **Damage and parry.** Weapon touching the opponent's **body** is a damaging hit + knockback — **unless the weapon fires a projectile** (owner decision 2026-10-19: "ranged weapons (shooting projectiles), their weapons do not damage, only their projetiles"): a projectile weapon's spine shoves but never cuts; its shot is its only damage. **[AMENDED 2026-11-02, `allcut-r62` — THE PROJECTILE RULE IS RETIRED at the owner's word (*"all weapons from now on deals damage if they touch the opponets body… launchers are boring to watch in the beginning as they have a hard time hitting the opponents and gaining growth"*): EVERY weapon cuts on body touch — the ten launchers AND the shield (its tangential no-damage clause was the rule's last remnant); the spine chip rides the WDEF base damage 1 and feeds grow() like any melee hit, so every launcher-side trait trigger wakes. The 2026-10-19 decision above is history.]** Weapon touching **weapon** is a **parry**: no damage, both spins recoil (flip), bodies shoved apart along the true contact normal. Every *fresh* exact touch is one parry — a hysteresis latch (the 4px `parryPad`) makes a sustained press count once, so no timer gates the physics or the events; full trigger semantics in law 2. The **Core contact law** below is the normative text. Whether a parry should also *reward* the parrier is an open question.
- **Growth, uncapped (owner decision).** Every damaging hit grows the attacker: the fighter's skill **and** the weapon's trait both apply. Fights are meant to get ridiculous — spinning out of control is the show. The only ceilings are sim stability (omegaCap 140 rad/s; adaptive substeps against tunneling), not gameplay. **Measured 2026-10-28 (pre-skills): that ceiling is 36.5 damaging hits away, and it clamps SILENTLY.** The fastest spin observed across 30 naturals is **103.5 rad/s** = base 3.5 + exactly 100 hits × 1.0/hit (weapon trait 0.70 + Speedy 0.30), so `omegaCap` 140 bites at 136.5 hits on that axis — no readout, no event, the fighter simply stops getting faster. Owner asked what this is; explained 2026-10-28, and of the four options offered the owner picked **measure the real limit first** — done the same day, read-only: **the clamp is DORMANT (removing it changes nothing at all) and the real ceiling is structural, hp ÷ damage = 100 hits → max spin 103.5.** The sim itself is stable to ω ≈ 258 at the worst of 484 pairs. Full numbers in the spin-ceiling measurement entry. Under the **Uniform base stats** decision (below), growth is the *only* source of spin/damage divergence — weapons start equal and snowball apart. On projectile weapons the spin axis *is* the fire rate, so `+SPD / Hit` means "shoots faster".
- **Fighters (placeholder roster).** **Speedy** — weapon spins faster per damaging hit (+0.30 SPD). **Heavy** — weapon hits harder per damaging hit (+0.9 DMG). These are their one-skill-per-game hooks (CONTRACT.md §Skills).
- **Hidden forcing.** The viewer always sees the roll as random; `newGame(seed, {weapons})` forces a combo silently (the future studio config exposes this as the curator knob; `render.json` will record the truth).
- **1v1 only** (owner decision). A 3-man "pure chaos" brawl is a wanted future mode — it will need SPEC's match-shape sentence widened by one line when it arrives.

**Classes as built (v1.2 + batch-4):** *melee* = radial hold, damaging spine, no shot (hammer, dagger, axe, sword, spear, mace, scythe, katana — and the **orb**, the sentinel shape: radial-hold melee with NO SHAFT, the floating business end alone at the tip of an invisible spine; its orbit is the native tip orbit — one rev per spin, reversed by every parry recoil, quickened by growth; its `len` is the orbit radius to the orb CENTRE, the first row whose art extends past its len — every consumer reads the polys, not len (REACH/SPAN from vertices, no tip launch, no headLead pivot, pop centre = bbox centre = the orb centre), audited at merge). *launchers* = fire a shot, spine never damages (the projectile rule): radial-hold **staff, wand** (tip launch) and tangential-hold **bow, crossbow, knives, tome, scroll** (middle, radially out of the belly) plus **boomerang, shuriken, javelin** (middle, tangentially in the spin direction). *shield* = tangential, no shot, no damage — the odd one out, awaiting design. *chain* = flail (2026-10-21, first of its class) + nunchaku (batch-4 2026-10-22, the first to ride the N-segment pre-wire: 2 segments, 1 free particle): radial hold, damaging spine like melee, but the spine is **segmented** — the base segment rigid, links and head hinged at joints and integrated as free particles under `flailJoint`/`flailDrag` (`flailStep`), so the end lags and whips behind the haft (flail: two ring links + spiked ball at J0/J1/J2; nunchaku: ring link + bar + stick at J0); their covering circles are baked **per segment** (flail 49 circles in 12/14/15/8 bake batches, tied 9/13/14/13; nunchaku 27 in 8+19, tied 8/19 — the runtime tie is geometric, centre-in-outer-ink, innermost first) and each rides its own segment's pose (`bladeCircles(…, f.fl)`), the only weapons whose hitboxes articulate. Hold is placement + launch point; **damage capability is decided by the projectile rule, not the hold** (owner 2026-10-19 — this replaced the v0.7.x "ranged = tangential = no spine damage" class rule, under which staff/wand wrongly damaged with their spines; fixed in v1.2).

- **Renderer facts.** Bots are ink-bordered colored discs with **only the black HP number inside**; a **bright white hit flash** marks whichever bot got hit — the frame's only hit punctuation. Weapons draw from their own collision data (verbatim path polygons + covering circles): **every weapon above every body**, grip tips tucked invisible under the own disc (the tuck rule; rim-held and handle-less weapons carry `tuck: false`). **Edge-leading mirror (owner decision 2026-10-22):** directionally asymmetric weapons mirror art AND hitbox together on spin sign (`leadFlip`, one source in the placement layer) on their declared axis — `lead: ±1` for the lateral cutting side (katana −1, scythe −1: the chisel EDGE, the hook BEAK; owner playtest: a mouth-forward hook "is spinning the wrong way from the beginning"), `headLead: ±1` for the along-chord head END (javelin +1, owner: "i think the javelin should also flip around like scythe and katana" — a d-mirror pivoting about the centred rim grip, tangential-only by boot guard) — so the business contour always faces the direction of motion; `view[i].flip` is the DISPLAYED factor — continuous only during a transition; the parry re-presentation is **animated** at owner word ("i thought something else, like a fast transition not an instant snap"):
the blade eases old → edge-on → mirrored as cos(π·p) over `CFG.flipMs` (180ms — raised from 90 at owner playtest "its still too snappy"; a mid-sweep re-parry lands the first flip and starts a second continuous one, and a hitstop overlapping the sweep freezes it with the frame), reading as a spin about its own spine — art-only, fight-phase-only (every phase entry snaps; the bell's roll is not a parry), frozen with the frame under a hitstop. The sim truth stays binary everywhere it matters: `view[i].fpSim` feeds the hitbox debug overlay (never the squash), the kill still latches the full ±1 contact pose (a damage event inside the window freezes into honest geometry; non-kill freezes are true pauses since pause-r20), and the sim/laws/audits never see the transition (fingerprints byte-identical). The disclosed art≠hitbox window (~5 drawn frames per flagged parry) is the owner-accepted trade — containment and proofs in Measured facts. The two invisible glint iterations were removed with it (`.qa/glintproof.mjs` retired; `.qa/flipproof.mjs` is the standing proof); the kill still latches the flip from the event's stored signed spin; the VS poster draws the canonical orientation (`drawFitWeapon` takes no flip).
No contact ghosts, no spin trails, no particles, no screen shake, no glow, **no game name on screen** — proof-of-contact lives entirely in the harness (owner decisions, step1c/step1d, archive); the growth tell lives only in the legend's SPD number. **Sigil (owner decision 2026-10-23):** every weapon carries exactly ONE diegetic element in the wielding fighter's cast color — shapes tagged `KC` are swapped to `COLS[f.idx]` in `drawWeapon`/`drawWeaponChain` (gold fallback for carrier-less renders; `KC` is an invalid CSS color, so an unswapped sigil fails visibly, never silently). The doctrine is prescriptive in **Weapon art** (6), the mark map lives in `roster-redesign-brief.md`; the mechanism is live at `build marks-r10`, inert until the redesign delivery tags shapes. Shots draw per kind, and **every kind inks its own hitbox disc** — a faint full-disc halo at exactly radius r under the art (owner directive 2026-10-19, visible-contact-first; the orb's original 28% halo is the shared language, `HALO` alphas are dials): disc-shaped shots: the drawn disc *is* the hitbox; arrows/bolts: the hitbox circle sits at the head, shaft and fletching trail *behind* it (the head tip spikes slightly past it forward — safe direction, ink leads the hit).
When any shot was thrown, the winner overlay's stats line grows a `shots X thrown / Y landed / Z swatted` tail. Preview tooling (chips: Pause / Slow motion / Fast forward / Restart / New seed / Hitboxes; seed row) never renders into a video; playback is a real-time catch-up loop at 1×, Slow motion ≈¼× and Fast-forward ≈4× (owner request 2026-10-19; the two are mutually exclusive — engaging one releases the other). **Hitstop (owner decision 2026-10-19 — trigger policy 1: "implement it, and do 1 trigger policy"):** every damage hit freezes sim time briefly — `CFG.hitStopMs` 60 (≈7 ticks); the killing blow gets `CFG.koStopMs` 400 (≈48 ticks) on the impact pose, *then* the K.O. beat runs its `koTicks` — with no card type: the K.O. announcement was removed at owner word 2026-10-21 ("i dont want it to be announced"); the round's end reads as the freeze, the faded death-mark disc and the scorebug tick, then the next reveal. The gate lives in the frame loop (`stopTicks` counts the accumulator down in sim ticks — set from the `hit` events in `consumeEvents`), so the sim sequence and every fingerprint are untouched by construction.
Parry/wall/bounce never stop time (no damage); same-tick stops max-merge, never stack; the freeze counts on the playback clock — fast-forward shortens it in wall time, slow-mo stretches it (constant sim-time pause); wall-clock FX (flash decay, banner) freeze with it so the impact frame holds, and `viewA` keeps its leftover fraction — no pose snap. Leftover freezes drain at `G.over` so the winner overlay decays normally. **The freeze is a TRUE pause of the on-screen frame (owner 2026-10-27, `pause-r20`):** nothing latches for non-kill hits — every freeze frame repeats the onset frame pixel-for-pixel, so a graze's freeze holds exactly what the viewer was already seeing and can introduce no gap. The 2026-10-21 hit still (contact-pose override for non-kill freezes) is SUPERSEDED by that word: its onset/release boundary micro-steps proved to be the only motion inside the window. The KILL still (2026-10-19) keeps latching the killing contact for the 400 ms K.O. hold, including a landing shot frozen at its impact point (spliced on death, so the impact was never a drawn pose). Renderer-only; born from the seed-12024 graze diagnosis in **Measured facts**. **Weapons visible at all times (owner 2026-10-21, seed 80117; final form: the single-canvas overflow band).** The canvas IS the sim square plus a 150-unit band, absolutely centred over its cssPx layout box (the wrap keeps the flow height; the band overhangs the chrome rows, pointer-transparent), at the approved disc scale U — tips past the square (worst ~146 units: long radial tip, body at the rim) draw whole into the band instead of cutting at the old canvas edge, which at the four axis directions coincides with the rim's outer edge and read as the weapon dipping UNDER the rim.

Disc pixel size, page flow and chrome untouched; renderer-only, fingerprints byte-identical. Disclosed: extreme top/bottom tips draw over the scorebug/legend rows (the out-of-bounds spectacle). The engine-era square-plus-margins frame and contract check 6's ink-in-margin question join open question 9, with the band as the preview precedent. The band's first pass positioned `#ov` against `#wrap` instead of against the centred main canvas, drawing the ring adrift by the canvas's centring offset (owner screenshot seed 46322: a shaft gap with an orphan tip at the page edge); `resize` now offsets the band by that centring offset — fixed same day, renderer-only, fingerprints byte-identical, suite green. **Render interpolation (v0.8.2, owner-approved; reference implementation: the owner's `sumo_war (2).html`, credited):** every actor draws at a pose blended between the last two tick poses — fighter positions and weapon angles (shortest-arc), shot positions — with alpha = the catch-up loop's leftover tick fraction, so motion stays even on displays whose refresh is not an integer multiple of the 120 Hz tick.
Whenever the sim is not stepping (paused, reveal, K.O. card, over) alpha = 1: those frames render the exact latest tick pose and the actors stand still (the reveal poster animates on its own phaseT clock over frozen actors). **The dice reveal — the VS poster (owner-designed 2026-10-19, copied verbatim at his word, then polished the same day on his playtest notes — smaller weapon fit, weapon name matched to the bot-name recipe, speed-line FX contained, unused `VS` fields stripped; replaces the floating-card default).** For its `revealTicks: 285` (~2.4s — extended from 165/~1.4s at owner word 2026-10-19, +1s: the extra second splits between a slower roll cadence (`land` 0.40/0.58 → 0.32/0.46 → 0.39/0.39 across the +1s and simultaneous-landing tunes — same shuffle counts over a longer window, so the steps themselves stretch) and a ~1.45s end hold, the same read-time reasoning as the label-block spread) a split-screen versus poster covers the arena disc: cream plates (`PLATE` = `TH.floor`), each tinted 0.55 with its cast color under a diagonal-stripe pattern, wipe in from the sides over the first ~26 ticks behind a giant VS (dead-centre ink divider, ROUND n above at y 128).
