### Core contact law (owner decision, 2026-10-16)

The fundamental-mechanics contract, set **before** the weapon redesign: every weapon, skill and hit rule — now and future — must satisfy these six. **Audit status (2026-10-19, v1.2):** all six were green at every full baseline from v0.8.1 through v0.8.3 (numbers in the archive), and are **re-proven green on the current 13-weapon v1.2 build** by the two sanctioned runs of 2026-10-19 — part 0 (42 battles, 6.4M substep poses) and the `--solidity` overlap gauntlet (76 battles, 1.1M rendered fight-ticks): zero violations of all six laws and all seven shot laws. The forced matrix — now **484 cells** at the 22-weapon roster — remains the one unrun scope (deferred with the balance pass). `measure.mjs` re-verifies all six against every event and every substep pose on every run ("what you see is what hits" — this is the principle's mechanics half). The shot laws extend these six — normative text and the seven-point audit live in **Projectile weapons**.

1. **Damage requires touch.** A bot takes damage only when the opponent's weapon overlaps its body disc — and the drawn disc *is* the collision circle (radius 64). Nothing else writes HP: walls, body-vs-body checks and spin growth never damage. *Status: law since v0.5, proven at every full baseline (0 phantom hits ever)* — every hit event stores its contact pose and the audit recomputes the touch from it. The projectile rule narrows the converse: a projectile weapon's spine touching the body deals **no** damage (shot only) — damage still requires touch; touch no longer guarantees damage from such a spine (law 7s audits it).
2. **Parry requires weapon-on-weapon collision.** Only the blade-vs-blade gap can trigger a parry; body proximity is irrelevant. The trigger is exact touch (surface gap ≤ 0); the 4px `parryPad` is the hysteresis re-arm margin and substep-sizing window, not a gameplay window. *Status: enforced and proven at every full baseline* — 0 parries ever fired without touch; every entry gap bites in. The one sanctioned extension: a blade touching a **shot** is a *swat*, not a parry (Projectile weapons) — audited to exact touch the same way (0 swats without touch ever). **Second sanctioned extension (owner option 1, 2026-10-21): the flutter gate.** After a parry fires, the latch cannot re-arm for `parryGate` 16 ticks even if the blades clear the pad; contacts inside the gate stay fully solid (resolver + approach-velocity kill) but fire nothing — no flip, no shove, no event. Born from the owner's seed-14052 playtest: a 4-clang vibrato burst (parries at +12/+4/+10 ticks, bottom cradle, wall-assisted) that "looks ugly for the viewer". Re-parry gaps are bimodal (flutter cluster ≤16 ticks vs legit p10 81), so 16 cuts the flutter and nothing else: post-gate scan over 20 naturals — gaps ≤16: 51 → **0**, bursts 36 → 5 (1.8 → 0.3 per battle, residuals being clean double-taps at ≥17 ticks). The trigger sentence therefore reads: every fresh exact touch **at least 16 ticks after the previous parry** is one parry; the latch — not a timer — still prevents re-fires during a sustained press, and the timer gates only the re-arm, never the solidity.
3. **Weapons are solids to each other.** No tunneling, no interpenetration — not on a rendered frame, not between frames. A per-substep resolver de-overlaps along the true contact normal (the bodies are pushed apart, then re-honoured against body-vs-body and the arena; weapons ride rigidly on bodies), kills the approaching velocity, and recoils the spins on fresh contact. Detection is guaranteed: substeps are sized so relative travel per substep ≤ half the narrowest contact window, so any real crossing spans at least two tests. Nothing gates it — the old cooldown skip was the bug. *Status: enforced and proven at every full baseline, and re-proven on v1.2 (part 0 + the solidity gauntlet)* — one representation class since v0.9 (every weapon is a path silhouette): the disclosed band was stated as ≤6px worst / ≤2% of fight-ticks (the infeasible-pin transient, attributable) — **bound FALSIFIED and mechanism CORRECTED 2026-10-28** by `--band-dump` geometry at both worst cases: measured **20.754px** (flail+scythe s104 t12272) and **14.673px** (crossbow+katana s102 t4588), both flagged visible through the 3px ink, with bodies at **exactly 2R (zero overlap)** and 45/169px of wall clearance and a 9-contact push at 90% alignment — so it is **not** a body pin and not chain-specific (the crossbow+katana pair is rigid). The real mechanism: translation-only projection on crossed ~205px-reach blades has a **fixed point ≈10px deep** that more passes do not improve, and the loop's only rotational DOF is the nudge, capped `nudgePx/REACH` (0.0588 rad) and gated one per tick per fighter, while the contact torque it accumulates (sim :1697-98) is reduced to `Math.sign` (:1713-14). The resolver rework is **deferred until after length growth**, which changes every reach and therefore every fixed point — see the Measured-facts entry of that date, judged since 2026-10-28 on the BAND class alone — the named edge-leading MIRROR class (a parry flipping a flagged weapon in the tick's last substep: sim truth, proven per occurrence, measured never drawn) is disclosed separately and does not widen the band; the dormant parts-class counters and report lines were trimmed from the harness 2026-10-19. Substep pre-resolution overlap is resolved in-substep and never rendered. Acceptance & calibration history: archive (law 3's entry) — mutation-tested with the resolver disabled at 22.83px worst, so the check has teeth.
4. **One damage per touch.** The first touch deals damage once; while the weapon stays in contact, no further damage; it becomes eligible again only after the blade clears the body by the re-arm margin (12px). Blades pass through bodies — solid to each other only (rule 3) — and that pass-through is what makes "still touching" and "leaves the body" well-defined. *Status: law since v0.5, proven at every full baseline* — the exact flag replica over every substep pose has never mismatched; re-arms only on real separation. **The projectile-rule exception (owner 2026-10-19):** a projectile weapon's spine touching the body still latches and shoves (same re-arm + knock — solidity survives), but deals no damage and emits no hit event, so the replica pairs only damaging edges — the replica mirrors the sim's exact gate (`shot || tangential`; the tangential half now covers only the shield). Law 7s proves no projectile weapon ever emits a melee hit. For shots the law is structural: a shot is consumed by the body it hits, so it can never double-damage — the audit instead proves *accounting* (every shot has exactly one proven departure; see Projectile weapons). **The sanctioned re-arm-side extension — DEEP-DISENGAGE GATE (owner option 1, 2026-10-23: \"do 1\"):** after a blade latch fires, re-arm needs not only the 12px `reArmPad` clearance but ALSO either a genuine disengagement (peak clearance since the latch ≥ `reArmDeep` 85px) or `reArmWait` 90 ticks out. Contacts inside the gate stay fully solid (the resolver is untouched — the gate events-only, the same division of labour as law 2's flutter gate): the latch holds, no fresh hit or knock fires, and a rocked blade pokes at ≥0.75s cadence instead of machine-gunning. Born from the owner's seed-24267 playtest — Heavy's javelin left and re-entered Speedy's body 3× in 95 ticks (44/51-tick intervals, five legal parries interleaved): \"the weapon going back and forth damaging speedy multiple times as the weapon leaves and reenters speedys body, this looks very ugly\". The gate rides the latch, so knock-only contacts (projectile spines, the shield) are gated identically; a buried blade can never re-arm (the pad clause fails), so \"one touch, one damage\" stays structural. The trigger sentence therefore reads: every fresh exact touch **after the blade cleared the body AND either disengaged to ≥85px peak clearance or stayed out ≥90 ticks** is one hit. measure.mjs's law-4 replica mirrors the gate exactly, the substep order included (peak updates before the check). Calibration history and the population proofs live in **Measured facts**.
5. **Parry recoils both weapons.** On a parry, both spin directions flip. With rule 6 this keeps the pair counter-rotating for the whole round: growth preserves sign, and zero-spin cannot occur (ω starts at ±weapon ω and only grows in magnitude). Future weapon traits may carry explicit exceptions to the recoil (owner's caveat) — any exception must be a named, documented weapon trait, readable where the weapon is taught (reveal poster / legend). **The standing exception: the swat** (a blade touching a shot destroys the shot and flips nothing) — named, documented, and taught on the reveal poster's trait lines (`blades swat arrows` etc.) and legend (`+SPD / Hit · arrow / rev`); on screen the swat reads as the shot popping out of existence (its contact ghost retired with all ghosts at step1d). *Status: enforced and proven at every full baseline since v0.7.2* — the audit tracks signed spins across every substep: every parry flipped both weapons, **0 unexplained sign changes anywhere** (swats included — the sign law is what proves they flip nothing), 0 zero-spins, so counter-rotation holds from bell to K.O.
6. **Counter-rotation from the bell.** Every round starts with the two weapons spinning in opposite directions (one clockwise, one counter-clockwise): a single seeded roll decides fighter 0, fighter 1 always gets the opposite. **Rolled, not fixed per cast** (owner decision, 2026-10-16) — a per-cast table would have to be kept even by hand and breaks the moment mirror duels or a large roster arrive. Counter-rotating blades mesh like gears at the contact point, so the double recoil reads as a clean clang, and the two silhouettes stay distinguishable mid-fight. *Status: enforced and proven at every full baseline since v0.7.2* — 0 same-direction openings ever, all openings at exact base-ω magnitudes (a uniform 3.5 across the roster). Before the law: 28/48 rounds opened same-direction.

Owner's words (2026-10-16): "weapons can never tunnel through each other or overlap ever … they should treat each other as solids" · "damage only happens once when a weapon first touches the opponent, as long as the weapon still touches, no additional damage is done, first when the weapon leaves the body, it is eligible to do damage again" · "when weapons collide in a parry, i want the weapons to rotate the opposite direction (there might be exceptions due to special weapon skills)" · "the bots should rotate their weapons in opposite direction of their opponents when game starts (so one rotating clockwise and the other counterclockwise)" · on the opening direction: "i think it should be rolled, imagine in the future a roster of 50 bots, it annoying to keep track of to keep it even" (2026-10-16).

Recorded caveat (so it is never "fixed" as a bug later): in an extreme pin — a body crushed against the wall by the other's blade — the resolver may not fully separate within a single substep; it iterates and pushes out over the next few. The audit's acceptance line for rendered-tick interpenetration: the disclosed ≤6px / ≤2%-of-fight-ticks pin band, any residual transient and attributable. **Second disclosed class, the edge-leading MIRROR frame (2026-10-28):** a parry flips both spins at the END of `bladeVsBlade`, and `leadFlip` mirrors a flagged weapon's covering instantly while the bodies stay put — so a parry landing in the tick's LAST substep hands the rendered frame a mirrored interpenetration no resolver pass ever saw. It is sim truth and the audits are specified to read truth (`CFG.flipMs`, canonical :129: the art sweeps old→edge-on→mirrored over 180ms "while the sim's hitbox is already at its new (true) pose … the sim/laws/audits never see it"), and it is never drawn: `.qa/chainlaw.mjs` Part F replicates the sweep and measures a worst DRAWN gap of −0.149px, sub-ink. Membership is proven per occurrence (a parry at the previous tick's last substep + a flagged weapon + the same body pose clearing the ink under the pre-flip mirror); anything unexplained stays in the band and still fails it. Full attribution in Measured facts (the `chainlaw` entry). **Whip amendment history, compressed (2026-10-21):** a drained-rotation "whip" escape was built and REVERTED the same day (the drain re-buried blades at the resolver's push-out rate and glued pinned pairs — owner: "now they are both stuck together … never separating"; the band metric at the time measured overlap DEPTH but not episode DURATION, where the glue lived). The adopted cure (owner go): the escape nudge stays instant but is capped at `nudgePx` 12px-at-the-head and gated to one add per tick per fighter (each escape spreads over ~3–12 ticks at ≤6px-head per drawn frame), paired with `parryPush` 525 → 700 so grapples end before wedges form. Measured at birth: visible overlaps 0, worst depth 0.81px, max run 27 ticks, glued battles 0/20; f.spin untouched, so law 5's sign audit stays clean by construction. Law 3's acceptance therefore reports two classes (measure.mjs since 2026-10-21): **visible** overlaps (>2.5px, through the 3px ink outline) keep the old line (<6px worst, ≤2% of fight-ticks); **sub-ink** overlaps (≤2.5px — on screen the inks cross, which is the contact itself) are a disclosed transient class. Unadopted candidates on record: renderer-side angle chase (a disclosed drawn-lag exception to drawn-equals-hitbox), and a resolver that stalls less (engineering-heavy). Full numbers in **Measured facts** (whip and separation entries).

**Chaos ceiling + wall bleed (2026-10-21, owner option 1 from a measured menu — owner wish: "i feel like i want to see more but not exaggerating scenarios where bots touch the upper rim … too much of it is boring"; sim-data change, fingerprints re-baselined).** A cap-1600 experiment earlier the same day was playtest-rejected ("its going a bit too fast for the eye to understand now": 40 top touches/battle, pace p50 1053, 45% of ticks above the old cap) and reverted byte-identically; the revert scan corrected the design premise — top-rim touches were never impossible at cap 1100 (a full-cap upward launch from mid-arena rises 432px to y≈68): the approved baseline yields **0.95/battle**, the owner's "very rarely" as literal truth. ### Uniform base stats (owner decision, 2026-10-16 — BUILT in v0.7)

Owner: "i think all weapons should have the same default spin speed and damage. The spin speed/damage only increases from on hit." Every weapon on the roster shares one base spin and one base damage; the only thing that moves either number is on-hit growth (fighter skill + weapon trait — both fire exclusively on damaging hits, so nothing else in the sim needs rewiring). Stats reset every round, so each round opens with both fighters at identical numbers spinning in opposite directions; divergence is purely earned, inside the round.

- **The uniform base (assistant's numbers, owner delegated the pick):** ω **3.5** rad/s, damage **1** — damage was 5 from v0.7 through `pause-r20`; the balance pass opened 2026-10-28 with the owner's ruling "dmg base for all is 1, and hp 100 stays the same" (`dmg1-r21`), explicitly a TEST of long uncapped-escalation games ("the game becomes more and more ridiculous with no cap to scaling, and then it end in pure chaos … this is just a thought we can always change it"). hp 100, ω 3.5 and every growth increment (0.7 / 0.9 / 1.6) were deliberately left untouched, so the escalation curve steepened without any other number moving. Measured consequences — rounds 1.16× longer, launcher mirrors no longer terminating, maxSpin 23.5 → 103.5 — are in the `dmg1-r21` entry in **Measured facts**; the round-ending rule (open questions 1 and 5) is now the blocking decision (**superseded later the same day, 2026-10-28: the owner ruled the non-termination deliberate until skills land — see open question 1 — so no round ending and no pressure ramp is being built, and these measurements stand as the frozen pre-skills baseline**).
- **Growth identity stays per-weapon** — but see the roster table's ⚠ note: the dagger's axis changed during the undocumented era (+SPD → +DMG), and the owner ruled 2026-10-28 that the skills pass decides every axis, so that ⚠ was a deliberate deferral — **discharged for the dagger the same day: +0.7 DMG ratified, Heavy synergy, no sim change**; the v1.0 batch copied traits wholesale from the existing classes ("melee = axe, ranged = bow; balance later"). Growth identity is therefore *provisional* now, not locked.
- **What differentiates a weapon:** length, drawn shape, hold, growth axis, and special effects (shot behaviour) — not base numbers.
- History: the v0.7 re-baseline consequences (buzzsaw vanished, heavy lean grew) and the v0.7 build record live in the archive. **[Amended 2026-10-28:]** "buzzsaw vanished" was a damage-5 fact — at base damage 1 (`dmg1-r21` onward) natscan reads maxSpin **103.5 rad/s on 8 of 30 naturals**, so the ≥25 rad/s band is crossed routinely and the buzzsaw is back. Open question 1's symptom list carries the current numbers; the ceiling's remaining headroom is measured in the skills-prep cost map.

### Fighter skill vs weapon trait — the model (owner ruling 2026-10-28: **M2**, two languages — **the first special skill BUILT as `skill-r29` and RETIRED at `nocombo-r34`**; see NO COMBOS below)

**The ruling.** A weapon's **trait** (the row field was `ability` until the 2026-10-28 rename below) is *data* — a growth rate on the shared axes, read at the one site where growth happens (`grow()`). A fighter's **skill** is a **hook** in `CONTRACT.md`'s sense: it reads the player and a small context and returns a modified value, never mutates state, never depends on another player's hook, **modifies an existing mechanic and never introduces one**, may consume the game's seeded RNG but never create or seed one, and leaves anything time-dependent to the game's own per-tick logic. One skill per player per game, expressed through one hook or several; identity stays global, skill stays local.

**Adopted lazily — this ruling changes no code.** CONTRACT's optionality rule (where a game calls a hook a player doesn't implement, the base value passes through unchanged) means the two shipped numeric skills — `Speedy {spin: 0.30}`, `Heavy {dmg: 0.9}` — stay legal exactly as they are, and the hook indirection is introduced by the **first non-numeric skill**, not before. Nothing is threaded speculatively; the canonical is untouched by this ruling (md5 `86ff2d5bffc6a3942e6c9eba12ccef09`, build `sigil-r23`).

**The consequence that shapes the pass.** Because a hook may not introduce a mechanic, anything a skill is meant to touch must exist in the *game* first: poison, frost, comet burn, damage-over-time and runtime length growth are **game-layer mechanics**, and only then can a skill modify them. The pass has two layers — **(1) authorized hook targets** (game mechanics, each owing its own probe) and **(2) the hooks themselves**.

**Why M2 and not M1 — the measured state of the one-language build.** `grow()` is the *only* sim consumer of `.skill` and `.trait`. Traits are binary across all 22 weapons (12 × `{spin: 0, dmg: 0.7}`, 10 × `{spin: 0.70, dmg: 0}`), so the unit of differentiation today is the *(fighter × weapon)* pair resolving to one of four growth vectors — the measured ω 103.5 maximum is exactly the Speedy × spin-weapon cell (+1.00/hit × 100 hits). The display hard-codes that binary: `SKILL_SHORT = f.skill.spin ? '+SPD' : '+DMG'`, so a fighter with both axes, neither, or a non-numeric skill is **silently mislabelled "+DMG / Hit"**; the ridiculousness trackers are exactly two (`G.maxSpin`, `G.maxDmg`) against a fixed three-channel SPD-DMG legend; and a shot inherits exactly one per-fighter quantity at birth (`dmg: f.dmg`), with `r`/`speed`/`len`/`turn`/`bounce` all reading the weapon row — which is what makes per-fighter shot axes the cheap spectacle (one line each at the birth site).

**Cost of any new axis** (the budget rule, from the skills-prep cost map): a fighter field plus its per-round reset · the consumer site that reads it at hit or launch time · the legend/poster, where a fourth channel is a layout change · a `maxDmg`/`maxSpin`-class tracker · the fingerprint's hashed fields · **and its own probe** — the facing pass's vacuous-unextended-run trap is the precedent: a harness that passes without covering the new flag proves nothing.

**Closed alongside it (owner pick 2026-10-28): parry rewards nothing, full stop — and no skill may reward a parry either.** That removes spin-per-parry, which the spin-ceiling measurement named the likeliest way to wake the dormant `omegaCap: 140`, and leaves **damaging hit, time and launch** as the only growth triggers. Time and launch are contextual, so either one is the first thing that forces a real hook rather than a number.

**Settled under M2 — the five rulings (owner, 2026-10-28).** **(1) Stacking: it adds.** A fighter's skill and the weapon's trait stack additively on the shared axes, exactly as `grow()` already does (`sk.spin + ab.spin`, `sk.dmg + ab.dmg`), so the numeric site is unchanged by the model ruling; a hook that modifies a *different* mechanic adds to the growth the weapon contributes rather than replacing it. **(2) Display: shown in the legend, as a short authored label.** The legend already carries a skill cell per fighter (the `class="ex"` cell between the name and the weapon columns), so this is an **authoring change, not a layout change**: `SKILL_SHORT`'s binary derivation (`f.skill.spin ? '+SPD' : '+DMG'`) is replaced by a per-fighter few-word line in the style of the existing poster prose (`line: 'Spins faster each hit'`) — the owner's example for a spear: **"gets longer"**. Two consequences: the silent-mislabel defect dies with the derivation (a both-axes / neither / non-numeric skill can no longer read "+DMG / Hit"), and the weapon column keeps its own `brief` + `line`. The SPD/DMG numeric cell is untouched — **a new *numeric* axis is still a layout change; a prose label is free.** **(3) Authorized hook targets: yes — length growth, per-fighter shot multipliers and knock.** Each is game-layer work first (a hook may not introduce a mechanic) and each owes its own probe. Length growth stays the expensive one: `W.len` is consumed at boot to build SPAN, REACH, the scaled polys and the baked covering circles, so runtime growth threads a per-fighter length scale through `spineFrame`, `bladeCircles` and the renderer, invalidates REACH (the parryGap prune bound) and MINR (the adaptive-substep budget), and cannot be caught by the boot LEN_MIN/LT gate — **the ceiling has to live inside the growth rule**. Shot multipliers are the cheap ones (`r`/`speed`/`len`/`turn`/`bounce` snapshot at birth, one line each, `dmg: f.dmg` as the precedent); knock is one hit-time read of a per-fighter field (today a global `CFG.hitKnock` 130, read at exactly two sites — `bladeVsBody` and `shotHitBody` — which makes it the **only cheap axis live on all 22 weapons** rather than on one class: the launch-snapshot axes are inert on the 12 melee weapons and runtime length growth is inert on the 10 projectile ones). *[Re-keyed by the axis-placement ruling later the same day: length growth and the shot multipliers are **weapon-row data**, not fighter hook targets — knock is the fighter-side universal axis. See **Axis placement** below.]* **(4) The spin cap: leave it.** `omegaCap: 140` stays silent and dormant (36.5 hits of headroom at +1.00/hit; stability limit ω ≈ 258 at the worst pair), revisited only if a spin-flavoured skill actually threatens to reach it — no sim change, no kept pair, no re-measurement. **(5) Elemental effects: yes, into the game layer — design deferred.** Poison, frost and comet/fire are authorized as **game mechanics**, which is what M2 requires before any skill can modify them; the owner's word on their shapes is "we will figer it out later". The art already pre-figures them: KF1/KF2 fire comet · KP1/KP2 poison · KN1 frost · KV1/KV2 fire-orange.

**NO COMBOS (owner ruling 2026-10-31, codified at `nocombo-r34`).** A skill and a trait may stack **only by addition on a shared axis**; neither may reach into the other's mechanic. There are **no unique fighter×weapon combinations**: one bot's weapon may never behave differently from anyone else's, and every skill must be **universal** (live on all 22 weapons) or **contextual in a class-independent way**, so a bot's identity survives the dice roll by construction. The ruling retired the one violation — `skill.lenSteps`, the `skill-r29` first special skill, which added ladder steps to the spear's cap for a single carrier. Owner, on the mechanic being floated again: *"if i ever did that, its a mistake on my side."* Every cap is therefore uniform (`LEN_STEPS` 12), and the rule lives where a builder will read it: the canonical's TRAIT/SKILL REGISTRY block (the FIGHTERS comment and the WHAT DOES NOT EXIST bullet). Same ruling, the shape of the rest of the pass: **weapon-trait mechanics first (20 remain), then the bot cast — every bot a unique skill — then balance**; skills and traits may add up where they share an axis. One lesson from the retired carrier survives as live doctrine: **damage-coupled growth is self-limiting**, because the holder's own damage sets the hit budget the growth has to fit inside.

**Axis placement (owner ruling 2026-10-28: "design it out").** An axis whose effect depends on the weapon **class** is carried as **weapon-row data** — a rate, exactly like `trait: {spin, dmg}` — and consumed by a game-layer mechanic: the launch-snapshot axes (`r`/`speed`/`len`/`turn`/`bounce`, live on the 10 projectile weapons) and runtime length growth (live on the 12 melee ones). A **fighter's skill** takes only what is live on all 22 weapons — spin growth, damage growth, knock (`CFG.hitKnock`, whose two consumers are `bladeVsBody` and `shotHitBody`) — or a contextual trigger that does not depend on weapon class — the class-independent contextual triggers are per-time and conditional-on-state only — **per-launch is class-dependent** (only the 10 projectile weapons ever launch), so a launch-triggered effect belongs on the weapon row, not on a fighter. **Why:** weapons are dice-rolled each round, so a fighter's identity has to survive the roll; a class-dependent fighter skill flickers (live on 12/22 or 10/22), while a weapon-keyed rate never does, because its line is only ever read while that weapon is held. **Consequence for display: no dark label can exist**, so the legend needs no conditional or dimmed state and this ruling owes **no chrome work** — the skill cell becomes the authored few-word line of ruling 2 and is always true, and the class-dependent flavour rides in the weapon's own `line`/`brief`. **M2 stays intact:** a rate on the weapon row is still *data*, the mechanic consuming it is still game-layer, and only the fighter's skill is a hook. **What it re-keys:** the length-growth spectacle ("gets longer") belongs to the **spear** — and to any other melee weapon given a length rate — not to a fighter; either fighter gets it whenever they hold that weapon, and it is still built in this pass. **Rejected with reasons** (so the fork is not re-litigated): conditional label wording ("longer reaches when melee") — free, but the label sits dark on half the rolls and the audience cannot tell why nothing happened; dimming the label while dark — cheap and idiomatic (the legend already carries `class="out"` for a dead fighter and `wp idle` + "rolling…" pre-reveal, it re-renders per frame and already resolves the held weapon, and chromecheck asserts legend *structure* only — `ccard`, `table`, `qn` — so it would cost one CSS rule, a re-run and the same treatment on the VS poster), but unnecessary once no dark label can exist. Both remain available if a specific skill is ever judged worth the flicker.

**The cast (owner ruling 2026-10-28): two generic bots, and the numeric tier is complete at two.** The cast stays at Speedy (`skill: {spin: 0.30}`) and Heavy (`skill: {dmg: 0.9}`) for now, and they are not placeholders — they are the **generic tier**: the two most legible skills possible, and SPEC’s naming rule satisfied outright ("Heavy" tells a viewer what to expect before the fight starts). Each owns one of the two universal numeric growth axes, so between them they cover the whole numeric space; there is no third generic skill left to write, which is why every later bot is **special/unique by necessity rather than by taste**. **That tier is what pays for the hook interface:** under M2 a numeric skill is *data* and needs no code, while a contextual skill (per-time, conditional-on-state, knock, length growth) is the first thing that requires hooks to exist — so **the hook machinery is not built until a special skill exists to hang on it.** **Parked with its analysis attached — knock is the cheapest available third axis.** `CFG.hitKnock: 130` has exactly two read sites, `bladeVsBody` (melee) and `shotHitBody` (projectile), so a per-fighter knock multiplier is live on all 22 weapons and satisfies the axis-placement ruling with no dark label.
The shelved shape was Heavy dealing more ("shoves harder") and Speedy taking less ("stays put"); both directions share one mechanic, one consumer pair and one probe, so the pair costs roughly one axis. When taken up it is a **sim change**: kept pair, fingerprint re-baseline, and a bound measured against `maxSpeed` 1200 / `subMargin` 1200 **before** any number lands. **Two things to watch, recorded so they are not discovered late.** (a) *A legibility asymmetry:* Speedy’s skill is visible — the weapon genuinely spins faster and compounds into something you can see — while Heavy’s currently reads as a climbing DMG figure and a shorter round, which is the weaker signal in a muted video on a phone. If the two ever feel unequal on screen, the fix is a visible expression of damage, not a bigger number. (b) *Do not tune +0.30 against +0.9 by eye:* whether they are equal in value is empirical — spin growth is bounded by the dormant `omegaCap` and buys spectacle plus hit frequency, while damage growth shortens a 100 hp round and is front-loaded — and it is owed to the sanctioned `measure.mjs` run, not to a judgement call.
**[PAID 2026-10-28 — the sanctioned run landed.]** Measured like-for-like, weapon class held constant, shield cells excluded: Heavy wins **65.6%** of melee mirrors (Speedy 34.4%; 108 cells, 2,073 rounds) and **75.1%** of projectile mirrors (Speedy 24.9%; 86 cells, 1,125 rounds). So they are not equal in value — and not parallel axes either. Damage reaches both offence paths (blades `dealt = a.dmg`; shots carry the thrower's `f.dmg` snapshotted at launch) while spin reaches neither, and since the 10 projectile weapons are exactly the 10 spin-trait weapons, Speedy holding one has `dmgGain = 0` and its shots do base damage for the whole battle. **No number moved as a result**; this is the evidence a future tuning decision would use, not a ruling. **Synergy grid, for the record:** 12 weapons carry `{spin: 0, dmg: 0.7}` and 10 carry `{spin: 0.70, dmg: 0}`, so each fighter has synergy weapons and cross weapons — four combinations, of which Speedy × spin-trait (+1.00/hit) is the cell that produced the measured ω 103.5 maximum. The dagger is the one row flagged ⚠ for the skills pass, and under this cast its axis question is concrete: +0.7 DMG makes it a Heavy-synergy weapon (1.6/hit together), +0.7 SPIN makes it a Speedy-synergy weapon (1.00/hit) and moves the roster split from 12/10 to 11/11.

**Owner ruling 2026-10-28 (post-`lengrow-r28`) — NO BALANCING DURING THE SKILLS PASS, and the three balance-shaped debts are deferred to its end.** Owner, after playtesting the triple-length spear: *"it looks good now, i think we should hold back on re run, all the stats you keep delivering about other weapons etc, i know its unbalanced etc, we are not trying to balance the game at all right now, we are making the skills/mechanics, a new balancing will come afterwards."* This is a standing rule change, not a one-off, and it binds the implementer's reporting as well as the work. **Deferred to the end of the skills pass, all three, by explicit owner confirmation:** (1) the **484-cell re-run** — it would snapshot win rates the first special skill immediately invalidates, and it costs ~7.16 h of the owner's machine to buy a number that gets thrown away; (2) the **rotational-DOF resolver rework** — deferred so it is designed against *final* geometry rather than redone when skills change reach or knock; law 3 stays **RED and disclosed** in the meantime, and the interim rule is that **nothing in the skills pass may depend on the resolver being correct**; (3) the **spear-bearing fingerprint cell** — deferred because the skills pass will move hashes anyway, so the pass should end with **one** new baseline rather than two. **Reporting rule that goes with it:** stop delivering per-weapon win rates, holder-win% comparisons and damage-vs-growth re-measurements; a Measured-facts entry now records **mechanics** — what the code does, what it costs, what is proven — and not a balance table. The one sweep that stays legitimate is the *"does this mechanic actually work"* differential (as `lengrow-r28`'s 50-cell run caught that +35% had shipped a crippled spear), reported as works / does-not-work rather than as a 22-weapon ranking. What is **not** deferred, because it is correctness rather than balance: the house gate, the build proofs and the `LEN_REMAP_CEIL` boot guard · `dmg` 0.3 staying marked **provisional** · the law-3 disclosure · the two blind axes in the fingerprint suite remaining *named* even though the cell that closes one is deferred.

**Owner ruling 2026-10-28 — WEAPON TRAITS RESET EVERY ROUND. The round is a hard reset boundary and no skill may carry trait growth across it.** Owner, rejecting a proposed first special skill whose entire mechanic was keeping the spear's accumulated length between rounds: *"i dont like this at all, each round weapons traits should reset."* This **ratifies shipped behaviour rather than changing it** — `rollWeapons` already zeroes all three growth axes at every round start (`f.spin = 0; f.dmg = W.dmg; f.lenStep = 0`, sim :1323-1325), so no code moved and no build stamp bumped. Its force is as a **constraint on every future skill**: cross-round persistence of a weapon trait is now forbidden outright, not merely unimplemented. The length ladder's top step remains the *geometry* ceiling and the round reset remains the *balance* bound — and the second of those is now an owner law rather than an implementation accident. A special skill must therefore express itself **within a round**: a higher ceiling, a faster rate, a different trigger, or a different effect. Never a carried-over state. Recorded here so the rejected shape is not re-proposed: it was cheap (~6 lines, zero new baked geometry, and the "retained step on a weapon with no ladder" hazard was already covered by the `ls ? LEN_LADDER[wId] : null` guards at sim :1117 and :2270) and it was still wrong, because it broke the round boundary. Separately measured while designing it, and worth keeping: for a carrier to be seen starting a round with retained length, he must draw the spear in **two different rounds of the same match** — about **0.6%** of matches at a uniform 1-of-22 roll. Any weapon-trait-hooked skill is roll-conditional at ~4.5% of rounds; that is a property of the random roster, not of this design, and every future special inherits it.

### Length growth — the spear's trait (owner ruling 2026-10-28, **BUILT as `lengrow-r26`, raised to +35% as `lengrow-r27`, then to +200% as `lengrow-r28` — all the same day** — rigid head, junction at 69.23, per-step RE-BAKED coverings)

**The proposal, and why it is a confirmation rather than a new direction.** Owner, 2026-10-28: *"ok, so i was thinking the spear should grow longer each time it hits an opponent, what do you think"*. That is exactly what the **axis-placement ruling** above already re-keyed: *"the length-growth spectacle ("gets longer") belongs to the **spear** — and to any other melee weapon given a length rate — not to a fighter; either fighter gets it whenever they hold that weapon, and it is still built in this pass."* So no doctrine moves. What this entry adds is the shape the earlier ruling left open: the rate, the ladder, the growth geometry, and the measured ceiling that bounds all three.

**Rate and ladder (owner pick 2026-10-28 via ask_user: "1.2% per hit, 12 steps").** **~1.2% per damaging hit, 12 discrete steps.** The sizing came from the baseline rather than from taste: 236,639 hits over 7,891 decided rounds is ~28.5 hits per round, so **~14 damaging hits per fighter per round**, and 1.012^12 = **+15.4%** — which lands inside the measured covering ceiling below with 3 points of margin. Reach goes 205.9 → **~228px** (61.44px radial grip + 144.5px covering extent × 1.154). Roughly one visible step per clean hit, topping out near the end of a long round. **Amended 2026-10-28, the same day, on the owner's *"i want it to be more ridiculous, so increase the growth of the spear even more"*: the rate is now `len: 0.0253` — 2.5% per damaging hit, 12 steps to **+34.96%** — build `lengrow-r27`.** The sizing logic above holds and was re-run rather than assumed: ~14 damaging hits per fighter per round still means a 12-step ladder tops out near the end of a long round, and +35% still lands inside the covering ceiling, but the ceiling is **not** the +18.6% in the table below — that measured a *uniform* stretch. Swept on the rigid map that actually shipped, with the covering held, MISS binds at **tip +39.5%** (shaft k 1.6469, miss 4.59 of the 4.60 band) and fails at +40% (4.61); POKE never binds and `minR` never moves. So +35% carries **4.5 points of margin in rate terms and 0.10px at the binding step**. Reach goes 210.412 → **261.971px** (measured, not estimated as ~228px above), i.e. **+24.5%** over base rather than the +10.8% of `lengrow-r26`. Past ~+40% the covering has to follow the growth — densify per step at boot, or re-bake the twelve rows through `inscribe.mjs --regen` — and neither was needed for this raise. **Amended again 2026-10-28 (`lengrow-r28`): the rate is now `len: 0.0959` — 9.6% per damaging hit, 12 steps to +200.1%, so the spear ends a round THREE times its shipped length.** Owner, on being shown +35%: *"its not ridiculous enough"*. Drawn tip 147.472 → **442.548px**, `REACH.spear` 210.412 → **505.488** (2.40×, so from mid-arena in the 1000px box its tip reaches the wall), top shaft factor **4.2769**. This is the raise that forced the covering to follow the growth — +35% was the last step a `d`-remapped covering could take — so all twelve steps now carry their own **re-baked** rows (`LEN_CIRCLES`, 22→50 circles per step, generated by `.qa/lengrow-bake.mjs`, never hand-edited). `LEN_STEPS` stays 12: at 9.6% a click is ~14px of visible spear, and with ~14 damaging hits per fighter per round the ladder still tops out near the round's end. **Measured on the same 50 forced-spear cells, +200% turned out to be a balance fix and not only a spectacle:** at +35% the spear won **3 of 50** battles (6%); at +200% it wins **33 of 50** (66%), close to the 65.9% holder win rate the 484-cell baseline recorded for the spear at its OLD `dmg` 0.7. The `dmg` 0.7 → 0.3 cut and the growth rate are therefore **coupled**, and +35% had left the spear the weakest weapon in the game. Undecided-at-budget went **down**, 36% → 28%, so the longer spear relieves stalls rather than causing them.

**No `lenCap` constant is introduced — the round IS the cap.** Owner, 2026-10-28: *"no cap let it snowball, we will balance laer if it gets too ridiculous"*. That is safe here for a structural reason: **stats reset every round** (the "fresh snowball" ruling), so growth can never compound across a battle, and a round delivers only ~14 growth events. Stalled rounds are self-limiting too — growth requires a damaging hit, and a stall has few. The 12th step is therefore a **technical** ceiling set by the hitbox, not a gameplay cap; the later balancing conversation is about the *rate*, not the ceiling. Note this is a genuine snowball unlike the other two axes: length raises the *contact area*, which raises the hit rate, which raises the growth rate — superlinear, where spin and damage growth are linear. That is the reason a bound was worth finding even though none was mandated.

**Length-only, NOT uniform — the owner's stated fear, and the reason the obvious implementation was rejected.** Owner: *"does uniform mean on ll sides? i was actually preferring only the lenght, im scared the spear will become "thick""*. It does: a uniform scale multiplies `d` (along the spine), `l` (across it) and `r` (the circle radius) together, so the spear would visibly fatten as it grew. **Rejected.** The chosen geometry stretches **`d` only, holding `l` and `r`** — the shaft elongates and nothing thickens.

**The measured ceiling on length-only growth.** Stretching `d` alone spreads the baked covering circles apart along the spine while their radii stay fixed, so past a per-weapon limit the union stops covering the drawn silhouette and a body inside the art can fail to take damage — precisely the *"gap hits"* the owner made top priority on 2026-10-19. Computed from each weapon's `CIRCLES_V2` rows (the spine-line half-chord `sqrt(r²−l²)` of each circle, swept for interval contiguity under a `d`-stretch `k`):

| weapon | length-only stretch before the covering splits |
|---|---|
| sword | +53.9% |
| hammer | +28.2% |
| mace | +19.9% |
| **spear** | **+18.6%** (reach 205.9 → 233px) |
| axe | +6.6% |
| katana | **+0.0%** — its spine-line circles are already exactly tangent |

The limit is set by each weapon's **baked circle spacing**, not by design intent, so it differs per row and cannot be assumed. The spear's *shaft* alone tolerates **+84%** (r 8.3 circles on a 9.0 pitch, 7.6px of overlap each); what binds at +18.6% is the **head cluster** (circles #11→#14, whose span is bridged by two purely-lateral barb circles contributing nothing on the spine line). **Caveat, recorded so the number is not over-trusted:** this is a *spine-line* proxy. True 2D coverage of the wide head fails somewhat earlier, so **+18.6% is a ceiling, not a budget** — and the ladder's top step owes a real `ingest.mjs` coverage check before it is baked. At the chosen 12 × 1.2% the design sits at +15.4%, inside even the proxy.

**The trilemma, and how the per-round reset dissolves it.** *Length-only*, *no cap* and *no gap hits* cannot all hold: length-only + no gap hits is bounded; length-only + no cap produces gap hits past ~+18%; no cap + no gap hits requires a uniform scale, i.e. thickening. The escape is that growth resets each round, so "no cap" never actually means unbounded — ~14 hits is the bound, and 1.2% × 14 fits inside the proven limit. All three are had at once. **Amended 2026-10-28 (`lengrow-r27`): the trilemma's shape stands, its numbers move.** *"gap hits past ~+18%"* was measured on a **uniform** `d`-stretch; on the rigid map that shipped, with `l` and every `r` held, the swept bound is **+39.5% tip growth** — roughly double — because the head cluster translates as a rigid body instead of being elongated, so only the shaft's circle spacing has to be bridged. And *"1.2% × 14 fits inside the proven limit"* is now **2.5% × 12 = +35%**, which fits inside +39.5% with 0.10px to spare at the binding step. All three are still had at once; the escape is still the per-round reset, and the ladder top is still the geometry ceiling. **Amended again 2026-10-28 (`lengrow-r28`): the wall was hit, and then passed by baking.** The +39.5% swept bound is real, but it bounds only a **`d`-remapped** covering — radii held while the spacing scales. Re-packing each step against its own stretched silhouette lifts it: at +200% the twelve baked rows gate at poke -0.30px and miss **2.30-4.25px**, *better* than the shipped base row's 4.25, because a fresh pack fits the stretched silhouette instead of inheriting the base spacing. The trilemma's third horn is therefore wrong as stated: "no cap + no gap hits" requires **re-baking**, not thickening. The art still never thickens (only `d` is remapped; no poly point's `l` is ever written), and the per-round reset is still what bounds the snowball.

**Pre-baked ladder, not a runtime stretch.** The canonical's inscribed-covering invariant is *"a uniform scale of an inscribed covering stays inscribed"* (:462-463) — and a `d`-only stretch is **not uniform**, so it cannot inherit that proof. Each step therefore needs its **own** covering, baked by `ingest.mjs` from its own `d`-stretched poly. Precedent exists in the canonical itself: :452-455 already rescales the hammer/axe/spear polys at boot by `LT / maxD(P)` and re-derives their coverings. Two bonuses follow — the art stays *authored* rather than deformed at runtime, and **discrete steps read better on video**: a spear that clicks visibly longer per hit is a beat a viewer can see, where continuous 1.2% is invisible until it suddenly is not. Cost is ~12 extra covering rows for one weapon (19 circles each), a per-fighter step index, and a lookup in `bladeCircles` plus the renderer. **Amended 2026-10-28 (built as `lengrow-r26`): the per-step covering is exactly as specified, but the bake is NOT `ingest.mjs`'s and the map is NOT a uniform `d`-stretch.** The owner's geometry ruling of the same day (ask_user) chose **"rigid head, junction at 69.23"** over the recorded uniform stretch, and the measurement backed the choice:
`.qa/lengrow-gate.mjs` in uniform mode first breaks the house gate at **+6.1%** (miss 5.14px against a 4.6px band), because stretching the head cluster deforms the very barb geometry its covering was packed against; under the rigid map — every point at or behind the junction `J` scales by one factor `k`, every point past it translates by one shared delta `(k-1)·J` — the head moves as a **rigid body**, its protrusion past the last circle stays at the shipped ~3.0px, and **all twelve steps pass**. So the recorded conclusion *"each of the twelve steps must be baked"* is correct for the geometry it measured and **moot for the geometry that shipped**: `LEN_LADDER` is built **at boot** from the already-`:452-455`-normalised polys, inherits the shipped covering, and remaps `d` only — no `ingest.mjs` pass, no authored rows, and `.qa/bake-rows.mjs` is not on this build's path. The two bonuses survive unchanged: the art is never deformed at runtime beyond the ruled map, and a step is still a visible click. `k` is **derived, never authored**: `k_s = 1 + ((1.012)^s - 1)·tip/J`, giving shaft factors 1.0197 → **1.2520** to deliver the owner's 1.2%-on-the-**tip** observable (tip factors 1.0120 → 1.1539, **+15.39%**).
**Amended again 2026-10-28 (`lengrow-r28`): this paragraph's original conclusion is now the shipped design, arrived at by a third route.** The original text called for an `ingest.mjs` bake of authored rows; the `lengrow-r26` amendment retired that in favour of a boot-time `d`-remap that "costs no data". At +200% the remap route is past its ceiling, so per-step coverings ARE baked — but **not** by `ingest.mjs` and **not** as authored `INGR` data. `.qa/lengrow-bake.mjs` stretches the art per step in a scratch temp, runs the sanctioned row-splice baker (`.qa/bake-rows.mjs` → `inscribe.mjs`'s raster-EDT greedy union-inscribed regen — the same packer that baked all 22 shipped rows), and splices the twelve rows into a marked `LEN_CIRCLES` block. So **no new packing algorithm enters the sim**: the ladder reads baked data and maps only the art at boot. That **reverses the r26 amendment's claim that `.qa/bake-rows.mjs` is not on this build's path** — it now is, and it is the only tool that writes to the canonical. `--verify` re-gates every step's own row against its own art (12/12 PASS). The cost is what the original paragraph predicted: ~12 extra covering rows for one weapon, here 421 circles / 11.7 KB.

**Damage lowered alongside it, provisionally.** Owner: *"make it lower, it doesnt really matter, we are also balancing the damage later"*. The spear's `trait: { spin: 0.0, dmg: 0.7 }` becomes **`dmg: 0.3`**, flagged **provisional** — it is not a balance decision, it is a placeholder pending the damage pass. Stacking is unaffected (ruling 1: skill and trait add on the shared axes).

**What it will cost when built** — consistent with the cost map already on record above, restated against today's chosen geometry: a per-fighter `f.lenStep` plus its per-round reset · **`REACH` and `MINR` become per-fighter**, which touches the adaptive-substep budget (:1245-1252, `delta` from `MINR` and `relV` from `REACH`), the `parryGap` prune bound, and the nudge cap `CFG.nudgePx / REACH` (:1724) · `spineFrame`, `bladeCircles` and the renderer · the fingerprint's hashed fields · **and its own probe**, per the vacuous-unextended-run precedent (a harness that passes without covering the new flag proves nothing). The boot `LEN_MIN`/`LT` gate at :663-664 **cannot catch this** — it checks authored `W.len` on the shared table at boot, so the ceiling has to live inside the growth rule, exactly as the earlier cost map said. And `W.len` must never be mutated: it is shared table data, so writing to it would leak across both fighters and across rounds. **Amended 2026-10-28 (built): this cost map is partly superseded by the smaller scope the owner chose.** `f.lenStep` and its per-round reset landed as described (`:1163`, and `:1251` inside `rollWeapons`, which the reveal branch calls at `phaseT === 0`) · `bladeCircles` and the renderer landed (`drawWeapon` gained an optional `polys` with `const PS = polys || W.poly.polys`, `drawWeaponOn` an optional `ls`, and both fight-view call sites pass `f.lenStep`; the reveal poster and the stills stay step 0, which is correct because a fresh fighter *is* step 0) · **`spineFrame` needed no step at all** — it is a radial hold and has no length input. **`REACH` and `MINR` did NOT become per-fighter**: the owner picked the minimal spear-only build with the budget question disclosed rather than engineered away. `REACH.spear` is instead raised **once, at boot, to the top step's value** (210.412 → **233.107**), which is the conservative bound — so the under-budgeting this paragraph feared **does not occur**; what remains is that low steps are slightly **over**-budgeted (a few extra substeps while a spear is alive), and the nudge cap `CFG.nudgePx / REACH` (`:1724`) is 9.7% smaller for the spear. `MINR.spear` needed no change whatsoever: the ladder holds every `l` and `r`, so the thinnest circle is the same circle at every step (2.20). **The fingerprint's hashed fields were NOT extended** — `f.lenStep` is absent from the `:99-100` list — and the landing entry below explains why adding it would have bought nothing. **No hook machinery is required — this does not wait on a special skill.** Under M2 a *rate on the weapon row* is **data** and the mechanic consuming it is **game-layer**, so length growth needs no hook indirection. ### Movement speed — cruise, spikes and settle (doctrine + build 2026-10-21 — REVERTED same day at owner playtest; design record only)

**REVERTED at owner playtest (2026-10-21, owner: "ok i dont like that at all, it does not look natural anymore like it did before").** The sim is back to pre-doctrine ballistics, proven by fingerprint byte-identical to `.qa/fp-pre-cruise.json`. Everything below survives as a **design record only** — not normative, not to be re-proposed as-is without the owner; if the idea ever returns, it returns as separable pieces (floor-only vs settle-only) at owner word, with the playtest verdict on record.

Owner: "i think we should have a unified default speed everyone shares, but this can never be increased only by colissions … i dont want any bot to ever go below that speed, and a sped up bot does not maintain that speed forever"; on feel: "do what you think is best for the viewer, i want satisfying 'predictable/realistic' patterns (it also looks good right now)" with one explicit prohibition — no bot may ever change direction without a cause ("a bot if falling straight down and suddenly falls to the left with no interference"). The two dials were delegated to the assistant ("do what you think is best"): **cruise 250 px/s, settle half-life 0.5 s** — rationale at the end. The doctrine is normative for the build; the mechanics stay as shipped until then.

1. **Cruise is a floor, never a steer.** Every living fighter in the fight phase holds |v| ≥ cruise. The floor scales magnitude along the current travel direction only; at near-zero speed the fallback direction is gravity's. The regulator never adds lateral velocity: **direction is authored by gravity and contact alone** (walls, floor, bodies, blades) — the owner's falling-straight-down prohibition, written as a rule.
2. **Ballistics stay ballistics.** Gravity's own speed authorship — accelerating falls, slow apexes, the floaty arc that "looks good right now" — is never damped, and the round's launch speed (430) remains the opening ballistic baseline. Settle never touches gravity-authored speed; it only drains collision-authored excess.
3. **Only collisions author excess; excess settles.** Parry shove, hit knock, body-body exchange and the floor trampoline's injection add speed above the ballistic baseline; that excess decays with the settle half-life back toward the baseline, so a sped-up bot visibly calms (~12% of the excess left after 1.5s) and nothing ratchets forever. Today nothing subtracts speed — elastic walls preserve it, injections only add — so late-round pace creeps toward the temporary cap structurally; settle is the fix. Walls stay perfectly elastic (they preserve the arc energy that makes the current look); the floor re-injects its spike at every touch, so the perpetual bounce rhythm stays the show — now with a settling peak instead of a permanent one.
4. **Scope:** fight phase, living fighters only. Reveal, K.O. and over poses are untouched; the dead stay frozen as today.
5. **Spin doctrine stands as built:** shared ω 3.5, growth on damaging hits from fighter skill AND weapon trait — re-confirmed 2026-10-21 as balance-pass material, not a doctrine change (owner: "dont bother its going to be part of balancing later").
6. **Vocabulary (SPEC one-word rule):** **cruise speed** = the shared default floor; **excess** = speed above the ballistic baseline; **settle** = the excess's decay. No synonyms in docs, UI or harness output.
7. **Dial rationale (assistant, viewer-first, recorded for the balance pass):** cruise 250 — low enough that typical apex breathing (|vx| ≈ 250–430) survives as the approved floaty arc, high enough that the crawl/hover states (apex with little horizontal, bottom-centre cradle dwells — the stall reds' habitat) become a gentle glide: no dead air on the frame. Settle 0.5s — a parry shove separates the pair at full force first and calms afterwards, so spikes read as spikes and never as a new cruise. Both numbers join open question 1's knob list pending the first playtest. With settle carrying the pace-governor job, the temporary `maxSpeed` cap's keep/lift/replace verdict loses urgency: it degrades to a pure safety ceiling.
8. **When the build is ordered:** sim change → fingerprint ritual + the full fast tier; `measure.mjs` on owner go. Expect the stall tail and mirror-length reds to move (the floor removes low-speed dwells from both); the substep budget gains a trivially small floor term (cruise is far below impulse speeds).

**Build record (same day, owner order) — and revert:** built as a per-fighter excess ledger (impulses register, half-life drains; walls mirror, the floor re-anchors so the bounce stays ballistic — a decaying floor injection would have crushed the trampoline arc inside one half-life, disclosed at build); magnitude-only floor, no steering anywhere. Owner playtest rejected it same-day ("i dont like that at all, it does not look natural anymore like it did before"); all nine edits reverted byte-identically (`fp-after.json` restored; the cruise-era bytes at `.qa/fp-post-cruise.json`). Every number, proof and the one salvageable measurement (the floor removed low-speed dwells: four capped fingerprint cells terminated — the stall tail is real and addressable, this cure's feel was not acceptable) lives in **Measured facts**, entries "Cruise build" and "Cruise build REVERTED".

### Projectile weapons — the shot system (owner decisions 2026-10-16/17/19)

**Landed at roster-r12 (2026-10-25) — the kind registry and launch doctrine as they now stand:** nine data kinds in `SHOTS_ART` (arrow · bolt · knife · orb · spark · spell · halo · nova · vortex) plus the **copy kinds** star/boom/javelin, whose throws draw the wielder's own weapon polys at the area-centroid pivot (mid-meAT for hollow arcs) with slowed spins (owner word: the shipped ~10 rev/s aliased). Knives fire a **three-knife volley** (owner ruling b: cadence ×3 = damage-rate neutral; tips at the measured anchors (17.69,−60.95)/(50.7,−73.8)/(83.71,−60.95), each along its own blade axis in **spine-frame axes, never wAngle trig**; rim clamp on out-of-arena tips). The tome cycles halo→nova→vortex in **strict rotation** (provisional implementer recommendation, playtest silent); the scroll fires the spell comet. **[2026-10-28 — launcher consolidation plus two owner rulings: all three of those special-cases are now ROW DATA (`W.shot.volley` — the anchors, in WORLD px: they equal the ×1.3-scaled poly's own extremes and sit deliberately OUTSIDE the boot weaponScale loop, which scales shot r/off/len — `W.shot.revs` 3, `W.shot.cycle` the trio) and `fireShots` now contains no `f.weapon === …` test at all. The tome trio's PROVISIONAL marker is now a ruling: owner 2026-10-28 — the three kinds become mechanically distinct CONTENT in the skills pass (the affinity locals below already pre-figure fire/poison/frost), so the shipped rotation stands as the placeholder and adding or re-ordering kinds is a data edit. The tome row's `kind: 'page'` is vestigial: the cycle supersedes it in the launcher and HALO has had no 'page' tint since this split. Recorded, not removed — a data change is a sim change until proven otherwise.]** **Affinity locals** declared in-zone (scroll precedent):
KF1/KF2 fire comet · KP1/KP2 poison · KN1 frost · KV1/KV2 fire-orange — owner word 2026-10-25: they pre-figure the skill pass. Sigil doctrine on shots: one KC accent element per kind (dyed fletching, binding band, rune nucleus), whole-body KC waived only for the orb/spark family. **[2026-10-28, sigil legibility: for the four spell-family kinds the KC nucleus is no longer a delivered shape. It is a plain 32-gon carrier disc whose radius IS the launched hitbox (`WEAPONS.scroll.shot.r` / `WEAPONS.tome.shot.r`, derived so it tracks `weaponScale`), sitting on a dark ink plate at 1.3× that radius and flagged `vis: 1` so it paints without a stroke (the mechanism `drawPolySet`'s own comment had described since 2026-10-22 but that no shape could reach, because `build()` dropped the flag — now passed through). Owner pick "grow + solid mark", applied to all four kinds; the delivered nuclei (the scroll's 4-point star, the trio's 32-gon at r 5.25) are retired verbatim to CHRONICLE-archive.md and the flame layers stay delivery-verbatim. Measured reason: the delivered nucleus was 5.68 css px across with NO keyline at all, at 1.60–2.32:1 against its own flame, on a 15.4 ms dwell (≈0.93 frames).]** Launch-doctrine addenda (close item 8):
per-blade axes for fanned tangential volleys · art-centre spawns for copy kinds · rim clamp. `shot.len` survives as fingerprint-hashed flight state though no draw reads it — the legacy procedural shot draws (drawArrow/drawJavelin and the seven branches) retired at the 2026-10-25 cleanup, tombstoned at drawShot.

The sling (v0.7) established the archetype; the bow replaced it (v0.9, owner 2026-10-19: "the sling should be removed, instead make it a bow, and the projectiles should be arrows") and v1.0 generalised it into the shot system. The full sling history — its four default rules, the swat decision, the mid-spine launch era, the v0.7.x baselines — is in the archive; what follows is the current normative doctrine.

**The projectile rule (owner 2026-10-19, restating and widening the 2026-10-17 rule):** "ranged weapons (shooting projectiles), their weapons do not damage, only their projetiles." A weapon with a shot config deals **no spine damage**, whatever its hold — the radial-hold launchers (staff, wand) included. The spine stays a full solid: it latches and knocks the body (zero-damage shove), parries weapon-vs-weapon, and swats enemy shots. Its shot is its only damage.

**Firing is physics, not a scheduler.** One shot leaves per full revolution of the spin (a per-fighter radian accumulator, `fireAcc += |spin|·sdt`, releases at 2π) — **spin rate IS fire rate**, no cooldown stat, no ammo, no new vocabulary: `+SPD / Hit` on a launcher *is* faster shooting. Firing falls out of the physics because nobody pilots these bots.

**Launch doctrine (owner 2026-10-19):** "when the weapon is radial, shoot from the tip, when it is the opposite, shoot from the middle, like bow and crossbow." A **radial-hold** launcher releases at the spine **tip** (t = 1), flying outward along the spine (staff, wand). A **tangential-hold** launcher releases at the spine **middle** (t = 0.5, the grip point on the rim); there the direction splits per weapon: *shooting* weapons (bow, crossbow — `fire: 'radial'`) send the shot radially **out** of the grip, offset by `shot.off` so the head starts at the belly — a bow shoots where its belly faces, not along its limbs; *thrown* weapons (boomerang, shuriken) leave **tangentially in the spin direction**. Law 6s recomputes every launch from its stored firing pose to the hold-derived point (0 off-point ever, 6175 checked at the v1.2 probe). This supersedes the v0.7.2 "always from the middle" rule.

**Shot damage (owner decision, 2026-10-16):** the shot launches with the thrower's **current** damage — snapshotted at launch — and there is no separate projectile stat (one damage number per fighter, `a.dmg`; it grows on hit via the fighter's skill, so a Heavy's shots fatten +0.9 per hit while a Speedy's stay light and come faster).

**Shot flight and deaths.** Straight flight, no gravity, no drag — the boomerang alone curves (its locked 421×250px oval, row turn 4.0 with the 0.65 elongation modulation, anchored to its wielder — `halo-r39`). Deaths, in the fixed deterministic per-substep order rim → body → swat → shot-shot: **rim** kills (law 1 — walls never damage); the sanctioned exceptions are the shuriken star's **ETERNAL RICOCHET** (`shot.ricochet`, `ricolaw-r41` — the rim never kills a star; it mirrors forever at row speed), the boomerang's **pierce**, and the crossbow's **NAIL** (`shot.pin`, `pinlaw-r44` — the bolt sticks just inside the rim as a shot AT REST, `speed` 0, keeping its impact flight line as the drawn facing (`pinfix-r45`; the inward knock vector is stored separately as `pnx/pny`); it ends only on the foe's body (the law-4 hit, consumed), the foe's blade (swat), an in-flight enemy shot (cross) or the roll-clear; the owner walks through his own nails; nail×nail never crosses — statics cannot visibly resolve). Shot-vs-shot is ENEMY-ONLY since `multgrow-r42` (generalizing the r41 star exemption at the owner's option-A ruling): SAME-OWNER pairs skip the cross test on EVERY shot class — friendly fire does not exist; enemy pairs still cancel both. **Body** contact is a damaging hit and consumes the shot (law 4 structural — the fourth row-owned exception is the javelin's **SKEWER**, `skewer-r46`: the hit does NOT consume the spear; it impales, carries the victim to the rim, pins and bleeds them, and only the victim's own blade cutting it, an enemy cross, or the roll ends it; a killing hit consumes normally). **Blade** contact is a **swat**: the shot is destroyed and nothing else happens — no parry event, **no spin flip on either fighter** (the named, documented rule-5 exception; readable on the reveal poster and legend line). **Shot-vs-shot** cancels both — enemy pairs only (symmetric, provable). **No friendly fire** — built as *owner-blindness*: a shot is never tested against its owner's body, blade or SHOTS (`multgrow-r42`), so it can never self-destruct, self-swat or self-cross. **Law 3 turns asymmetric:** a shot has no body behind it to push, so instead of being separated it **loses every collision it makes** — never overlapping blade, body, rim or another shot on a rendered frame. Detection keeps the same guarantee as blades: substeps sized so relative travel per substep ≤ half the narrowest window — blade-tip vs shot speed is the largest relative velocity in the sim, and since v1.2 the shot-vs-shot term budgets the **worst pair** of in-flight shots (mixed speeds: spark 800 vs orb 430 — the old single-speed formula under-budgeted); the audit checks the sim's chosen k against both budgets every tick.

**Drawn shape vs hitbox.** Disc-shaped shots (orb, spark, star, boomerang) draw at exactly `shot.r` — the drawn disc *is* the hitbox. Arrows and bolts (`shot.len`) draw shaft + fletching **trailing behind** the hitbox circle, which sits at the head — the business end is what hits, the trail is paint. "What you see is what hits" survives with that stated reading.

**Audit extension (`measure.mjs`, mutation-tested at birth in v0.7; re-pointed at v1.2 and run the same day — part-0 naturals + the `--solidity` gauntlet, both green; the matrix portion awaits the balance pass).** Seven shot-law checks — 1s damage only on shot-touches-body (recomputed from the stored death pose; 0 phantom ever) · 2s swats only on exact shot-blade touch (swats flip no spin — proven by core law 5's sign audit) · 3s shots never overlap foe blade, foe body, rim, or another shot at tick-entry poses (doubles as the anti-teleport bracket: "outside at entry, biting at death") · 4s accounting — every fired shot has exactly one proven departure (landed / swatted / rim / cross / cleared at the round roll) or is still in flight at the battle end; a shot vanishing without an event is the tunneling alarm · 5s the substep budget audit — 0 violations, 0 `maxSub` engagements · 6s the launch doctrine — every launch recomputes to its hold-derived point · 7s the projectile rule — zero melee hits by projectile weapons, any hold; the core law-4 replica mirrors the sim gate (a gated rising edge is a flag-audited zero-damage shove with no hit event to pair). Shot hits do NOT pair with the bladeStuck replica (a shot is consumed — law 4 is structural) and deliberately do not feed the law-5 parry magnitude pairing (a shot hit grows the thrower *after* the same substep's parry, unlike blade hits — a pairing bug this caught in dev). Stall-timer semantics: hit/parry/**swat**/bounce; event-rate includes shot events. The combo matrix is **forced** (curator knob) — now **324 ordered cells** × 8 shared seeds with the 18-weapon roster (was 169 at 13), because natural rolls thin to a handful of rounds per cell.

### Hold styles (owner decision 2026-10-16, amended 2026-10-19 — BUILT)

How a weapon sits on the body. Owner verdict on the sling's original radial grip: **"it should not point outwards, it should be held along the edge of the body."** Two placements:

- **Radial** (the default): the spine runs straight out from the body centre, grip tucked under the disc (`SPINE_R0` 0.96). All melee weapons and the radial launchers (staff, wand). *Measured 2026-10-28 (authoring-scale pass):* the tuck is **one engine constant, identical for all 13 radial rows** — the grip mounts at `bodyR × SPINE_R0` = **61.44 px**, i.e. **2.56 px inside the rim**, and the own disc is clipped out of the weapon pass, so the overlap is hidden ink rather than a visible seam (11 of the 13 rows put their innermost ink at exactly r 61.44; the axe's butt cut starts 0.45 px forward of `d` 0, r 61.89; the orb is handle-less and floats 46.84 px clear, r 110.84). Detail budget belongs from the guard outwards.
- **Tangential**: the spine is a straight tangent chord at the body's rim point — grip centered on the rim at t = 0.5, both ends floating clear of the disc. Nine rows: bow, crossbow, boomerang, shuriken, knives, javelin, tome, scroll, shield. *Amended 2026-10-28 (authoring-scale pass item 2):* they no longer carry `tuck: false` — a tangential chord never tucks (its art straddles the rim, so the clip would notch it), and the render pass now derives that from `hold`; the nine redundant declarations were removed and only handle-less **radial** art still opts out by name (the orb). Because tangential rows are unclipped, ink inside the rim draws over the own disc — how far inside is per-artist today and is recorded as an open pick in the convention's **Placement & reach** bullet.

**Since v1.2 the hold decides placement and launch point only — not damage capability** (that is the projectile rule's job; the old "ranged = tangential" class identity is dead). A curved rim-hugging spine remains **parked**: the path representation could carry it now, but nothing needs it yet — the straight chord is the mechanics truth unless a future batch decides otherwise.

**Why the contact law holds by construction.** Placement lives in **one layer** (`spineFrame`: spine origin, unit direction, span for a body pose — plus `leadFlip`, the edge-leading mirror of 2026-10-22) consumed identically by the collision circles, the renderer and the harness's audit recomputes — the drawing cannot drift from the hitbox, its mirror included ("what you see is what hits" survives structurally, not by discipline).

### Locked frame (2026-10-15) — the channel's look

Owner-confirmed as **the vibe and look for all games on the channel**, not just this one. No live toggles; every element below is final until an owner decision reopens it. (The **weapon art** is a separate matter and is NOT locked — see below.)

- **Theme: PEBBLE.** Warm gray-taupe page (radial `#c6bda9 → #bab09b → #aca18b`), light warm-sand arena floor (`#e7dfca`) that reads *lighter than the page but never glaring*, cream surfaces (`#ede7d6`), warm ink (`#2e2b22`) and warm gray (`#4a4436`) type. The picker, nine candidates and every code reference were stripped at lock. SPEC.md carries the token record; Phase 3 lifts the table from `spinclash-preview.html` (`TH` object + `:root` tokens).
- **Arena & rim: Hairline.** The circle inscribed in the platform's square bounds; a mid-taupe band (`#a99f86`) with a dark hairline outer edge (`#8d8369`); the floor is flat (a graph-grid texture was tried and removed the same iteration).
- **Scorebug above the arena** — a plain row, no container: mini-bot discs, names in the players' deep tints, the series score big in ink. The only persistent place wins and large names appear.
- **Legend below the arena: Columns** — the frame's **single sanctioned container**: one cream card holding a real `<table>`, two rows, reading order `[mini-bot · tint name · skill code] …air… [weapon · trait code] …air… [SPD · DMG]`. Shorthand codes read `+SPD / Hit` / `+DMG / Hit`; launchers read `+SPD / Hit · <shot> / rev`; the dice-reveal poster teaches the full sentences once per round so the legend can stay terse. Auto table layout aligns every column vertically across rows and hugs the codes to their names; stat numbers live in fixed 3ch tabular boxes so growth never reflows anything (a regression that dropped those boxes once moved the table at double digits — the rule is written here so it survives future edits). Bot names and weapon names carry equal weight (800). No HP in the legend (it lives on the bots), no wins (the scorebug carries them), no icons, no "knocked out" text (the row dim carries K.O.). The table was chosen after a subgrid and a fixed-track grid both died in the owner's viewer — it renders aligned in any engine. This layout is the platform's scoreboard design for every game.
- **Type & color economy — six colors in the whole frame.** Two cast fills (Speedy `#a8892f`, Heavy `#ff6b4a`) for actors only — bots, mini-bot discs; their two deep tints (`#4a3b12`, `#6f2818`, ≥4.5:1 on page and cream) for every name in type; warm ink bold for facts (series score, weapon names, stat numbers); warm gray for explanations (codes, skills). Raw cast color never sets type. Mini-bots are cast fill + the bots' ink border, empty inside, centered on the name's line in legend and scorebug alike.
- **No containers anywhere else.** In-arena moments — round banners — are type straight on the floor (the K.O. card's type was removed at owner word 2026-10-21, "i dont want it to be announced": the round's end reads as the kill-still freeze, the faded disc and the scorebug tick); the battle winner is type on a warm scrim, with the stats tail (`shots X thrown / Y landed / Z swatted`) when any shot flew. The **sanctioned exception is the dice reveal**: the owner-designed VS poster (2026-10-19) covers the arena disc for its 285 ticks and dissolves — a moment, not chrome. Transient name moments (the winner overlay) are announcements, not chrome.
