## Weapon art — the closed convention (locked 2026-10-18, CLOSED 2026-10-27)

Ratified in full at the owner vote of 2026-10-27 ("ok i vote yes") on the convention-close sheet (items 1-9 + P2/P3; the draft retired with the close). Everything below is PRESCRIPTIVE for every future weapon and batch; the descriptive history (the 2026-10-18 lock text, the two-paths era, the commission writeups) is retired verbatim to `CHRONICLE-archive.md`, "Retired at the 2026-10-27 close".

- **Path (2a/3a-3d):** the in-file poly builder via the artist-kit route is THE canonical path — *amended 2026-10-28 (hygiene pass #2): the tooling that realized the route was purged at the pre-balance checkpoint (`artist-kit.html`, `artist-kit.mjs`, `redesign-preview.mjs`, `sheet-v2.mjs`, `design-shots.json`), so the route is now PRESCRIPTIVE-ONLY — its grammar, paste ledger and design brief are retired verbatim to `CHRONICLE-archive.md` ("Retired at the 2026-10-28 pre-balance checkpoint") and the kit-route rebuild re-seeds from there plus the landed canonical art.* `ingest.mjs` stands dormant/superseded, kept at root without privilege (KEPT — it is the live weapon-merge gate with its combat gauntlet). Runbooks retire per delivery and rebuild fresh; `sheet-v2` *was* the standing review vehicle (purged 2026-10-28 — see the Sigil item for what that costs); owner direct edits are legal and reconciled into the record at next touch.
- **Paints (1a/1b/1c/7):** five in art — wood `KW #7a4a2a`, dark wood `KD #4f3220`, steel `KS #8fa3b5`, near-white `KP #eaf6ff` (cutting/striking faces AND paper), light blue `KB #9fe0ff` (gems, stars) — plus the uniform ink outline `#2e2b22`; flat fills, no gradients/texture/glow. Gold `KG` is RETIRED from art (sweep-r15, owner option B, 2026-10-27) and survives only as the carrier-less sigil fallback; amber retired 2026-10-18. The per-weapon reference-colour class is permanent under the scroll's four rules; the spell-family affinity locals (fire/poison/frost/fire-orange) are a permanent extension pre-figuring the skill pass.
- **Sigil (6a-6d):** exactly ONE diegetic carrier-coloured element per weapon via the `KC` tag (recolor-first, never on KP, interior-ink preferred); the one-`KC` invariant is gated by sheet-v2's x1 — *amended 2026-10-28: `sheet-v2.mjs` was purged at the pre-balance checkpoint, so `x1` is review-only until the kit-route rebuild restores a tool that counts `@carrier` polys;* shot nuclei are `KC` ownership carriers inside the doctrine, review accents are tooling outside it; the realized mark map (22 rows) is recorded in the close entry in **Measured facts**.
- **Handheld spec (4a-4d):** the **length band** — floor `LEN_MIN` 54 (the orb, shortest shipped weapon) to ceiling `LT`, named for the spear, **both ends boot-gated** since 2026-10-28 (balance pass item 2; a convention before that, which is how the crossbow came to overshoot it silently in 2026-10-21); one shaft size (~11.5u full width); plain brown butt; flat butt cut; deviations only as named, disclosed owner picks; bands are guidance; per-family proportions carry no prose rules — reference implementations outrank prose; the veterans' rounded caps stay grandfathered until their next art touch (registry re-derived from the delivered art at roster-r12).
- **Placement & reach (2026-10-28, authoring-scale pass item 1 — owner "i want you to do 1 and 2"; every number below measured from the shipped canonical with its own formulas, not estimated).** Both mount rules are **rim-based — nothing is ever drawn from the body centre.** Reach is *measured* from the centre only because that is the sim's single contact coordinate (two discs, centre-to-centre), which is exactly why a reach figure reads larger than the art's own length:
  - **Radial:** the grip (spine `d` 0) mounts at `CFG.bodyR × SPINE_R0` = **61.44 px** — **2.56 px inside the 64 px rim** — from one engine constant shared by all 13 radial rows, so the overlap is not per-weapon data and a new weapon cannot get it wrong. The own disc is clipped out of the weapon pass, so those 2.56 px are *hidden ink*, not a visible seam: the shaft emerges at the rim and reads as held. **Detail budget belongs from the guard outwards** (owner decision 2026-10-18) — anything drawn inside the first ~2.5 px is eaten by the clip. Measured innermost ink: **11 of the 13 radial rows at exactly r 61.44** (hammer, dagger, sword, spear, mace, staff, wand, flail, nunchaku, scythe, katana); the **axe** at r 61.89 (its butt cut starts 0.45 px forward of `d` 0 — sub-pixel, recorded not fixed, and fixing it would cost an art re-bake); the **orb** at r 110.84, i.e. **46.84 px clear of the rim** (handle-less by design — see its row, whose older "overlaps the disc by ≈15px" comment omitted the 61.44 mount offset and is amended in place).
  - **Tangential:** the chord's **midpoint sits exactly on the rim** (64 px), perpendicular to the radius, both ends clear of the disc. Nine rows: bow, crossbow, boomerang, shuriken, knives, javelin, tome, scroll, shield. Tangential art is never clipped (derived from `hold` since 2026-10-28), so ink inside the rim draws over the own disc.
  - **The two reach formulas** (`REACH` is computed at boot from the shipped polys; these are its closed forms — `len` = authored spine, ×1.3 `weaponScale` as played, +1.5 px ink half-stroke): **radial** `reach ≈ 61.4 + 1.3·len + tip-corner + 1.5` → at the ceiling, **206–214 px**, the whole class inside an 8 px band (spear 210.4 with its point on the spine … axe 212.1 with a tapered tip ±54.6 … hammer 213.6 with a flat face ±47.0). **Tangential** `reach ≈ hypot(64, 1.3·len/2) + 1.5` → at the ceiling, **~102 px** (javelin 101.9). Because the chord is centred on the rim, more `len` buys reach by Pythagoras rather than addition — which is why the longest spines in the game (javelin and crossbow, 147.5 as played) sit near the *bottom* of the reach table. Class spread, not unfairness. Full 22-row table: the length-band entry in this section.
  - **Authors do not aim at `LT` by hand.** The heavy four are equalized at boot by measured factors off their own authored tips: mace ×1.00000 (authored maxD 113.44 — the ceiling's source), spear ×1.00053 (113.38), hammer ×1.00389 (113.00), axe ×1.01105 (112.20); the crossbow is cut down by `KX` ×0.99118 (authored 114.45). A new weapon just lands inside the `LEN_MIN`…`LT` band and the boot gate says so: proportions are the author's, the number is the engine's.
  - **The tuck clip can never hide a hitbox:** ink at r ≤ `bodyR` from the own centre cannot be inside the opponent's disc at any legal separation (centres are 2 × `bodyR` = 128 px apart at contact), so "what you see is what hits" survives the clip.
  - **OPEN — recorded, not legislated (needs an owner pick before the next tangential commission):** how a tangential chord's art straddles the rim is currently per-artist, and the shipped nine disagree. Measured radial extent from the body centre: entirely outside — knives 65.7…137.8, crossbow 66.0…130.0, bow 64.0…130.0, boomerang 63.1…135.2; straddling — javelin 56.6…71.3 (±7), scroll 50.8…77.2 (±13), tome 56.2…82.6 (7.8 inside), shield 58.4…85.7 (5.6 inside — a shield covering the body edge, deliberate). Candidates: (a) declare straddling legal and bound it (e.g. ≤ 8 px inside the rim), (b) require entirely-outside like the bow class, (c) leave it to reference implementations, as the convention already prefers for proportions. No behaviour consequence today; it is an art-direction decision.
- **Directionality (5a-5c):** `lead: +/-1` for lateral business contours — **four rows, all -1: katana and scythe (2026-10-22), dagger and staff (2026-10-28 facing pass, owner playtest on the dagger's one-sided white bevel)** — and `headLead: +/-1` for along-chord head ends (javelin +1); art and hitbox mirror together on spin sign; the 180 ms flip transition is the one accepted art-hitbox-divergence window; chains are forbidden the flags by boot throw; the flag registry stands as re-quoted at the landing (leadproof 178/178, 286/286, 182/182, **86/86, 232/232** — the last two added 2026-10-28, when the facing pass extended PROBES/Part A2/CELLS for the dagger and the staff as this harness's own header requires; **an unextended leadproof reports ALL PASS while covering nothing new**, which is what it did on that landing's first run). The 22-row facing audit that found them — KP centroid, off-axis covering circles, outline asymmetry per row — is in the facing-pass entry in **Measured facts**; it confirms the unflagged rows are unflagged for a reason (mirrored double bevels, the orb's zero off-axis circles, chains boot-forbidden) and records the mace's spiral highlights and the tangential rows' radial-axis KP as deliberately *not* facing cues.
- **Circles (roundness class, 2026-10-27):** true circles are cut as 32-gons at authored centre and circumradius; elongated wraps keep their authored contours (the aspect gate above 1.15 exempts them).
- **Bakes and gates (2b-2d):** covering circles generate from the same polys (draw and hitbox cannot drift); parameters locked canonical (1.2u inflate, min r 4, floor 2.0 plus named overrides scroll 1.6 / axe 1.8); no retroactive epsilon/gauntlet for the v1.0 builder batch — the standing suite is the proof regime; partial art edits splice via `.qa/bake-rows.mjs`; the inscribe gate runs after any art edit; leadproof/flipproof re-quote for flagged weapons.
- **Legibility (1d/P3):** silhouette-first and exaggeration stand as guidance; the old squint-at-120px and min-feature gates are retired; the old lock's "squash test" naming is amended to "squint test" (verified against the archive text at the close).
- **Amendment clause (P2):** carried from the 2026-10-18 lock — the owner's in-session word overrides any line here, and the amendment lands in the record the same day.

## Design principles for all games

- **Structure before flavour.** Boredom is fixed by mechanics that generate swings, not by scheduled events or character complexity.
- **Reversals must be attributable.** A swing should be caused by something the audience can point at — a contact, a capture, a raid — never by a hidden number or a scheduled event. (The dice roll is exempt by design: it is an *initial condition*, shown openly before the round, never a mid-fight swerve.)
- **Quiet frame, loud fight.** The owner's settled taste across every visual round: warm, clean, undistracting chrome; all motion and color budget spent inside the arena. Effects never obscure match state; ridiculousness comes from mechanics, not decoration.
- **Hitboxes are the contract with the viewer.** The audience's trust rests on "what you see is what hits": the drawn silhouette *is* the collision shape, every registered contact is provable on the frame it's shown, and solids never silently pass through solids. Owner, 2026-10-16: "for the viewer perfect hitboxes is the most important." SPINCLASH's **Core contact law** is this principle written as rules; a headless audit re-verifies it after every change. It ranks above visual polish — a beautiful frame that lies about contact is a broken frame.
- **Fundamentals before furniture.** Settle the mechanics contract (what damages, what collides, what is solid) before investing in anything drawn on top of it — owner, 2026-10-16: "we need to get the fundamental mechanics right before going further with the weapons." Weapons get redesigned repeatedly; the contact law they must obey does not. (Distinct from *Structure before flavour*, which is about what cures boredom.)

2. **Parry reward — ANSWERED (2026-10-28, owner: parry should not reward anything; re-confirmed for skills the same day, owner pick "Forbid it — parry rewards nothing, full stop").** Parry stays a pure denial valve: no growth, no position, no tempo — and **no skill may reward a parry either**. Consequence, measured: spin-per-parry was the spin-ceiling entry's likeliest way to wake the dormant `omegaCap: 140`, so the clamp stays asleep on that axis and the remaining growth triggers are damaging hit, time and launch. The **comeback-valve half is NOT answered by this** — if a comeback mechanism is ever wanted it has to come from somewhere other than the parry.
3. **Skill vs weapon-trait model — ANSWERED (2026-10-28, owner ruling verbatim: "M2").** Two languages: a weapon's **trait** is data (a growth rate on the shared axes), a fighter's **skill** is a `CONTRACT.md` **hook** that modifies an existing mechanic and never introduces one. Adopted **lazily** — the two shipped numeric skills stay legal and no plumbing is added until the first non-numeric skill lands. The doctrine, the measured case against M1, the per-axis cost checklist and the five decisions that follow all live in **Fighter skill vs weapon trait — the model** in the SPINCLASH section.
4. **Shield design** — what is a weapon that cannot damage *for*? Current state is a placeholder that stalls mirrors; the balance pass decides (damage-on-parry? shove-only win condition? cut it?). **MEASURED 2026-10-28** (first sanctioned `measure.mjs` run, COMPLETE at 484 of 484 cells): the shield holder won **0 of 569 rounds in either hand** — 308 rounds as Speedy's weapon across 21 cells, 261 as Heavy's across 21 cells (the partial figure was Heavy 0 of 229), and `shield+shield` completed **zero rounds in 8 battles**, all eight running to exactly the 420.0s budget with 0/8 terminated — under KO-only rules it cannot win at all, and because `grow()` fires only on a damaging hit, its `trait: { spin: 0.0, dmg: 0.7 }` **can never activate**, nor can its wielder's fighter skill; both are inert data. It is also the mechanism behind question 1's `shield+shield` non-termination — neither side is capable of a KO, so that cell can only ever exhaust the 420s budget. The balance pass still decides, but now against a number rather than a suspicion. **[AMENDED 2026-11-02, `allcut-r62` — the MECHANISM half is ANSWERED by ruling: the shield cuts on touch like every weapon, so it CAN KO, and its `trait: { spin: 0.0, dmg: 0.7 }` plus its wielder's fighter skill are LIVE (the smoke caught its first-ever grown-damage hits). What a now-damaging tangential wall is FOR stays with the balance pass; the 0-of-569 record above is a pre-r62 fact.]**

**Base damage 5 → 1 across the roster, build `dmg1-r21` (2026-10-28 — owner ruling "dmg base for all is 1, and hp 100 stays the same"; a sanctioned sim-data change and the balance pass's first landing).** The ruling's intent, in the owner's words: a test of whether long uncapped-escalation games are good — "the idea is the game becomes more and more ridiculous with no cap to scaling, and then it end in pure chaos, lets imagine spear geting longer each hit, suddenly it is hilariously long, which is exciting for viewers to watch, this is just a thought we can always change it". The edit is 22 `dmg: 5` fields → `dmg: 1` plus the build stamp (`pause-r20` → `dmg1-r21` in the `<title>`, the `#build` label and one comment cross-reference): the **inverse-diff against the pre-change canonical is EMPTY**, so those 25 lines are the entire change. hp 100, ω 3.5, every growth increment (0.7 / 0.9 / 1.6), all geometry and all pacing dials untouched.
**Measured in this environment (fast tier; the sanctioned `measure.mjs` matrix run remains owed — `measure.mjs` never runs without the owner's go).** (a) **Rounds with a melee damage-dealer got 1.14–1.50× longer:** `cellscan` totals 172,837 → 200,414 ticks (1.16×), worst cell hammer+dagger 122 s → 183 s, parries 311 → 402 (longer rounds, more clangs). (b) **Pure-launcher mirrors stopped terminating:** `projectile-fix`'s recorded termination red went **4/18 → 9/18 battles with no winner in 300 s**, and the failures are exactly the both-sides-ranged cells — **bow+crossbow 3/3, staff+wand 3/3, wand+bow 2/3, boomerang+shuriken 1/3** — while every cell with a melee damage-dealer still ends (staff+hammer: hammer wins 94–143 s; wand+sword: sword wins 84–146 s). `cellscan`'s bow+crossbow cell sits at exactly 50,400 ticks in BOTH builds, i.e. it was already pinned at the harness cap at damage 5: this class was marginal before the ruling and is now solidly stuck. Mechanism (analysis, not measured): both denial channels scale faster than the damage channel — shot-vs-shot cancels grow with the square of the shots in flight and swats grow with the defender's blade speed, while a landing is now worth 1 instead of 5, so a mirror can settle into an equilibrium where HP never drains. (c) **Naturals turned pathological: 0 → 4 of 20 seeds** (15, 34, 37, 40; wall > 20 s or aborted), seed 40 hitting natscan's 420 s cap **with no winner** (at damage 5 it finished in 253 s); natscan wall time 76 s → 227 s. (d) **The chaos the ruling was after did arrive, and its shape is VOLUME, not size:** maxSpin across those four seeds went **23.5 → 103.5 rad/s** (the `omegaCap` is 140), which at the base fire-rate law is **16.5 shots per second**, and maxShots in flight went 5–10 → **15–28**. Sim cost per tick roughly tripled (0.19 → 0.70 ms/tick, maxK 27–34 → **63–68** substeps) without touching the `maxSub 512` brake. For scale: at ω 103.5 a heavy-four tip moves ≈21,600 px/s against a body chaos ceiling of 1,200 — the readability ceiling discussed before the ruling, now reached in natural play. (e) **Attribution — the fingerprint delta is damage-driven, not roll-driven:** `rollattr` over seeds 11–20 gives **identical per-round weapon rolls for 8/10 seeds**, and the two exceptions (13, 15 — both boomerang mirrors) differ only because the battle no longer finishes inside rollattr's 150 s window, so its later rounds are never rolled. Tick columns differ throughout, as expected.

**The length band — floor 54 (the orb), ceiling named for the spear, both ends boot-gated (2026-10-28, balance pass item 2; owner rulings "max length is spear" then "length stays the same, capped at spears length", floor pick 54, and yes to enforcing both ends at boot; no length changed, no fingerprints moved).** Doctrine: every weapon's authored spine sits between **`LEN_MIN` 54** — the orb's len, the shortest weapon shipped, so the floor bans nothing today and exists only to stop a future commission delivering something too short to touch — and the ceiling **`LT`, named for the SPEAR**. The naming is a clarification, not a change: the heavy four (hammer, axe, spear, mace) have been force-equalized to one shared number since 2026-10-21, so the spear sits exactly at the ceiling and nothing exceeds it, and the crossbow (cut down from 116 that day) and the javelin sit at it too. `LT`'s numeric source deliberately stays the **mace's tip, 113.44 pre-scale** (147.5 as played), within **0.06 units** of the spear's authored 113.38 — re-pointing it would be a real sim change (six weapons 0.05% shorter, fingerprints moved, hitbox re-bake) for no gameplay difference, and the ruling was explicit: "length stays the same". The band is **hold-blind by len**, as ruled ("that is for both radial and tangential"): it governs the drawn spine, NOT reach — reach still spreads ~94 px (tome) to ~214 px (hammer) across the two hold classes, because a radial spine adds to the grip offset while a tangential chord is centred on the rim and reaches out only by Pythagoras. That spread is class identity, not a cap violation, and it is the number any future length-growth axis would have to be bounded by (a reach band, when length growth exists).
Implementation: `const LEN_MIN = 54` above the `weaponScale` boot loop plus two loud throws inside it, checked **pre-scale** against `W.len` — the same mechanism as the existing `lead`/`headLead` boot guards. The convention became a gate because the crossbow silently overshot the ceiling in 2026-10-21 and only the owner's eye caught it.
Proofs: the canonical boots clean (chromecheck PASS, inscribe GATE: PASS) and **fingerprints 8/8 BYTE-IDENTICAL** vs `.qa/fp-dmg1-r21.json` — no shipped weapon sits outside the band, so the guard is behaviour-neutral by construction. Both ends were then proven LIVE rather than dead code by staging two throwaway pages (dotted, deleted in the same command): orb `len 40` → `Error: orb: len 40 is under the length floor 54 (the orb — shortest shipped weapon) — STOP`; dagger `len 130` → `Error: dagger: len 130 exceeds the length ceiling LT 113.44 (the spear's length; the heavy four are equalized to it) — STOP`. Canonical md5 `293829002479b4b6e05a856a188d624e` → **`ab17bdf05ab701cd363fad75720482b1`**; no stamp bump (behaviour-identical — the cleanup and rename precedent; the on-screen build stays `dmg1-r21`).
Recorded here because this pass measured it — **the roster's exact reach figures**, computed with the canonical's own `REACH` formula from the shipped polys: hammer 213.6 · axe 212.1 · mace 210.5 · spear 210.4 · scythe 209.4 · katana 209.2 · nunchaku ≈208.6 · flail ≈206.4 (chain weapons use the path bound, so these two are straight-pose lower bounds) · sword 195.5 · staff 193.1 · dagger 164.3 · orb 153.9 · boomerang 144.3 · wand 139.6 · knives 139.3 · bow 131.5 · crossbow 131.5 · shuriken 113.0 · javelin 101.9 · shield 95.9 · scroll 94.1 · tome 94.0 px. Two consequences worth keeping: within the len-equalized heavy four the reach order is set by **head width**, not length (hammer ±47.0 and axe ±54.6 lateral against the spear's ±12.8 point), and **the longest weapons by len are not the longest by reach** — the javelin and crossbow tie for the longest spine (147.5) and sit third- and fifth-from-bottom in reach, while the orb (shortest spine, 70.2) out-reaches nine weapons. That is exactly why the band is on len and any future fairness bound has to be on reach. **Unreconciled, recorded not guessed:** open question 9's "hammer-class reach ≈ 231px as played" does not match the 213.6 computed from the shipped polys; the ~17px gap is unexplained (candidates: the figure predates the 2026-10-21 `REACH` fix, or it quotes a chain weapon's path bound rather than the hammer's). It is quoted in a CONTRACT-compliance context, so it deserves a real reconciliation.
**The authoring-scale pass — weapon defaults, a derived tuck, and the placement/reach rules published (2026-10-28; owner ruling "i want you to do 1 and 2" on the two recommendations that came out of the "wouldn't one shared dimension be easier?" question — the goal being quoted verbatim: "my goal is to make it easier to scale as at one point we are introducing new weapon and if all have similar dimenasion/starting points its a lot easier to design". **Item 2 (code).** `omega: 3.5` and `dmg: 1` were written out on all 22 rows: **44 literals, zero variance**, pure copy-paste that a new weapon's author had to reproduce correctly — a forgotten `omega` reads `undefined` (NaN spin), a stale `5` silently resurrects the pre-2026-10-28 damage build. They are now `const WDEF = { omega: 3.5, dmg: 1 }` spread **first** into every row, so a weapon that ever needs a different rate overrides in place (`{ ...WDEF, name: 'X', omega: 4, … }`). They are POLICY constants, not per-weapon design: uniform spin and base dmg 1 against hp 100 are owner rulings. `tuck: false` joined the derived set the same day — a tangential chord never tucks (its art straddles the rim, so the clip would notch it), which is why all nine tangential rows used to repeat the field; the render pass now reads it off `hold` (`tuck !== false && hold !== 'tangential'`) and the nine declarations are gone, leaving only handle-less **radial** art to opt out by name (the orb). **A new weapon therefore declares just: name, len, hold when tangential, ability, line, shot when it launches, poly.**
Item 2 also corrected a **stale placement claim inside the orb's own comment**: "at weaponScale 1.3 the orb centre orbits ≈ 70px out, its inner edge ≈ 49px vs bodyR 64, so the orb now overlaps the disc by ≈ 15px and draws over it" omits the radial **mount offset** `bodyR × SPINE_R0` = 61.44 px that every radial row's art is drawn from — the same omission that made the reach figures look like they were measured from a centre-drawn weapon. Measured: orb centre **131.6 px** out, inner edge **110.8** vs rim 64 → **46.84 px clear**, nothing overlaps, nothing draws over the disc, and its `tuck: false` is a no-op today (kept as insurance). The comment's advice "raise `len` to ≈ 65 for a just-touching look" also pointed the wrong way — +1 `len` = +1.3 px of orbit, so 65 would widen the gap to ≈ 61 px — which matters now that `len` is floored at 54 and **54 is the orb's value**: bringing the orb closer to the body needs a *mount* rule for handle-less art (a per-weapon mount radius, or mounting detached art from the rim instead of the grip), an owner decision, not a `len` tweak. The owner's playtest words stay verbatim; only the arithmetic is amended, in place, with the date.

**The spin ceiling measured — `omegaCap` 140 is dormant, the real ceiling is structural, and the sim is stable to ω ≈ 258 (2026-10-28, owner pick "measure the real limit first" out of four offered options; read-only, no code changed, canonical byte-identical before and after at `54ab0e5b784962987fdec6cc71cd6636`).** The owner met the item with "what is this ? i dont understand", so the finding is stated plainly: every damaging hit spins the winner faster, nothing in the *game* limits that, but the code carries a hard stop at 140 rad/s purely so the physics cannot tunnel — and the question was how close the game actually gets to it. **Method (three read-only measurements).** (1) *Analytic:* the sim's own substep-sizing rule, `k = ceil((subMargin + Σ(|vel| + ω·REACH))·dt / δ)` with δ = (MINR[a]+MINR[b])/2, clamped to `maxSub` 512 and dt = 1/120, solved per pair for the ω at which required k reaches 512 — all 484 ordered pairs. (2) *Empirical:* a staged copy with `omegaCap: 100000` (`.qa/.uncapped.html`, deleted afterwards; the canonical was never edited for this) run through natscan and projectile-fix and diffed against the capped runs.
(3) *Structural:* per-round accounting of hits, damage and spin on the seeds that peak. **Finding A — the clamp never engages.** With the clamp removed, natscan is **identical on 30/30 seeds** (total ticks 891,003 on both sides, no-winner naturals 33 and 36 on both sides, every maxSpin unchanged) and projectile-fix is **identical across all 18 forced cells** (A 0, B 0/11893 launches off doctrine, C **0/320771** budget-under-provisioned ticks, D 9/18). Nothing in the shipped game reaches 140 rad/s. **Finding B — why: the ceiling is HP, not the clamp.** A round ends when hp 100 is drained, which at base damage 1 is exactly **100 damaging hits**; the fastest spin axis is +1.0/hit (launcher ability 0.70 + Speedy 0.30), so the structural maximum is 3.5 + 100×1.0 = **103.5 rad/s** — precisely the observed peak, on 9 of 30 naturals (seeds 13, 15, 30, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37, 40). Verified per round: the peak rounds are pure-projectile (blade hits [0,0]) with the spinner's maxDmg pinned at 1.00 (Speedy + a launcher never grows damage) while its heavy opponent grew to 10.9–20.2. Reaching 140 needs **137 hits**, i.e.
hp ÷ damage above 137. Melee weapons cannot get close: their ability spin is 0.0, so Speedy + melee tops out at 3.5 + 100×0.30 = 33.5. **Finding C — the true stability limit.** Blade-budget saturation (required k = maxSub 512) across the 484 pairs: worst **axe+axe at ω 257.8** (δ 1.80, REACH sum 424.3), then axe+flail / flail+axe 276.0, hammer+axe / axe+hammer 278.6, axe+spear 288.0; p10 323.8, **median 424.6**, p90 765.8, loosest orb+orb 4346.5 (MINR 21.8 — a sphere has no thin circle). **No pair saturates below ω 140.** The projectile budget at ω 140 peaks at k = 63.3 (a bow shooting at an axe-wielding foe) = **12.4% of maxSub**, so blades bind, not shots. Body velocity is second-order (the ω·REACH term dominates, and `subMargin` 1200 already covers knock/push/bounce impulses); `CFG.cruise` no longer exists — the movement doctrine was reverted 2026-10-21 — and `maxSpeed` is 1200. **Reading of the three findings together.** The 36.5-hit headroom figure recorded earlier the same day was arithmetically right but framed wrong: the binding constraint is hp ÷ damage per hit, and the clamp is *conservative* rather than tight — it bites at 54% of the worst pair's stability limit and about a third of the median's.
**What would wake the clamp** (all skills-pass material): hp above ~137, damage per hit below 1, rounds long enough to land 137+ hits, or — the likely one — **a skill that grows spin without a damaging hit** (spin-per-parry, spin-over-time, spin-per-launch). Waking it would still be silent to the player unless a readout is added, but physics degradation would NOT be silent: `maxSub` engagement is flagged both by the audit (`G.auditK` stores [chosen, blade-required, projectile-required] per tick) and by projectile-fix's check C. **Recommendation recorded, decision left open:** raising 140 today would change nothing (proven dormant) and the measured band says the sim tolerates ~258 at its worst, so the useful trigger for revisiting is the first spin-without-damage skill; a *visible* cap, if the owner wants one for the show, is a legend/render change and not a sim change.

**The skills model ruled — M2, two languages: a weapon's ability is data, a fighter's skill is a hook (2026-10-28, owner ruling verbatim: "M2", picking the model question as the pass's first decision; owner pick the same turn on the parry interaction: "Forbid it — parry rewards nothing, full stop").** Analysis only — **no code changed, no plumbing added, canonical untouched** (md5 `86ff2d5bffc6a3942e6c9eba12ccef09`, build `sigil-r23`, 3083 lines; the doctrine subsection, the two answered open questions and this entry are the whole landing). **The ruling.** Ability = weapon data, a growth rate read at `grow()`; skill = a CONTRACT hook — reads player + small context, returns a modified value, never mutates, never depends on another player's hook, modifies an existing mechanic and never introduces one, may consume the seeded RNG but never create or seed one, leaves time-dependent state to the game's per-tick logic; one skill per player per game. **Adopted lazily by design:** CONTRACT's optionality rule keeps `Speedy {spin: 0.30}` and `Heavy {dmg: 0.9}` legal as shipped, so the hook indirection arrives with the **first non-numeric skill** and not before — the anti-over-engineering path, and the reason this ruling costs nothing today. **What it settles.** Open questions **2 and 3 are ANSWERED in place**: parry rewards nothing and no skill may reward a parry, which removes spin-per-parry (the spin-ceiling measurement's likeliest `omegaCap` waker) and leaves damaging hit / time / launch as the only growth triggers — the latter two contextual, so either forces a real hook. **What it forces.** Since a hook may not introduce a mechanic, poison, frost, comet burn, damage-over-time and runtime length growth are **game-layer** work first and hook targets second; the pass has two layers, and the tome trio's "CONTENT" ruling is partly a game-mechanics decision rather than a skills one. **Measured grounds for M2 over M1** (read out of the canonical, not assumed): `grow()` is the only sim consumer of `.skill`/`.ability`; abilities are binary across all 22 weapons (12 × `{spin: 0, dmg: 0.7}`, 10 × `{spin: 0.70, dmg: 0}`); `SKILL_SHORT` derives its legend label binary-wise, so a both-axes / neither / non-numeric skill is silently mislabelled "+DMG / Hit"; the trackers are exactly `G.maxSpin` + `G.maxDmg` against a fixed three-channel legend; and a shot inherits exactly one per-fighter quantity at birth (`dmg: f.dmg`), with `r`/`speed`/`len`/`turn`/`bounce` reading the weapon row — which is why per-fighter shot axes are the cheap spectacle. **Still open, in gating order:** additive stacking vs override · whether skills are displayed at all · which mechanics are authorized as hook targets (length growth, per-fighter shot multipliers, knock — today a global `CFG.hitKnock` 130) · the spin cap (140, silent, 36.5 hits of headroom at +1.00/hit; stability limit ω ≈ 258) · whether elemental effects enter the game layer in this pass. **Owed alongside, unchanged:** the sanctioned `measure.mjs` run on the owner's machine (`.qa/chainlaw.mjs` FIRST), best run once before and once after this pass — its 19 forced cells miss the dagger and the staff and its expected counts predate both damage-1 and the facing pass — and the kit-route rebuild, which a skill only needs if it touches art.

**The five M2 rulings — stacking adds, skills are shown in the legend, three hook targets authorized, the spin cap left alone, elemental effects into the game layer (2026-10-28, owner answers verbatim: "1. it adds / 2. they are shown in the legend. for instance right now we have weapon name and then the skill, its just a short sentence or few word, for instance with a spear 'gets longer' or something similar. / 3. yes / 4. yes" — item 4 clarified by pick: leave `omegaCap` 140 as it is and revisit when a spin-flavoured skill exists — "/ 5. elemental effects yes, as you pointed out, posions,frost and comet/fire, we will figer it out later").** Analysis only — **no code changed, no plumbing added, canonical untouched** (md5 `86ff2d5bffc6a3942e6c9eba12ccef09`, build `sigil-r23`, 3083 lines): this entry and the doctrine subsection's new "Settled under M2" paragraph are the whole landing. **What each ruling costs.** *(1) Stacking adds* → the numeric site is already correct, so nothing moves until a hook modifies a different mechanic. *(2) Legend labels* → an authoring change, **not** a layout change:
the legend already renders one skill cell per fighter, so `SKILL_SHORT`'s binary derivation is replaced by an authored few-word line and the silent-mislabel defect dies with it; the SPD/DMG numeric cell is untouched, and a new *numeric* axis would still owe the layout change the cost map priced. *(3) Hook targets authorized* (length growth, per-fighter shot multipliers, knock) → game-layer work first, each with its own probe; length growth remains the only axis needing engineering (boot-derived SPAN/REACH/scaled polys/covering circles, the invalidated REACH prune bound and MINR substep budget, and a ceiling that must live inside the growth rule because the LEN_MIN/LT gate cannot catch runtime growth), shot multipliers are one line per axis at the birth site, knock is one hit-time read of a per-fighter field against today's global `CFG.hitKnock` 130. *(4) Spin cap left alone* → no sim change, no kept pair, no re-baseline; the headroom and stability figures in the spin-ceiling entry stand as measured. *(5) Elemental effects authorized into the game layer, design deferred* → poison, frost and comet/fire become game mechanics before any skill can modify them (CONTRACT hook rule 4), shapes to be figured out later; the shot accents already pre-figure them (KF1/KF2 fire comet · KP1/KP2 poison · KN1 frost · KV1/KV2 fire-orange).
**Next:** the skill list for Speedy and Heavy — and whether the cast grows — since the legend labels, the authorized hook targets and the elemental shapes all depend on which skills actually exist. The dagger's axis (⚠ "skills pass decides") is now a cheap *data* ruling under M2: an ability is weapon data, so it is one number and no plumbing. **[RULED 2026-10-28: +0.7 DMG stands — and it cost no code, being the shipped value.]** **Measured correction, caught while grounding the skill list (this entry, row 29 and the doctrine subsection were corrected in place):** the knock field is **`CFG.hitKnock: 130`**, not `CFG.knock` as the skills-prep cost map wrote and these entries repeated — the identifier was wrong, the value and the analysis were not. The same read-out settled a structural fact the skill list turns on: `CFG.hitKnock` has exactly two consumers, `bladeVsBody` (melee) and `shotHitBody` (projectile), so **knock is the only cheap axis that is live on all 22 weapons** — the launch-snapshot axes (`r`/`speed`/`len`/`turn`/`bounce`) are inert on the 12 melee weapons, and runtime length growth is inert on the 10 projectile ones. A skill built on a class-dependent axis is therefore dark for roughly half the roster, which CONTRACT's optionality rule permits (the base value passes through) but the legend label does not: "gets longer" on a bow says nothing true.

**Axis placement ruled — class-dependent axes go on the weapon, universal axes on the fighter, so no legend label can ever be dark (2026-10-28, owner pick: "Design it out — weapons carry class-dependent rates", settling the dark-label fork before any skill was chosen because it constrains the whole list).** Analysis only — **no code changed, no chrome changed, canonical untouched** (md5 `86ff2d5bffc6a3942e6c9eba12ccef09`, build `sigil-r23`, 3083 lines): this entry and the doctrine subsection's new **Axis placement** paragraph, plus a re-key note on ruling 3 so the live doctrine stays coherent, are the whole landing. **The rule.** An axis whose effect depends on weapon **class** is weapon-row **data** — a rate like `ability: {spin, dmg}`, consumed by a game-layer mechanic: the launch-snapshot axes (`r`/`speed`/`len`/`turn`/`bounce`, the 10 projectile weapons) and runtime length growth (the 12 melee ones). A fighter's **skill** takes only what is live on all 22 weapons (spin growth, damage growth, knock) or a class-independent contextual trigger. **Correction, caught on re-read the same turn:** this entry and the doctrine paragraph first listed per-launch as class-independent, which is wrong — only the 10 projectile weapons ever launch a shot, so a launch-triggered fighter skill is dark on the 12 melee ones; the class-independent contextual triggers are per-time and conditional-on-state only — **per-launch is class-dependent** (only the 10 projectile weapons ever launch), so a launch-triggered effect belongs on the weapon row, not on a fighter. **Why it wins.** Weapons are dice-rolled per round, so a fighter's identity must survive the roll; a class-dependent skill flickers on 12/22 or 10/22 of them, while a weapon-keyed rate never does because its line is read only while that weapon is held. **What it buys.** Dark labels become impossible, so the legend needs no conditional wording and no dimmed state — ruling 2's authored few-word skill line is always true and this ruling owes **no chrome work**. Measured support: `CFG.hitKnock` has exactly two consumers (`bladeVsBody`, `shotHitBody`); the shot birth site snapshots `r`/`speed`/`len`/`turn`/`bounce` from `W.shot` and only `dmg` from the fighter; the legend re-renders per frame and already resolves the held weapon; chromecheck asserts legend structure only (`ccard`, `table`, `qn`) and reports byte counts without asserting them. **What it re-keys.** The length-growth spectacle ("gets longer") belongs to the **spear** and any other melee weapon given a length rate, not to a fighter — either fighter gets it when they hold that weapon, and it is still built in this pass. M2 is untouched by this: weapon rates are data, the mechanic is game-layer, only the fighter's skill is a hook. **Rejected with reasons recorded** so the fork is not re-litigated: conditional label wording (free, but dark on half the rolls and unexplained to the audience) and dimming the label while dark (cheap and idiomatic — the legend already carries `class="out"` and `wp idle`/"rolling…" — but unnecessary once no dark label can exist); both stay available if a specific skill is ever judged worth the flicker. **Next:** the skill list — which universal axes and contextual triggers Speedy and Heavy get, and whether the cast grows. The dagger's axis (⚠ "skills pass decides") remains a one-number data ruling. **[DISCHARGED 2026-10-28: +0.7 DMG ratified, no sim change.]**

**The weapon row's `ability` renamed to `trait` — vocabulary only, behaviour-identical (2026-10-28, owner word verbatim: "ok we cahnge it to trait for the weapons", after raising the confusion himself: "we need to get some proper terminology for the 'bot skill' and the 'weapon skill', as i get confused"; his first proposal was fighter = "passive" with the weapon taking "skill" or "ability").** **The ruling as landed: fighter = SKILL (unchanged), weapon = TRAIT (renamed from `ability`), and never the bare nouns in prose — always *fighter skill* / *weapon trait*.** **Why the swap was rejected, with reasons recorded.** (a) `skill` is not a game-local word to move: SPEC's glossary defines it — "What makes a player behave differently. A set of optional, passive **hooks** into one game's mechanics … Exactly one skill per player per game" — and CONTRACT §Skills carries it across every future game and the Phase 8 player pool, so giving it to the weapon would make the platform's term mean two things in one repo. (b) "passive" cannot discriminate here: SPINCLASH has **no player input at all** — both combatants are bots and every mechanic is automatic — so the weapon's rate is exactly as passive as the fighter's, and the word is already spent as the adjective inside SPEC's own definition ("optional, passive hooks").
(c) The confusion was legitimate and baked in: "skill" and "ability" are near-synonyms in ordinary game vocabulary, and the live Core contact law already carried the collision — one clause read "Future weapon skills" while the next reached for "a named, documented weapon trait". That clause is now "Future weapon traits"; the owner's own 2026-10-16 quote beside it ("special weapon skills") stays verbatim as his words. **Scope, measured.** Canonical: **30** word-boundary sites — 22 weapon rows, 1 inline comment ("axe ability"), 5 block comments, and 2 code sites (`grow()`'s `WEAPONS[f.weapon].ability` and the legend `brief` derivation `W.ability.spin`) — plus a 10-line VOCABULARY comment above `WDEF` recording the rename and its discipline. `uploads/ingest.mjs`: **1** site, the dormant SVG gate's emitted row template — **a coupling that would have silently produced a traitless weapon** on any future ingest, since `WDEF` defaults only `{omega, dmg}`. Docs: 26 occurrences across GAMES.md's live regions (roster table header, the reveal-poster and legend doctrine, the growth/spin doctrine, the M2 subsection, open questions 1 and 3, the vocabulary map, the testing recipe's ingest caveat) and 2 in SPEC.md's frame description.

**The length-growth coverage probe — the ladder is safe BECAUSE it is pre-baked, and the runtime-stretch shortcut is now refuted by measurement (2026-10-28; owner pick via ask_user: "start with the coverage probe"; the two routing questions that followed were both delegated — "do what you think is best" and "again whatever you think is best". No sim line moved: canonical md5 `a217471e2f6a93d5f6e5037abe088d7d`, build `cross-r24`, 3,102 lines, no fingerprint disturbed. The probe is read-only, writes nothing, runs no battles and never invokes `measure.mjs`.)**
*(1) The instrument.* `.qa/lengrow-proof.mjs`, **274 lines, md5 `218f4f84da1f6d699e8dbbb3902279be`**, runs in ~3s. It loads the canonical through the house `leadproof.mjs` loader, rebuilds the spear's runtime poly (**5 drawn shapes, 19 covering circles, runtime len 147.47**) and sweeps the stretch factor `k`. Two metrics: `eps(k)`, the house sliver metric defined exactly as `ingest.mjs` :462-469 defines it; and `touch(k)`, the deepest a body disc (`CFG.bodyR` 64) can overlap the drawn silhouette while missing **every** covering circle — the "gap hit" the owner made top priority on 2026-10-19 (*"they dont wanna see these 'gap' hits"*), and what law 1 looks like from the viewer's seat.
*(2) The threshold this probe started from was the wrong one, and only measurement showed it.* The 3px ink outline is **not** a usable criterion here: the shipped spear **already** carries a **2.97px** uncovered tip protrusion, leaving **0.03px** of headroom, so "does it cross the ink?" is answered *yes* at k=1.0001 and carries no information. The honest criterion is the **delta versus the shipped weapon**. The sweep's `verdict` column still labels against the absolute ink, for continuity with the 2026-10-19 priority — it must be read against the baseline row, not against 3px, and the file now says so in its own header.
*(3) The measurement.* `eps` / `touch` / Δtouch-vs-shipped: **k=1.0 → 2.00 / 2.92 / — (SHIPPED BASELINE, already a gap hit)** · k=1.0489 (+4.9%) → 2.57 / 3.18 / +0.26 · k=1.10 (+10.0%) → 2.82 / 3.42 / +0.50 · **k=1.1539 (+15.4%, the design point) → 2.68 / 3.78 / +0.86** · k=1.186 (+18.6%, the spine-line proxy limit) → 3.13 / 3.92 / +1.06 · k=1.25 → +1.42 · k=1.40 (+40%) → 5.17 / +2.25. Degradation is **~0.07px per ladder step**, monotonic and unbounded in `k`.
*(4) The mechanism is derived, not merely observed.* Under a `d`-only stretch that **holds `r`**, the art tip outruns the circle that was packed to cover it, and the protrusion grows in closed form: **`protrusion(k) = (tipD − lastD)·k − lastR`**. With art tip `d` 147.47 and outermost circle `d` 141.8 `r` 2.7 that is **`5.67k − 2.7`** → 2.972px at k=1 (measured 2.92) and **3.845px at the design point (measured 3.78)**; the 0.07px residual is the 1px candidate grid. Corroborated independently by the `touch@` column, whose deepest gap hit marches outward along the spine from x=208 to x=230 across the sweep. **The entire degradation is the tip** — nothing else in the silhouette loses coverage.
*(5) Verdict: PASS for the recorded design, FAIL for the shortcut.* The **pre-baked ladder is safe**: `ingest.mjs` packs circles against *each step's own* stretched silhouette, so the tip circle is resized per step and the protrusion stays at the shipped ~3.0px — **zero degradation across all 12 steps**. A **runtime `d`-stretch is not viable**: +0.86px at the design point, growing without bound. This is the number that justifies baking twelve coverings instead of stretching one polygon, and it upgrades the design note *"Pre-baked ladder, not a runtime stretch"* from an invariant argument (a `d`-only stretch is not uniform, so it cannot inherit *"a uniform scale of an inscribed covering stays inscribed"*, :462-463) to a **measured** one.
*(6) One disclosed conservatism.* `eps` here is computed on the **plain even-odd interior** of every sub-polygon — `ingest.mjs`'s own `covers()` test for `type === 'poly'` — rather than on ingest's inflated grid-and-narrow-column-fill solid. This probe's solid is therefore a **subset** of ingest's, so its `eps` can only **under-report** a hole that ingest would catch. That is valid for the `k`-sweep because the identical definition is used at every `k`, and the sweep is the design input; `touch` is unaffected, being measured against the drawn silhouette. The ladder's top step still owes a real `ingest.mjs` bake, which will supersede this interior.
*(7) A process defect in producing this entry, disclosed.* A `write_file` of a rewritten probe **returned success and did not land**; the run whose numbers are recorded above was executed by the **previous 263-line version**. Detected from three formatting markers in its output that only the old file produces (`bodyR 64` rather than `64px`, the shape/circle-count line, and bracketed coordinates). No number changed — the older body is the better-documented one, and its conservatism is exactly point (6) — but the new verdict block had been patched onto a body that had not been re-read, so the body was then read, every identifier the verdict uses was confirmed present, and the file was re-run end to end with `node --check`. Standing lesson reconfirmed: **a tool reporting success is not the file saying so.**
*(8) Where this leaves the build.* Step 3 (the **minimal spear-only** build the owner scoped: `f.lenStep` plus its per-round reset, the ladder, `bladeCircles`/`spineFrame`/renderer, and `grow()` applying the rate — with `REACH` and `MINR` left as per-weapon tables and the substep budget's slight under-budgeting of a grown spear disclosed rather than fixed) is **unblocked**, and its geometry route is now fixed by measurement rather than by preference: **each of the twelve steps must be baked.** Owed before the ladder ships: that real `ingest.mjs` bake of the top step.

**The resolver's inverted stall test fixed, with the two comments it had falsified — landed alone as `stall-r25`, and it is NOT behaviour-neutral (2026-10-28; this is step 2 of the skills-pass order the owner picked — probe → resolver fix landed alone → length-growth build — with both routing questions delegated, "do what you think is best" and "again whatever you think is best". Canonical md5 `a217471e2f6a93d5f6e5037abe088d7d` → **`cd5f4de10e15c35fc4e97ac579f47673`**, build `cross-r24` → **`stall-r25`**, line count **held at 3,102**. The pre-edit file was backed up outside the workspace before the first stroke.)**
*(1) The defect, verified in source before the edit rather than from the earlier diagnosis.* `deep ≤ 0`, more negative being deeper, so **progress is `deep` RISING toward 0**. At :1708 the test read `if (deep - gapPrev > -0.02)`, and TRUE is the branch that either nudges-and-continues or breaks at :1729. That expression is true on large progress and on mild regression, and false only when penetration regresses by more than 0.02px — so the loop **declared a stall exactly when it was converging**, and always exited after two passes (one, plus one after the nudge). The corrected `< 0.02` makes pass 1 fall through to :1731 on real progress, nudge on the genuine stall at pass 2, and break at pass 3. That reproduces the "2 passes vs 3 passes" the `--band-dump` diagnosis had already measured on the worst-case pose, so the mechanism is confirmed twice by independent routes.

*(11) An instrument defect found while proving this landing: `chromecheck.mjs`'s byte counts are NOT reproducible, and only its PASS/FAIL is meaningful.* During verification its reported `legend=` length moved **806B → 821B** between two runs, which looked like a user-visible regression from the sign fix. It is not. Isolating stamp-vs-sign gave the opposite ordering (pre-edit 830B, stamp-only 822B, final 807B), and five consecutive runs of the **same byte-identical file** (md5 re-verified before the loop) gave **810, 823, 810, 809, 806** — a 17-byte spread, wider than the delta being investigated. Cause: canonical **:2275**, `let seed = 1 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 1e5)` in the app-state section, which `chromecheck.mjs` **does not stub** (it stubs `performance.now` to 0 and drives `requestAnimationFrame` with synthetic timestamps, but leaves `Math.random` live). Each run therefore rolls a different matchup, and the legend's weapon cards render different names. The **sim is unaffected** — :96 declares *"SIM — pure. No DOM, no Math.random, no Date/performance below this line until the RENDERER section"*, the RENDERER banner is at **:2000-2001**, and :2275 sits inside it, i.e. outside the pure-sim region by design; `fingerprint.mjs` also passes explicit seeds, which is why the fingerprints are stable to the byte while this one diagnostic wanders. **Standing rule from this: never use `chromecheck`'s `bug=`/`legend=` byte counts as a change detector; run it for its assertions.** All five runs of the final build PASSed, and the **pre-edit content PASSed 3/3 as well, at 820 / 842 / 835B** — a range that *overlaps* the final build's 806-823B, so the two builds are indistinguishable on this metric, which is precisely why it proves nothing. `bug=219B` was stable across every run of both; only the legend wanders, because only the legend renders the rolled weapon names. A fix was considered and **deliberately not built**: pinning the seed would make the counts reproducible but freeze `chromecheck` onto one matchup forever, trading away the random-coverage it currently gets for free. The cheap correct version is a printed `--seed` (default random, reproducible on demand), which is a QA-tool change with no bearing on this landing and is recorded as an option rather than an owed item.

*(1) Why a rate change alone could not deliver it, measured before the number was offered.* With the covering held — radii untouched, spacing scaled by the rigid map — `.qa/lengrow-gate.mjs --mode rigid` last passes at shaft **k 1.6469 = tip +39.5%** (miss 4.59 of the 4.60 band) and fails at **+40%** (4.61). *(2) The route taken: re-bake with the house packer, so no new algorithm enters the sim.* Two mechanisms could pass +39.5% — densify the covering at boot (interpolate circles where the remapped spacing outruns the held radii) or re-pack each step offline. The second was chosen because it reuses the **sanctioned** packer: `.qa/lengrow-bake.mjs` drives `.qa/bake-rows.mjs` → `inscribe.mjs`'s raster-EDT greedy union-inscribed regen, the same code that baked all 22 shipped rows. *(3) Art and circles agree, and here is the argument rather than the assertion.* The stretch is injected **post-normalisation and pre-weaponScale** during the bake, while the boot ladder maps the **booted** (post-weaponScale) polys. Those coincide exactly because the rigid map is homogeneous of degree 1 in (d, J): with `J = maxD * lenJ` in both spaces and `maxD_boot = 1.3 * maxD_ingr`, `map(1.3d) = 1.3*map(d)`. So a row baked against the stretched INGR art *is* a row for the stretched booted art. Verified from the live boot rather than trusted: the ladder's step-s circles are the baked objects **by identity**, step 0 is still the shipped row and shipped polys by identity, and `bladeCircles` at step 7 emits exactly 36 circles whose radii match `LEN_LADDER.circles[7]` element for element.

*(8) The 50-cell balance sweep, and the hole it found in `lengrow-r27`.* Same harness, same ten opponents (hammer, sword, scythe, axe, mace, katana, dagger, shield, flail, staff) × seeds 1-5, forced spear in slot 0, run against **both** builds. **Spear win rate: 3 of 50 (6%) at +35%, 33 of 50 (66%) at +200%.** The 484-cell baseline recorded the spear's holder win rate as **65.9%** when its `dmg` was 0.7 — so tripling the length has put the spear back at roughly its historical strength at `dmg` 0.3, while +35% had left it **the weakest weapon in the game**. The `dmg` 0.7 → 0.3 cut and the growth rate are therefore **coupled**, and `lengrow-r27` shipped an under-powered spear that nothing in the house suite could see. *Two honesty limits on that comparison:* the 65.9% figure comes from the full 484-cell natural matrix under `measure.mjs`, whereas this is 50 forced cells at 5 seeds, so the agreement is suggestive rather than exact; and the sweep's "growth OFF" control zeroes `trait.len` while leaving `dmg` at 0.3, which is a **crippled** spear (it wins **0 of 50** on both builds) — so ON-vs-OFF deltas conflate growth with the damage cut and must not be read as the value of growth alone. The r27-vs-r28 ON comparison is the clean one.
*(9) Stalls went DOWN, and the small-sample scare that said otherwise.* Undecided at the 18,000-tick budget: **+35% → 18/50 (36%)**, **+200% → 14/50 (28%)**. Three cells is not a sample; fifty says the opposite. The lesson is the one already on record from the proof-slice bias — a differential proves *divergence*, and must not be read as a *trend*.
*(10) A boot guard, so the ceiling cannot be exceeded silently.* `LEN_REMAP_CEIL = 1.395` is the swept +39.5% wall, and the ladder builder now **throws at boot** if a growing weapon's top step exceeds it without baked rows, and throws if `LEN_CIRCLES` carries any number of rows other than `LEN_STEPS`. The failure mode being guarded is a silent gap hit — the one thing the owner made top priority — so it is worth a hard stop rather than a comment. `.qa/lengrow-bake.mjs` reads `trait.len`, `lenJ` and `LEN_STEPS` **out of the canonical**, so the baked rows cannot drift from the row that consumes them, and it names the **build stamp** rather than a date in its provenance line because this sandbox's clock runs ahead of the owner's local date (a recorded trap) and would otherwise bake a wrong day into the file.
*(11) Disclosures. (a)* The step count was delegated and stays **12**: the ceiling bounds *total* growth, so more steps at 9.6% would need re-baking anyway, and 24 would halve the per-hit drama and double the baked data; 6 would plateau at hit 6 and stop being a snowball. *(b)* The substep budget is now computed from `REACH` 505.488 for the spear, **2.40× base**, so spear battles cost more substeps than they did — unmeasured in wall-clock terms here, and the 484-cell re-run will show it. *(c)* `POPC`'s pop-in centre is still not remapped: cosmetic, and pop-in happens at round start where `lenStep` is 0. *(d)* A grown spear's tip reaches **505px** from the body centre in a 1000px arena, so from mid-arena it touches the wall and the art will overhang the rim — nothing clips it, and at +300/+400% it would extend past the arena entirely. That is a look decision, not a correctness one, and it is now the owner's to call. *(e)* `.qa/lengrow-gate.mjs` and `.qa/lengrow-proof.mjs` still default to a `rate` that tracks the row, but their **remap** measurements no longer describe the shipped ladder past +39.5%.

Current state and "Next" are updated, and the standing-baseline paragraph records the third no-move. New tool **`.qa/lengrow-bake.mjs`** (dry run / `--verify` / `--write`, marker-delimited splice that preserves every other byte; verified: only the 22-line block changed on re-run). `.qa` goes 10 → **11 files**, workspace 28 → **29**. `scratch/docreflow.mjs` FIRST, then `scratch/navgen.mjs` (46 → 47 entries).

**The first special skill — `skill-r29`: a fighter's skill raises the spear's growth cap from 12 steps to 18, and the carrier was chosen by measurement (2026-10-28; owner picked "C2 then C3 staged", then rejected C2 outright with *"i dont like this at all, each round weapons traits should reset"*, then picked cap 18 from a measured menu and deferred the carrier to *"decide after I see it"*. Canonical md5 `4d0467dc5faafeb4480a72e2dcbbd8e5` → **`11f87c88b2bb091988fd0c34abdac298`**, 3,279 → **3,332 lines**, stamp `lengrow-r28` → **`skill-r29`**.)**
**[RETIRED at `nocombo-r34`, 2026-10-31 — the owner's NO COMBOS ruling (see "Fighter skill vs weapon trait"): `skill.lenSteps` is deleted from the row and from the sim, every cap is uniform at `LEN_STEPS` 12, the six carrier-era rows (steps 13–18) are purged from `LEN_CIRCLES`, `REACH.spear` returns to 505.488, and Speedy's label returns to '+SPD / Hit'.
