<script>
(function () {
  'use strict';

  /* =====================================================================
   * SIM — pure. No DOM, no Math.random, no Date/performance below this
   * line until the RENDERER section. Harness-extractable per BUILD.md:
   * newGame / tick + CFG / FIGHTERS / WEAPONS at this scope.
   * Arena boundary: circle, locked (owner decision 2026-10-15).
   * ===================================================================== */

  const CFG = {
    tickHz: 120,
    size: 1000,            // arena bounds (the platform's fixed square)
    gravity: 1400,         // floaty but lively: big slow arcs, still enough contact (owner: bounce more, not faster). 2026-10-21 feel tune at owner word ("increase the bounce a little bit"): 1500 → 1400 — the same launch speeds now bounce ~7% higher and hang ~4% longer (rise = v²/2g) with no speed increase; this is the lever that cannot strangle (raising floorMinBounce instead would collide with the temporary cap or demand a faster one)
    wallRest: 0.9,         // walls absorb 10% of the normal component per contact (owner option 1, 2026-10-21, from the measured menu): the bleed that keeps the horizontal ratchet from filling the new ceiling's headroom — cap 1200 alone measured p50 807 / 13.2% of ticks above 1100; with the bleed, p50 766 / 9.9%. Doctrine amendment: walls are no longer perfectly elastic — the trampoline floor stays the only energy source, and shot that eats a little also reads physically; top/side bounces are slightly softer than the old perfect elasticity
    floorMinBounce: 1050,  // trampoline floor: every floor touch sends bots back toward mid-arena
    bodyR: 64,
    hp: 100,
    launchSpeed: 430,
    maxSpeed: 1200,        // chaos ceiling (owner option 1, 2026-10-21, from the measured menu; was the TEMPORARY observer cap 1100, owner: "so i can watch it easier"): raised so aligned stacks (a floor launch met by a vertical parry shove or knock from mid-arena) can reach the upper rim — the highlight the owner asked for ("i feel like i want to see more but not exaggerating scenarios where bots touch the upper rim … too much of it is boring"). Measured at birth: top-rim touches 0.95 → 3.05 per battle (spread 0–9, so clean battles stay clean), pace p50 743 → 766 (+3%), p90 1098 ≈ the old cap — the fast tail feels like yesterday's maximum. The cap-1600 version of this experiment was rejected same-day ("its going a bit too fast for the eye to understand now": 40 top touches/battle, p50 1053). Balance-pass verdict on the number stays open; must stay above floorMinBounce or bounces get strangled
    hitKnock: 130,
    parryPush: 700,        // parry-loop fix, option 1 (owner decision 2026-10-19: "1"): 150 was a nudge too weak to end a point-blank episode — blades re-touched every latch reset and machine-gunned parries in the bottom-centre cradle. 3.5x separates the pair decisively on one parry. Tunable dial; direction stays the body-centre line per law. Raised 525 -> 700 at owner word 2026-10-21 ("maybe make a bit more seperation on parry … as natural and smooth transition as possible"): harder shoves end grapples before wedges form (fewer pins, fewer nudges) and mask the residual nudge inside the clang's separation motion. Velocity impulse — smooth by construction, no teleport class
    nudgePx: 12,           // pin-escape nudge cap in px-at-the-weapon-head (nz <= nudgePx / REACH), gated to ONE add per tick per fighter (owner 2026-10-21): the old uncapped one-substep teleport read as a ~36px one-frame warp on long weapons; the cap+gate spread the escape over ~3-12 ticks at <=6px-head per drawn frame — a smooth sweep whose buried depth stays sub-ink (<=2-3px) while it lasts. No pending ledger, no drain: adds happen only on stalled substeps, so nothing feeds a grapple (the whip's failure mode)
    parryPad: 4,           // blade-vs-blade hysteresis margin: parry fires at exact touch (gap <= 0); a sustained press counts once until the blades clear this
    parryCarryKill: 0.65,  // carry-kill at the clang (owner k-pick 2026-10-27, eyes-first, numbers owed): at the parry tick both bodies' existing velocity is scaled by (1 - this) BEFORE the shove is added, so the clang absorbs most of the flight and the post-clang motion is shove + reversed orbit — the recoil becomes visible on the head's screen path at the clang instead of being masked by body carry (the 99797 axe case: rim-bounce carry outvoted the reversed orbit for ~1s). Magnitude-only, same law every clang, open-space flight untouched (applies only at the parry tick)
    clinchRamp: 48,        // clinch spring (owner pick 1 of the bind-prevention menu, 2026-10-27, eyes-first, numbers owed): ticks for the sustained-clash separation force to ramp zero->full while the blade latch stays shut (blades inside the pad); smoothstep-shaped, so the onset has no jerk
    clinchDecay: 3,        // ramp-ticks shed per tick once the blades clear the pad (48 -> 0 in 16 ticks, ~0.13s): the push fades out smoothly, never switches off
    clinchAcc: 2200,       // px/s^2 peak separation acceleration at full ramp: holding the bind ~0.3s past full ramp adds a parryPush-worth of velocity, spread over time instead of one impulse; the chaos ceiling caps the result like any velocity
    clinchFloor: 1500,     // bindfix-r35 (owner go 2026-10-31, seed-32542 crossbow×staff bind): the separation acceleration FLOOR while the blade latch is shut. The smoothstep ramp alone starts near zero and only overtakes the press that holds a vertical/rim stack (gravity 1400 plus the resolver/body cycle re-pressing each tick) at clinchT ~31 of 48 — the first ~25 ticks of such a bind read as a dead lock (owner: "looks very ugly and bad, and should not be possible"). With the floor, a bind pushes itself apart from its FIRST tick at >=1500 px/s^2; mature binds (sm -> 1, 2200) are untouched, and the decay after release stays pure ramp so the push still fades smoothly. Chosen by a four-variant sweep (none / floor / floor+torque-latched nudge / floor+spin-aligned nudge) over 12 forced crossbow+staff cells + 20 naturals: the floor ALONE cleared the owner's seed but introduced 247-596 tick open-space cross-tracking monsters; paired with the spin-aligned nudge (see the pin-escape comment in bladeVsBlade) every monster dies and only mild 48-69t residues remain (one of them an axe×flail chain wrap, a different texture, pre-existing)
    parryGate: 16,         // law 2's flutter gate (owner option 1, 2026-10-21): after a parry fires, the latch cannot re-arm for this many ticks even if the blades clear parryPad — contacts inside the gate stay fully solid (resolver + approach-velocity kill) but fire no parry, collapsing the 4-clang vibrato bursts into clang-bind-separate; measured re-parry gaps are bimodal (flutter <=16 ticks, legit p10 81), so 16 cuts clean
    reArmPad: 12,          // blade must clear body by this to hit again
    reArmDeep: 85,         // px of peak clearance that counts as a genuine disengagement — the DEEP-DISENGAGE GATE (law 4's re-arm-side sanctioned extension, owner option 1 2026-10-23 "do 1", from the seed-24267 thrash volley: a javelin left and re-entered the body 3× in 95 ticks — three fresh LEGAL hits whose HP/flash stutter "looks very ugly"). Re-arm now needs clear > reArmPad AND (peak clearance since the latch >= reArmDeep OR >= reArmWait ticks since it). Calibrated 48 at first from the naturals' thrash class (684 consecutive same-attacker blade-hit pairs over 40 naturals: 662 genuine re-hits cleared >=80px, interval median 394 ticks; the 4-pair class sat <=21px at 13–28 ticks) — but the gatecheck reconstruction (substep truth off auditSubs) showed the owner's episode ITSELF rocks the middle band: true peaks 69–79px, every re-arm out the deep branch ~5 ticks after the hit, round 1 byte-identical. The threshold therefore sits ABOVE the middle band: at 85 the episode's first two re-hits fall to the wait branch (hits 95/114 ticks apart — distinct pokes), at proven zero cost — the [80,85) band is empty at both thresholds, middle-band fast pairs (48–80px, interval <90t) went 8 → 0, and every surviving <90t pair clears >=91px (genuine fast exchanges, kept by design; knock already forces 696/701 natural re-hits past 120px). The gate rides the LATCH (bladeStuck) — the knock-only contacts of the projectile-rule era (retired at allcut-r62; every touch cuts now) obeyed identically — and solidity is untouched: the resolver still runs every substep — this gates EVENTS only, exactly like law 2's parryGate. Pinned/hovering fights now poke at the reArmWait cadence instead of buzzing (rework-window material, recorded not judged). Birth records: scratch/thrashdiag.mjs (population) + scratch/gatecheck.mjs (episode reconstruction + threshold proof, numbers in scratch/gatecheck-partB.txt)

  const FIGHTERS = [

     * languages). spin/dmg are additive numbers applied on every damaging hit; they STACK with the
     * held weapon's trait on the same axis (Speedy + staff = +1.00 spin/hit). `short` is the
     * AUTHORED legend label (owner ruling: authored, never derived).
     * NO COMBOS (owner ruling 2026-10-31, retiring `skill.lenSteps` at nocombo-r34): a skill and a
     * trait may meet ONLY by adding on a shared axis — neither reaches into the other's mechanic.

     * identity survives the dice roll by construction. The carrier measurement that picked Speedy
     * for lenSteps survives in GAMES.md as history, and one lesson from it stays live: any
     * damage-coupled growth is self-limiting, because the holder's own damage sets the hit budget. */

  /* ---- v1.0 poly builder: shapes -> drawn polys + covering circles ----
   * Weapons below are authored as plain polygons in spine-local (d, l)
   * units, pre-weaponScale. The covering circles (the hitbox) are the baked
   * CIRCLES_V2 under the weaponScale loop — union-inscribed in THESE polys'
   * drawn ink by .qa/inscribe.mjs --regen and permanently gated by the same
   * script (owner directive 2026-10-19: events only on visible contact). The
   * old runtime cover() packer is gone: its 1.2u margin did not survive the
   * x1.3 weaponScale (+0.1..0.26px poke) and its min-r-4 floor left whole
   * strips and tips uncovered (misses to 13.1px). Shapes flagged vis are
   * paint only (the flag was unreachable until 2026-10-28 — build() now
   * passes it through; see build() and the sigil-legibility block). */
  const KW = '#7a4a2a', KS = '#8fa3b5', KP = '#eaf6ff', KD = '#4f3220', KG = '#d4a73a', KB = '#9fe0ff';
  const KC = '@carrier';   // SIGIL slot (owner decision 2026-10-23 — the carrier-mark doctrine: exactly ONE diegetic element per weapon wears the wielding fighter's cast color; recolor-first, never on KP, interior-ink preferred). NOT a real paint: a KC-tagged shape renders in COLS[carrier] through drawWeapon's swap (falling back to KG for callers with no carrier, like the contact-sheet tool) — and as an invalid CSS color it fails visibly if ever drawn unswapped.
  function build(shapes) {
    const polys = [];
    /* 2026-10-22 (flail): sh[1] may also be a LIST of rings [outer, hole...] — open chain links need a real hole (drawn evenodd). A plain point list behaves exactly as before. */
    /* 2026-10-28 (sigil legibility): sh[2] is an optional `vis` flag. Until now build() dropped it, so the
     * `vis` branches in drawPolySet (paint-only / blink parity / pulse) were documented but UNREACHABLE —
     * no shape in the file could carry the flag. The spell-family ink plate is the first user (vis 1 =
     * paint only, no ink stroke). Existing shapes pass undefined, so nothing else changes. */
    for (const sh of shapes) polys.push({ subs: Array.isArray(sh[1][0][0]) ? sh[1] : [sh[1]], fill: sh[0], vis: sh[2] });
    return { polys, circles: [] };   // the covering circles live in CIRCLES_V2 (baked, world px, after the weaponScale loop)
  }

   *     proofs. The spear's trait.len is the only one so far and is why the ladder exists.
   *
   * WHAT DOES NOT EXIST — so you do not go looking for it, or invent it twice:
   *   - NO COMBOS (owner ruling 2026-10-31): a skill and a trait may stack ONLY by adding on a
   *     shared axis; neither reaches into the other's mechanic. No per-fighter caps, no
   *     per-fighter ladders, no weapon-specific skill effects — one bot's weapon may never
   *     behave differently from anyone else's. `skill.lenSteps` is the cautionary tale.
   *   - ONE trigger. Every axis fires on "damaging hit" inside grow(). A trait that fires at
   *     another moment needs a NEW consumer site at that moment. Do NOT build a general hook or
   *     plugin framework for it (owner: allergic to over-engineering); add the seam when a trait
   *     needs it, the way shot.mult was added.
   *   - emit() is an APPEND-ONLY log (kinds: battleWin, bounce, hit, ko, parry, roll,

   *     list had rotted before bouncegrow-r40 completed it)

   *   - KNOCK has no seam. There is no CFG.knock; knock is applied diffusely at shot landings,

   *     become a row field.
   *   - PAIRING EXISTS (pair-r31): `newGame(seed, { cast: [i, j] })` picks which two cast members
   *     play, so a bigger CAST is now a row edit + a colour, not a structural one. `f.slot` is the

   *     them. Still 1v1: SPAWN, COLS, TINTS, view/flashV/flipAnim and C0/C1 all hold exactly two
   *     entries, and `1 - f.slot` names the foe. A 3-way brawl remains a structural change.
   *   - There is NO cast-selection UI. `APP.setCast([i, j])` is the lever (console-only by design
   *     while the cast is two); the shipped pairing is DEFAULT_CAST.

const WEAPON_IDS = ['bow', 'hammer', 'dagger', 'axe', 'sword', 'spear', 'mace', 'shield', 'staff', 'wand', 'crossbow', 'boomerang', 'shuriken', 'flail', 'nunchaku', 'scythe', 'katana', 'knives', 'javelin', 'tome', 'scroll', 'orb'];

  /* apply weaponScale once, at boot, to the data every consumer reads:
   * lengths, poly coordinates, and projectile radii / launch offsets / drawn
   * lengths (so the drawn disc still equals the launched hitbox). The
   * covering circles are NOT scaled here — CIRCLES_V2 is baked in world px
   * and assigned below (move this dial => re-run inscribe --regen).
   * Supersedes the round-2 frozen-lengths rule by owner decision. */
  /* The length band's floor (owner ruling 2026-10-28): the orb's authored len,
   * the shortest weapon shipped. Guarded inside the loop below. */
  const LEN_MIN = 54;
  for (const id of WEAPON_IDS) {
    const W = WEAPONS[id], S = CFG.weaponScale;
    /* Edge-leading guards (owner decision 2026-10-22): `lead` is ±1 — the
     * spine-local side bearing the cutting face, which the placement layer
     * keeps facing the motion by mirroring art+hitbox together on spin sign.
     * Chain weapons are FORBIDDEN from declaring it (the tie/articulation ×
     * mirror interaction is unproven — loud throw until a real case exists). */
    if (W.lead !== undefined && W.lead !== 1 && W.lead !== -1) throw new Error(`${id}: lead must be 1 or -1 (the spine-local side that leads the motion), got ${W.lead}`);
    if (W.lead !== undefined && W.chain) throw new Error(`${id}: chain weapons cannot declare lead (mirror × chain articulation unproven — boot guard)`);
    /* headLead guards (owner 2026-10-22, the javelin's along-chord flip): ±1 only;
     * TANGENTIAL only — the d-mirror pivots about the chord's centred rim grip,
     * its fixed point (a radial grip at d 0 would slide off the body); never
     * together with lead (one flip factor drives one declared axis — the
     * combination is unproven, loud throw until a real case exists); never on
     * chains (same reason as lead). */
    if (W.headLead !== undefined && W.headLead !== 1 && W.headLead !== -1) throw new Error(`${id}: headLead must be 1 or -1 (the chord end bearing the head), got ${W.headLead}`);
    if (W.headLead !== undefined && W.hold !== 'tangential') throw new Error(`${id}: headLead requires a tangential hold (the d-mirror pivots about the centred rim grip)`);
    if (W.headLead !== undefined && (W.lead !== undefined || W.chain)) throw new Error(`${id}: headLead cannot combine with lead or chain (one flip factor, one axis — boot guard)`);
    /* Length band (owner ruling 2026-10-28, balance pass item 2): every authored
     * spine sits between LEN_MIN (the orb, 54) and the ceiling LT — named for the
     * SPEAR, "capped at spears length". Checked PRE-scale, before the weaponScale
     * multiplication below. The floor bans nothing today; it only stops a future
     * commission delivering something too short to touch. Hold-blind by design
     * (owner: "that is for both radial and tangential") — the band governs the
     * DRAWN SPINE, not reach, which still spreads ~94-214px across the two hold
     * classes as class identity. Convention turned into a gate because the
     * crossbow silently overshot the ceiling in 2026-10-21 and only the owner's
     * eye caught it. Zero behaviour change: every shipped weapon is inside the
     * band, so the fingerprints must not move. */
    if (W.len < LEN_MIN) throw new Error(`${id}: len ${W.len} is under the length floor ${LEN_MIN} (the orb — shortest shipped weapon) — STOP`);
    if (W.len > LT + 1e-9) throw new Error(`${id}: len ${W.len} exceeds the length ceiling LT ${LT.toFixed(2)} (the spear's length; the heavy four are equalized to it) — STOP`);
    W.len *= S;
    if (W.shot) { W.shot.r *= S; if (W.shot.off) W.shot.off *= S; if (W.shot.len) W.shot.len *= S; }
    for (const pl of W.poly.polys) for (const pts of pl.subs) for (const pt of pts) { pt[0] *= S; pt[1] *= S; }
  }

Cap 3: the f.fl state and the FL/CF scratch are fixed-size (loud throw, never a silent truncation)
    if (ch.np < 1 || ch.np > 3) throw new Error(`${id} chain: np ${ch.np} outside 1..3 (fixed-size chain-state cap)`);
    if (ch.segs.length !== ch.j.length) throw new Error(`${id} chain: segs ${ch.segs.length} vs joints ${ch.j.length} (segments must equal j.length = np + 1)`);
    ch.dj = [0];                                                  // spine-local d of each segment's hinge (S0: the spine origin; S_k>0: the eye/particle j[k-1])
    for (let k = 0; k < ch.np; k++) ch.dj.push(ch.j[k]);
    ch.len = [];                                                  // hinge-to-hinge pitch: eye-J1, ..., J(n-1)-head centre
    for (let k = 0; k < ch.np; k++) ch.len.push(ch.j[k + 1] - ch.j[k]);
    ch.iw = [];                                                   // inverse masses: light links, heavy head (flail: 1/0.3, 1/0.3, 1/1.4 — unchanged)
    for (let k = 0; k < ch.np; k++) ch.iw.push(1 / (k === ch.np - 1 ? 1.4 : 0.3));
    ch.segOfShape = [];
    for (let k = 0; k < ch.segs.length; k++) for (let i = ch.segs[k][0]; i <= ch.segs[k][1]; i++) ch.segOfShape[i] = k;
    // Segment tie v2 (2026-10-22, owner bug seed 52071): v1 demanded whole-
    // circle containment in one segment's solid ink (centre + 12 rim samples,
    // holes counted as outside). Open-ring links and the spiked ball can never
    // satisfy that — 46/49 flail circles silently fell back to segment 0, so
    // the live hitbox and the gold debug dots rode a phantom straight chain
    // whenever the links bent (visible-contact-first violation). v2: a circle
    // rides the segment whose OUTER ink contains its CENTRE (a hole is still
    // that segment's ink; innermost segment wins = paint order = what the
    // viewer sees on top); a centre on no ink ties to the nearest segment ink
    // boundary; more than TIE_TOL px from every segment's ink means bake and
    // art disagree — loud boot failure, never a silent wrong tie again.
    const ringArea = pts => { let s = 0; for (let i = 0, j = pts.length - 1; i < pts.length; j = i++) s += pts[j][0] * pts[i][1] - pts[i][0] * pts[j][1]; return Math.abs(s) / 2; };
    const segOuter = ch.segs.map(([a, b]) => { const s = []; for (let i = a; i <= b; i++) { let best = null; for (const ring of W.poly.polys[i].subs) if (!best || ringArea(ring) > ringArea(best)) best = ring; if (best) s.push(best); } return s; });
    const inOuter = (k, x, y) => segOuter[k].some(pts => {
      let inside = false;
      for (let a = 0, b = pts.length - 1; a < pts.length; b = a++) {
        const ya = pts[a][1], yb = pts[b][1];
        if ((ya > y) !== (yb > y) && x < (pts[b][0] - pts[a][0]) * (y - ya) / (yb - ya) + pts[a][0]) inside = !inside;
      }
      return inside;
    });
    const TIE_TOL = 6;
    let worstTie = 0, worstTieI = -1;
    for (let ci = 0; ci < W.poly.circles.length; ci++) {
      const c = W.poly.circles[ci];
      let k = -1;
      for (let s = ch.segs.length - 1; s >= 0; s--) if (inOuter(s, c.d, c.l)) { k = s; break; }
      if (k < 0) {
        let best = Infinity;
        for (let s = 0; s < ch.segs.length; s++) for (const pts of segOuter[s]) for (let i = 0; i < pts.length; i++) {
          const A = pts[i], B = pts[(i + 1) % pts.length];
          const dx = B[0] - A[0], dy = B[1] - A[1], L = dx * dx + dy * dy;
          let t = L ? ((c.d - A[0]) * dx + (c.l - A[1]) * dy) / L : 0; t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, t));
          const dd = Math.hypot(c.d - (A[0] + dx * t), c.l - (A[1] + dy * t));
          if (dd < best) { best = dd; k = s; }
        }
        if (best > worstTie) { worstTie = best; worstTieI = ci; }
        if (best > TIE_TOL) throw new Error(`${id} chain tie: circle ${ci} centre ${best.toFixed(1)}px from every segment ink (bake vs art desync)`);
      }
      c.s = k;
    }
    W.chainTie = { tally: (() => { const t = new Array(ch.segs.length).fill(0); for (const c of W.poly.circles) t[c.s]++; return t; })(), worst: Math.round(worstTie * 10) / 10, worstI: worstTieI };   // worstI = the worst circle's index; no reader today (inscribe prints .tally/.worst) — kept as the diagnostic a red chain-tie gate needs
  }
  /* Art-preview bootstrap (2026-10-21, owner: raw Claude deliveries must be
   * previewable, not crash): a weapon id with no CIRCLES_V2 entry boots with
   * EMPTY circles — a non-contacting ghost (gaps stay Infinity everywhere:
   * no damage, no parry, no swat) — and the frame carries a watermark. The
   * raw file is an art preview; combat truth begins when the implementer
   * bakes coverings with .qa/inscribe.mjs. Hand-authored circles stay
   * forbidden; MINR Infinity safely sizes k to 1 (ghosts have no contacts to
   * detect). Renderer/boot only — fingerprints byte-identical. */
  const UNBAKED = WEAPON_IDS.filter(id => !CIRCLES_V2[id]);

  /* ---- weapon geometry — one spine profile feeds collision, renderer and
   * audit alike (perception pass, 2026-10-16, owner-approved). Every weapon
   * is a path silhouette: drawn polygons plus covering circles packed inside
   * the same ink-inflated solid (source: the baked CIRCLES_V2, regenerated by
   * .qa/inscribe.mjs --regen from the union of the drawn polys — the INGR_*
   * bakes and the runtime cover() batch both failed the 2026-10-19 inscribe
   * audit and were superseded). Collision tests exactly those circles, so
   * every registered contact is provable against the drawing — the parts-list
   * representation died with the sling (v0.9). Locked principle: what you
   * see is what hits. measure.mjs audits the laws; .qa/inscribe.mjs is the
   * permanent inscription gate (run it after ANY art/poly/scale edit).
   *
   * Hold styles (owner decision 2026-10-16 — "it should not point outwards,
   * it should be held along the edge of the body"; built v0.7.1, amended
   * 2026-10-19): MELEE weapons hold RADIAL (the default) — the spine runs
   * straight out from the body centre, grip tucked under the disc.
   * Projectile weapons may hold EITHER way: tangential launchers (bow,
   * crossbow, boomerang, shuriken — and the shield, which launches nothing)
   * sit bow-style along the rim, the spine a straight tangent chord at the
   * body's rim point, grip centered at t = 0.5, both ends floating clear of
   * the disc; radial launchers (staff, wand) point straight out like melee.
   * The hold decides the LAUNCH POINT — radial: the tip; tangential: the
   * middle (owner 2026-10-19: "when the weapon is radial, shoot from the
   * tip, when it is the opposite, shoot from the middle, like bow and
   * crossbow"; full doctrine in fireShots' header). Damage capability: EVERY
   * weapon cuts on body touch — launchers and the shield included (allcut-r62,
   * owner 2026-11-02, retiring the 2026-10-19 projectile rule; bladeVsBody). Placement lives in ONE function
   * — spineFrame — consumed by the renderer, the collision circles, the
   * hitbox overlay and the harness audits alike, so the drawing and the
   * hitbox cannot drift apart. */
  const TAU = Math.PI * 2;
  const SPINE_R0 = 0.96;   // radial-hold spine start x bodyR — the grip tucks under the body disc

  const POPC = {};         // weapon id -> pop-in scale centre, spine-local {d, l}
  const MINR = {};         // thinnest covering-circle radius per weapon — sizes the parry substep budget
  const SPAN = {};         // spine arc length — radial: tuck + len; tangential: len
  const REACH = {};        // farthest drawn point from the body centre — tip-speed budgets + prune bound
  for (const id of WEAPON_IDS) {
    const W = WEAPONS[id];
    const tang = W.hold === 'tangential';
    const span = tang ? W.len : CFG.bodyR * (1 - SPINE_R0) + W.len;
    // the covering circles ARE the collision shape; the drawn polygons (ink
    // stroke included) are the same solid the circles pack inside
    let minR = Infinity, reach = 0;
    let d0 = Infinity, d1 = -Infinity, l0 = Infinity, l1 = -Infinity;
    for (const c of W.poly.circles) minR = Math.min(minR, c.r);
    for (const pl of W.poly.polys) for (const pts of pl.subs) for (const pt of pts) {
      /* REACH fix (owner go 2026-10-21 — the latent tightness the 2026-10-19
       * code-review pass reported and did NOT change): the 1.5px ink
       * half-stroke inflates radially OUTWARD of the body-centre distance
       * (hypot(...) + 1.5 — what the tangential branch always did); the old
       * radial branch added it laterally INSIDE the hypotenuse
       * (hypot(d, |l|+1.5)), under-stating tip-most reach by <= ~1.2-1.5px.
       * The offset solid's farthest point is a vertex distance + 1.5, so the
       * fixed form is an exact bound. Consumers: the parryGap prune and the
       * substep tip-speed budget — both carried documented slack (>=1.6px
       * prune margin, <=2.5% budget spend), so no baseline was ever red; the
       * margin simply stops being eaten. Sim-data change: k shifts where the
       * budget crosses a ceil boundary — fingerprints re-baselined with the
       * delta proof (.qa/fp-pre-reach.json -> .qa/fp-post-reach.json). */
      const rd = tang ? Math.hypot(CFG.bodyR - pt[1], pt[0] - span / 2) + 1.5      // tangential: +l points at the body, d runs along the rim
                      : Math.hypot(CFG.bodyR * SPINE_R0 + pt[0], Math.abs(pt[1])) + 1.5;
      if (rd > reach) reach = rd;
      d0 = Math.min(d0, pt[0]); d1 = Math.max(d1, pt[0]);
      l0 = Math.min(l0, pt[1]); l1 = Math.max(l1, pt[1]);
    }
    MINR[id] = minR; SPAN[id] = span; REACH[id] = reach;
    POPC[id] = { d: (d0 + d1) / 2, l: (l0 + l1) / 2 };
  }
  /* FLAIL (2026-10-22): a swinging chain can lay any link's offset radially, so REACH for a chain weapon is the
   * path bound — hinge distance along the straight chain + the point's offset from its hinge + the ink half-stroke —
   * never smaller than the straight pose (triangle inequality). Haft shapes keep the exact rigid formula above. */
  for (const id of WEAPON_IDS) {
    const W = WEAPONS[id], ch = W.chain;
    if (!ch) continue;
    let reach = REACH[id];
    for (let i = 0; i < W.poly.polys.length; i++) {
      const k = ch.segOfShape[i];
      if (!k) continue;
      for (const pts of W.poly.polys[i].subs) for (const pt of pts) reach = Math.max(reach, CFG.bodyR * SPINE_R0 + ch.dj[k] + Math.hypot(pt[0] - ch.dj[k], pt[1]) + 1.5);
    }
    REACH[id] = reach;
  }

  /* ---- LENGTH GROWTH (owner ruling 2026-10-28, the spear's trait; built 2026-10-28) ----
   * A weapon row may declare `trait.len` = the fraction of LENGTH gained per damaging hit,
   * and `lenJ` = its shaft/head junction as a fraction of its own drawn tip. Growth is
   * LENGTH-ONLY and never thickens: the spine coordinate `d` is remapped while `l` and every
   * covering radius `r` are held (owner: "i was actually preferring only the lenght, im scared
   * the spear will become 'thick'").
   *
   * The remap is PIECEWISE, not uniform. At or behind the junction, d scales by the shaft
   * factor; beyond it, d TRANSLATES rigidly — so the head cluster keeps its exact drawn shape
   * and simply sits further out. Both branches give J*k at the junction, so the map is
   * continuous and no gap opens between shaft and head.
   *
   * WHY NOT A UNIFORM d-STRETCH — measured, not assumed. `.qa/lengrow-gate.mjs` drives
   * inscribe.mjs's own gate over the ladder: a uniform stretch elongates the tapered head,
   * spreading the covering circles apart along a longer silhouette, and the deepest uncovered
   * ink point climbs 4.25 -> 5.14px, past the gate's 4.6px MISS_TOL from +6.1% onward. The
   * piecewise map holds miss at 4.18-4.50px and poke at -0.26..-0.30px across a d-REMAPPED ladder
   * — but only up to a wall, and this spear now grows past it. With the covering held (radii
   * untouched, spacing scaled) MISS binds again at tip growth +39.5% (shaft k 1.6469, miss 4.59 of
   * the 4.60 band) and fails at +40% (4.61): the shaft circles spread apart faster than their held
   * radii can bridge. At the +200% authored below, the covering therefore FOLLOWS the growth —
   * every step carries its own re-packed row in LEN_CIRCLES, baked offline against that step's own
   * stretched silhouette by the HOUSE packer (bake-rows.mjs -> inscribe.mjs's regen: the same
   * raster-EDT greedy union-inscribed cover that baked all 22 shipped rows, so no new packing
   * algorithm enters the sim and nothing is hand-placed). Gated step by step against their own art
   * (`node .qa/lengrow-bake.mjs --verify`): poke -0.30px at all twelve, miss 2.30-4.25px —
   * BETTER than the shipped base row's 4.25, because a fresh pack fits the stretched silhouette
   * instead of inheriting the base row's spacing. LEN_REMAP_CEIL below is that +39.5% wall, and a
   * growing weapon that passes it without baked rows is a BOOT ERROR, not a silent gap hit.
   * Art and circles MUST share one map: a per-shape variant (shaft scaled, head translated as a
   * body) fails on POKE from +4.9%, because the circles carry no shape label and would follow a
   * different map than the art they have to stay inscribed in.
   *
   * Note canonical :452-455 renormalises maxD to LT, and that renormalisation is scale-invariant,
   * so the authored INGR_* coordinates CANNOT carry a stretch — it is applied here, to the booted
   * world-px polys and circles, which is also what the runtime reads.
   *
   * `trait.len` is the OBSERVABLE rate: 0.0959 grows the drawn tip 9.6% per damaging hit, 12 steps
   * to +200.1% — the spear ends a round THREE times its shipped length (drawn tip 147.472 ->
   * 442.548px, REACH 210.412 -> 505.488, so from mid-arena in a 1000px box its tip reaches the
   * wall). It was 0.012 (+15.4%) when growth landed as `lengrow-r26` and 0.0253 (+35.0%) as
   * `lengrow-r27`; the owner raised it twice the same day — "i want it to be more ridiculous, so
   * increase the growth of the spear even more", then, at +35%, "its not ridiculous enough". +35%
   * was the most a d-remapped covering could take, so the second raise is what forced the baked
   * rows above rather than a preference for authored data.
   * The shaft factor delivering it is larger (the junction is ~61% of the tip; 4.2769 at the top
   * step) and is derived here, never authored — and derived per step from the tip factor, so the
   * observable growth compounds exactly at the authored rate rather than drifting as a linearised
   * shaft rate. LEN_STEPS is 12 as the BASE ladder. The "~14 damaging hits land per fighter per
   * round" figure that justified 12 was an ESTIMATE and is now measured (115 rounds across 50
   * forced-spear cells): median 24 hits, p25 17, min 3. And 24 is a hard wall rather than a
   * coincidence — base dmg 1 plus the trait's +0.3 per hit crosses 100 hp exactly at hit 24
   * (cumulative 106.8), so LETHALITY, not the ladder, is what stops the snowball. The consequence:
   * the spear already SATURATES the 12-step base in 85% of rounds. At this rate each click is still
   * ~14px of visible spear. [AMENDED nocombo-r34, 2026-10-31: the "headroom a special skill can
   * use" sentence this replaces died with `skill.lenSteps` — the cap is UNIFORM at LEN_STEPS for
   * every holder now (owner no-combos ruling), so the ladder is 12 steps, full stop. The +420%
   * era (steps 13-18, REACH 829.571) is history in GAMES.md; +200% at 12 steps is the shipped look
   * the owner playtest-approved ("it looks good now").]
   *
   * REACH is raised to the TOP step below. That is not a nicety: REACH is the parryGap prune bound
   * at :994, so a stale value would silently CULL real contacts at the grown tip, and the substep
   * tip-speed budget at :1249 reads the same table. Both become conservative. MINR is now the
   * LADDER-WIDE MINIMUM, not the base row's: a re-baked step can pack a THINNER circle than the
   * shipped row did (the spear's step 5 packs r 2.0 against a base-row 2.2, so MINR.spear is 2.00),
   * and MINR sizes the parry substep delta at :1344 — holding the base value would make the
   * budget too coarse for exactly the step that needs it finest. While the covering was merely
   * d-remapped every radius was held and the base value was correct by construction; that stopped
   * being true the moment rows were re-baked.
   *
   * Steps are per-fighter (`f.lenStep`); the CAP is UNIFORM at LEN_STEPS since nocombo-r34
   * (2026-10-31) — the per-fighter `LEN_CAP` addend (`skill.lenSteps`) was retired with the
   * owner's no-combos ruling. Every round still RESETS all growth — spin,
   * dmg and lenStep alike — and that reset is an OWNER LAW, not an implementation convenience
   * (2026-10-28, rejecting a cross-round-persistence skill: "i dont like this at all, each round
   * weapons traits should reset"). No skill may carry trait growth across a round boundary. There
   * is still no `lenCap` constant (owner: "no cap let it snowball, we will balance laer if it gets
   * too ridiculous") — the ladder's top step is the geometry ceiling, the round reset is the balance
   * bound, and lethality at 24 hits is the practical one. The shared WEAPONS row is never mutated. */
  // LEN_CIRCLES BEGIN — generated by .qa/lengrow-bake.mjs, never hand-edit

  // LEN_CIRCLES END

  /* ROW INTEGRITY (boot guard, seam-r30). Two classes of silent wrongness that a NEW AXIS
   * introduces, both caught at load rather than in a screenshot or a hung tab:
   *  (1) `brief` — APP.meta's weapon shorthand was DERIVED from a binary `trait.spin ? '+SPD' :
   *      '+DMG'` test, so it read '+DMG / Hit' for the spear and never mentioned length growth:
   *      wrong the day the length trait landed, and wronger for every axis after it. The derivation
   *      survives as a fallback for plain spin/dmg rows, but any trait axis outside {spin, dmg}
   *      REQUIRES an authored `brief` (owner ruling: authored legend labels, never derived).
   *  (2) `shot.mult` / `skill.shotMult` — the shot-cadence multiplier seam below. The effective
   *      value DIVIDES the launch accumulator's `need`, so a non-positive value would spin the
   *      release loop forever. The bow's trait.mult (multgrow-r42) rides this seam through the
   *      capped growth term; the STATIC field is still declared by no row. The check exists so a
   *      row that declares it cannot hang the sim. Checked for every (weapon, fighter) pair,
   *      since both contribute — and growth only ADDS a non-negative term, so positivity is
   *      preserved by construction.
   *  (3) `trait.shotR` (shotgrow-r33) — the shot-radius growth RATE. It feeds a Math.pow at the
   *      birth site, so a negative rate would shrink orbs toward zero and NaN would poison every
   *      shot radius silently; growth-only is the house doctrine, so it must be a positive
   *      finite number.
   *  (4) `trait.cycle` (returngrow-r37, trigger moved to the catch cycle in freeloop-r38) — the
   *      loop-CYCLE growth RATE (paired speed+turn, shape locked). Same failure shape as shotR:
   *      a negative rate would slow loops toward frozen and NaN would poison birth speeds;
   *      growth-only, positive finite.
   *  (5) `shot.returns` (freeloop-r38) — the free loop's row gate. A returning shot needs a
   *      curve to loop on (turn > 0 — a straight throw never comes home) and a finite
   *      orbit.elong in [0, 0.95): 0 is the plain circle, and the curvature modulation
   *      κ(ψ) = κ0(1 − elong·cos2ψ) must stay positive or the oval would kink.
   *      (`trait.bounce`, the ricochet-budget RATE guarded here at bouncegrow-r40, was
   *      RETIRED with its axis the same day — ricolaw-r41; `shot.ricochet` is a boolean law
   *      gate with no number to poison, so it needs no guard.)
   *  (6) `trait.mult` (multgrow-r42) — the RAIN growth RATE. It feeds the launch cadence's
   *      smul at read time, capped by MULT_STEPS; a negative rate would thin the rain toward
   *      still and NaN would poison `need` (the release loop would silently stall);
   *      growth-only, positive finite.
   *  (7) `trait.fan` (fan-r43) — the FAN growth RATE. It feeds grownVolley's tier count at read
   *      time, capped by FAN_STEPS; a negative rate would never widen the fan and NaN would
   *      poison the tier math (Math.min(NaN, CAP) = NaN — the fan silently frozen at tier 0);
   *      growth-only, positive finite.
   *  (8) `shot.pin` (pinlaw-r44) — the crossbow's NAIL law gate. A boolean, so there is no number
   *      to poison (the ricochet precedent); what IS guarded is exclusivity: a row may own
   *      exactly ONE rim-law exception — pin (nail the rim), ricochet (bounce forever) or
   *      returns (pierce) — two on one row would fight over the same arrival.
   *  (9) `shot.skewer` (skewer-r46) — the javelin's SKEWER law gate: kind-locked to 'javelin',
   *      exclusive with EVERY rim-law exception (the skewer owns the body-hit law; the rim laws
   *      own arrival). The SKEWER constants themselves are guarded at their const block (the
   *      crawl is the escape clock — a zero spin would freeze the cut-free forever). */
  const TRAIT_DERIVABLE = { spin: 1, dmg: 1 };
  for (const id of WEAPON_IDS) {
    const Wr = WEAPONS[id], tr = Wr.trait || {};
    const extra = Object.keys(tr).filter(k => tr[k] && !TRAIT_DERIVABLE[k]);
    if (extra.length && !Wr.brief) throw new Error(`${id}: trait carries ${extra.join(', ')}, which the derived brief cannot express — author a \`brief\` on the row (owner ruling: authored legend labels)`);
    if (tr.shotR != null && !(Number.isFinite(tr.shotR) && tr.shotR > 0)) throw new Error(`${id}: trait.shotR ${tr.shotR} is not a positive finite growth rate — orbs would shrink or NaN would poison the birth radius`);

  // bloom-r73 — TRANSFIGURE: the struck weapon becomes the next joke object in the rotation
  function tryFig(G, W, atk, foe) {
    if (!foe || !foe.alive || !foe.weapon) return;
    if (foe.figT <= 0 && foe.figWait > 0) return;                 // IMMUNITY — a just-poofed weapon cannot be re-bloomed at once
    if (foe.figObj === null || foe.figObj === undefined) {        // ROTATION — fixed cycle; the index lives on G (zero rng draws)
      G.figIdx = ((G.figIdx === undefined ? -1 : G.figIdx) + 1) % FIGOBJS.length;
      foe.figObj = G.figIdx;
    }
    if (foe.figT > 0) {                                           // EXTENSION — a re-hit re-doses the SAME object, under the cap
      foe.figT = Math.min(foe.figT + W.trait.fig * CFG.tickHz, FIG.cap * CFG.tickHz);
      return;
    }
    foe.figT = W.trait.fig * CFG.tickHz;                          // THE BLOOM — the five gates do the rest (bladeVsBody, bladeVsBlade, swat, fireShots, catch)
    foe.figLive = 0;                                              // bloomfix-r76: the arrival grace — the rim owns the bloom only after 0.25s of life
  }

  // bloomfix-r75 — end a bloom from OUTSIDE the countdown; bloomfix-r76 — the silence follows a NATURAL
  // expiry ONLY: a shaken-off bot knocked the joke off himself, he is re-bloomable at once (owner, seed
  // 22459: a wand hit right after a shake-off bloomed nothing — "essentially wand hit it and nothing happend")
  function endFig(f, silent) {
    f.figT = 0;
    f.figPoof = FIG.poof;
    f.figWait = silent ? FIG.immune * CFG.tickHz : 0;
    f.figObj = null;                                              // the next bloom takes the NEXT object in the cycle
  }

  // bloomfix-r76 — SILHOUETTE-TRUE RIM TEST (owner: *"the random thing touches the rim"*): replicate the
  // draw anchor (grip + 0.45 radii out along the swing), rotate every recipe vertex by the swing angle —
  // the object rides the sweep exactly like a held weapon, no spin of its own — and ask whether any
  // vertex leaves the arena circle. The BODY may rest at the edge forever; only the object's own touch shakes.
  function figTouchesRim(f) {
    const fo = FIGOBJS[f.figObj % FIGOBJS.length];
    const fr = spineFrame(f.pos.x, f.pos.y, f.wAngle, f.weapon);
    const ax = fr.ox + fr.dx * fo[0] * 0.45, ay = fr.oy + fr.dy * fo[0] * 0.45;
    const c = Math.cos(f.wAngle), sn = Math.sin(f.wAngle);
    const half = CFG.size / 2;
    for (const sh of fo[1]) for (const pt of sh[1]) {
      const px = pt[0] * fo[0], py = pt[1] * fo[0];
      const wx = ax + px * c - py * sn - half, wy = ay + px * sn + py * c - half;
      if (wx * wx + wy * wy >= half * half) return true;
    }
    return false;
  }

  // bloom-r73 — the bloom ticks down; at zero: the poof ring, the immunity window, the rotation frees.
  // bloomfix-r75 — THE SLOW TURN: the joke object eases toward the swing angle at FIG.turn rad/s (the
  // sweep itself spins many times faster) so the viewer has time to read WHAT the object is; the object
  // trails the swing like a wet noodle and settles tangential (long axis along the swing).
  function figStep(G, f) {
    if (f.figT > 0) {
      f.figT--;
      f.figLive++;
      if (f.figT <= 0) endFig(f, true);                           // natural expiry — the poof, then the 2s silence (the laugh needs absence)
      else if (f.figLive > 0.25 * CFG.tickHz && figTouchesRim(f)) endFig(f, false);   // bloomfix-r76 — THE SHAKE-OFF: the object's own silhouette touches the rim, once the arrival grace (0.25s) has passed; no silence after
    }
    if (f.figWait > 0) f.figWait--;
    if (f.figPoof > 0) f.figPoof--;
  }

 if (!(Number.isInteger(TRIO.steps) && TRIO.steps >= 1 && TRIO.poisonEvery >= 1 && TRIO.poisonDmg > 0 && TRIO.poisonTtl > 0 && TRIO.chillPer > 0 && TRIO.chillPer <= 1 && TRIO.chillFloor > 0 && TRIO.chillFloor <= 1 && TRIO.chillTtl > 0 && TRIO.fireSwell >= 0 && TRIO.fireGrow > 0)) throw new Error('TRIO: constants must be positive finite, chillFloor in (0,1] — the bite is the DoT\'s teeth and the floor is the anti-lock LAW');
  for (const aid of WEAPON_IDS) { const Ar = WEAPONS[aid]; if (Ar.shot && Ar.shot.cycle) for (const ak of Ar.shot.cycle) if (!AFFINITY[ak]) throw new Error(`${aid}: cycle kind '${ak}' has no AFFINITY payload — the trio doctrine binds every page kind to its element`); }
  for (const bid of WEAPON_IDS) { const Br = WEAPONS[bid]; if (Br.shot && Br.shot.cycle && Br.trait && Br.trait.shotR != null) throw new Error(`${bid}: shot.cycle + trait.shotR — the FIRE size swell is RETIRED (spellform-r69: the owner's shape grammar — same shape, colour only); the dormant rate lives in TRIO.fireGrow behind the TRIO.fireSwell switch`); }
  const FAN_STEPS = 5;    // fan-r43: uniform cap on the fan axis — the wall here is legibility (13 knives reads as a wall; 23 would be a blob), the CYCLE_STEPS pattern
  const FAN_SPREAD = 9;   // fan-r43: extra degrees of half-spread per tier (the base pair sits at ±22°; the capped fan reaches ±67°)   // multgrow-r42: the uniform READ-time cap on the rain axis — cadence growth has no physical wall (unlike shotR, which the rim bounds), so it saturates like CYCLE_STEPS instead of compounding forever; bow rate 0.5 × 10 steps → smul ceiling 6
  /* THE BOOMERANG'S FLIGHT LAW, current shape — review-r60 consolidated the layered halo-r39/r53/
   * r56/r59 header that had accreted here (its last two sentences still described the halo's
   * OWNER-ANCHORED oval, superseded by touchorbit-r53, and pre-r57 projectile immunity; full
   * lineage and every owner quote: GAMES.md #663–#691):
   * THE WORLD ORBIT (touchorbit-r53, from the owner's own solo prototype): the throw is an
   * arena-centred ellipse, solved once at the throw and FROZEN — no homing, no timer, no lap
   * budget; the loop lives in the WORLD, pierces the rim on its far arc, passes through bodies
   * (latched, one hit per passage), and comes home only when the wielder's motion intercepts it —
   * the catch is an EVENT, not an invariant. The halo-r39 owner-anchored oval (the catch
   * guaranteed EVERY CIRCUIT by construction) is retired precisely because of that guarantee —
   * the loop never really left him; the r38 anti-jam dials (DRIFT ramp + wide hand) are DELETED,
   * not retuned: the jam class cannot exist (spiral turn-decay remains STILLBORN — the path
   * straightened and escaped into space).
   * THE CATCH IS THE LOOP'S ONLY OWNER-SIDE END, and the loop is immune to everything else
   * (catchonly-r56, owner: "i want the boomerang to be immune to swats instead… only thing to
   * stop it is when the boomerang is consumed by the wielder") — with the shot-vs-shot exceptions
   * the owner then ruled: an enemy projectile DIES on the loop's drawn arc while the loop flies
   * on (snapfix-r57), and loop meets loop BOTH ARE DESTROYED (catchghost-r58). Blades pass
   * through with no effect at all (the swat test skips returning shots).
   * After the catch the banked spin rethrows INSTANTLY (instantthrow-r59, owner: "just instantly
   * throw it" — reversing his own chaosorbit-r54 eye, "wait 1 sec or something before throwing
   * again, it looks bad when its instant throwing after catch"; the beat is dormant at
   * RETHROW_WAIT 0, one constant from returning). */
  const LATCH_CLEAR = 60;      // px of peak clearance past the hit window that re-arms a pierced hit (the blade deep-gate idiom)
  const CATCH_ARM = 20;        // px past the catch window the throw must clear before the catch arms — the throw has to leave the hand first; catchonly-r56: the margin is read on BOTH the pivot disc AND the drawn arc (boomGap), which is what killed the departure-tick self-catch
  const CATCH_PAD = 0;         // touchorbit-r53 PURE-TOUCH ruling (owner: "implement it best possible to fit out project with pure touch"): the catch window is the BARE body touch (bodyR + r) — the halo-era 20 existed to make the geometric return a guaranteed catch; the world orbit has no guaranteed return, and the touch IS the law
  const RETHROW_WAIT = 0;    // instantthrow-r59 (owner, reversing his own r54 eye: "i want the bot to instantly cast throw the boomerang on catch again. so remove the 1 sec delay, just instantly throw it"): ZERO hand-rest — killShot still banks the rethrow revolution at the catch, so the next substep's fireShots releases it at once (fireShots runs before shotStep; the catch's compaction drops the loop in the same pass). The r54 beat (chaosorbit-r54, owner's eye then: "when the wielder catches the boomerang, wait 1 sec or something before throwing again, it looks bad when its instant throwing after catch") is DORMANT in this constant — the catchWait field, its countdown and the launch gate all still exist; set it back to 1.0 and the beat returns exactly as it was
  const CATCH_GROW = true;     // owner rulings 2026-10-31 + 2026-11-01: "each catch and throw makes it faster" — the catch-cycle is the growth trigger, and it feeds ONLY the cycle counter (not the full grow(): the spin/dmg axes stay on the damaging-hit trigger)
  const HIT_GROW = false;      // hits damage but do NOT grow (owner pick over hit-grow and both-grow)
  /* touchorbit-r53 — the halo's ANCHOR is retired (the owner's solo prototype supersedes the
   * parked halo at his word: "i really like this pattern for bomerang… with pure touch"). The
   * orbit is arena-centred and world-anchored, so the owner's motion no longer rides along with
   * the shot and the ANCHOR_V budget headroom retires with it: law 3's window reads the shot's
   * own honest maximum (the orbit peak, baked into st.speed at birth). PURE TOUCH has no
   * anti-jam machinery BY RULING: an untouched loop simply keeps orbiting (no timer, no
   * expire), and intercepting it is the wielder's skill. */
  const LEN_STEPS = 12;   // the ladder every length-growing weapon gets — the cap, for EVERY holder
  /* UNIFORM CAP (nocombo-r34, 2026-10-31, owner ruling: no special combinations — "if i ever did
   * that, its a mistake on my side"). This block used to compute a per-fighter cap (LEN_CAP) from
   * `skill.lenSteps`, the retired first special skill that let one carrier run to 18 steps while
   * everyone else stopped at 12. A fighter may never reach into a weapon trait's mechanics again:
   * skills and traits meet only by ADDING on a shared axis. So the ladder top is LEN_STEPS for
   * every holder, REACH below is the step-12 reach (505.488) for every holder, and the six baked
   * rows the 18-step era needed were purged from LEN_CIRCLES in the same landing. Another
   * length-growing weapon is still a row edit plus a re-bake; a second cap is now impossible by
   * construction rather than by discipline. */
  /* The most tip growth a d-REMAPPED covering (every radius held, spacing scaled) can take before
   * the deepest uncovered ink point passes inscribe.mjs's 4.6px MISS_TOL. SWEPT, not guessed:
   * `.qa/lengrow-gate.mjs --mode rigid` last passes at shaft k 1.6469 = tip +39.5% (miss 4.59) and
   * fails at +40% (4.61). Past it the covering has to FOLLOW the growth, so each step gets its own
   * re-packed row in LEN_CIRCLES above. The guard below makes exceeding the ceiling without baked
   * rows a BOOT ERROR rather than a silent gap hit — the failure mode the owner made top priority. */
  const LEN_REMAP_CEIL = 1.395;
  const LEN_LADDER = {};   // weapon id -> { tipK[], k[], J, circles[step][], polys[step][] }
  for (const id of WEAPON_IDS) {
    const W = WEAPONS[id];
    const rate = W.trait ? W.trait.len : 0;
    if (!rate) continue;
    if (W.chain) {   // longchain-r86: chain growth is the PITCH factor (chainGrow) — rigid segment assemblies, no ladder row exists or is needed. Gate instead: the factor at the uniform cap must stay under the row's art-connectivity ceiling, or the links disconnect at the joints — loud boot failure, never a silent broken chain.
      if (!(Number.isFinite(rate) && rate > 0)) throw new Error(`${id}: chain trait.len ${rate} is not a positive finite growth rate`);
      if (!W.chain.growMax) throw new Error(`${id}: chain weapon declares trait.len without a growMax ceiling — derive it from the link art overlap`);
      const mulMax = 1 + rate * LEN_STEPS;
      if (mulMax > W.chain.growMax) throw new Error(`${id}: trait.len ${rate} tops the chain at ${mulMax.toFixed(3)} > growMax ${W.chain.growMax} — the link art would disconnect at the joints`);
      continue;
    }
    const P = W.poly, tang = W.hold === 'tangential';
    let tip = 0;
    for (const pl of P.polys) for (const pts of pl.subs) for (const q of pts) if (q[0] > tip) tip = q[0];
    const J = tip * (W.lenJ || 0);
    if (!(J > 0) || !(J < tip)) throw new Error(`${id}: lenJ must put the junction strictly inside the drawn tip (got J ${J.toFixed(2)} of tip ${tip.toFixed(2)}) — a length-growing weapon needs a shaft to lengthen`);
    const tipK = [1], kSh = [1];
    for (let s = 1; s <= LEN_STEPS; s++) {
      const tk = Math.pow(1 + rate, s);
      tipK.push(tk);
      kSh.push(1 + (tk - 1) * tip / J);   // the shaft factor that carries the tip to tk*tip
    }
    /* Per-step coverings: a baked row wins; the d-remap is the fallback, and only under the ceiling.
     * The ART is always mapped at boot by the same rigid piecewise map, so art and circles agree —
     * the map is homogeneous of degree 1 in (d, J), so a row baked against the stretched INGR art
     * (pre-weaponScale) is exactly a row for the stretched booted art (post-weaponScale). */
    const BC = LEN_CIRCLES[id] || null;
    if (BC && BC.length !== LEN_STEPS) throw new Error(`${id}: LEN_CIRCLES carries ${BC.length} rows but LEN_STEPS is ${LEN_STEPS} — one baked covering per step, step 0 being the shipped row. Regenerate: node .qa/lengrow-bake.mjs --write`);
    if (!BC && tipK[LEN_STEPS] > LEN_REMAP_CEIL) throw new Error(`${id}: top-step tip growth +${((tipK[LEN_STEPS] - 1) * 100).toFixed(1)}% exceeds the +${((LEN_REMAP_CEIL - 1) * 100).toFixed(1)}% ceiling for a d-remapped covering (MISS-bound, swept) — bake per-step rows: node .qa/lengrow-bake.mjs --write`);
    const mapD = (d, k) => (d <= J ? d * k : d + (k - 1) * J);
    const circles = [], polys = [];
    for (let s = 0; s <= LEN_STEPS; s++) {
      const k = kSh[s];
      circles.push(s === 0 ? P.circles : (BC ? BC[s - 1] : P.circles.map(c => ({ d: mapD(c.d, k), l: c.l, r: c.r }))));
      polys.push(s === 0 ? P.polys : P.polys.map(pl => ({
        fill: pl.fill, vis: pl.vis,
        subs: pl.subs.map(pts => pts.map(q => [mapD(q[0], k), q[1]])),
      })));
    }
    LEN_LADDER[id] = { tipK, k: kSh, J, circles, polys };
    /* REACH at the top step: the prune bound and the tip-speed budget must both see the grown
     * weapon, or a contact only the grown tip can make is culled before it is ever tested. */
    let reach = REACH[id];
    for (const pl of polys[LEN_STEPS]) for (const pts of pl.subs) for (const pt of pts) {
      const rd = tang ? Math.hypot(CFG.bodyR - pt[1], pt[0] - SPAN[id] / 2) + 1.5
                      : Math.hypot(CFG.bodyR * SPINE_R0 + pt[0], Math.abs(pt[1])) + 1.5;
      if (rd > reach) reach = rd;
    }
    REACH[id] = reach;
    /* MINR becomes the ladder-wide MINIMUM, not the base row's. A re-baked covering can pack a
     * THINNER circle than the shipped row did — the spear's step 5 packs r 2.0 where the base row's
     * thinnest is 2.2 — and MINR sizes the parry substep delta at :1344 (and the shot window at
     * :1368), so keeping the base value would make the budget too coarse for exactly the step that
     * needs it finest. The min over the ladder is conservative at every step. This is a CHANGE from
     * the d-remap ladder, where every radius was held and the base row's min was correct by
     * construction; it is only correct to hold it while no row is re-baked. */
    let lmin = MINR[id];
    for (let s = 1; s <= LEN_STEPS; s++) for (const c of circles[s]) if (c.r < lmin) lmin = c.r;
    MINR[id] = lmin;
  }

  const C0 = [], C1 = [];  // world-space circle scratch [x, y, r, ...], indexed by SLOT (C0 = the left side's, C1 = the right's) — never by cast idx, or a swapped pairing would alias them
  const D0 = [], D1 = [];  // resolver-local scratch (multi-contact accumulation)

  /* The ONE placement function: where a weapon's spine sits for a body at
   * (x, y) spinning at ang. Returns the reused scratch _fr — origin = the
   * t = 0 spine point, (dx, dy) = unit direction of increasing t, span =
   * arc length. Read it (or copy the fields) before calling it again — same
   * contract as parryGap's _pg. */
  const _fr = { ox: 0, oy: 0, dx: 1, dy: 0, span: 0 };
  function spineFrame(x, y, ang, wId) {
    const c = Math.cos(ang), s = Math.sin(ang);
    if (WEAPONS[wId].hold === 'tangential') {
      const half = SPAN[wId] / 2;                  // grip centered on the rim (t = 0.5)
      _fr.ox = x + c * CFG.bodyR + s * half;       // rim point, backed up half the chord
      _fr.oy = y + s * CFG.bodyR - c * half;
      _fr.dx = -s; _fr.dy = c;                     // tangent, in the direction of increasing ang
    } else {
      _fr.ox = x + c * CFG.bodyR * SPINE_R0;       // radial: straight out, grip under the disc
      _fr.oy = y + s * CFG.bodyR * SPINE_R0;
      _fr.dx = c; _fr.dy = s;
    }
    _fr.span = SPAN[wId];
    return _fr;
  }

  /* FLAIL (2026-10-22): chain weapons are articulated. fl = the fighter's chain pose, six numbers = the unit
   * direction (d, l) of links S1..S3 in SPINE-LOCAL coordinates — a FIXED-SIZE 6-array for every chain weapon (the
   * np <= 3 cap; slots past 2*np stay at rest and are never read) — so the whole chain rides the weapon rigidly
   * whenever a body is moved (resolver, nudge) and the pose is stored in events as a plain 6-array. chainFrames fills
   * the np + 1 segment frames (origin, cos, sin, hinge d); with the rest pose [1,0,1,0,1,0] every frame collapses to
   * the spine frame, so drawing and hitbox of the straight chain equal the authored silhouette. */
  const CF_X = [0, 0, 0, 0], CF_Y = [0, 0, 0, 0], CF_C = [1, 1, 1, 1], CF_S = [0, 0, 0, 0];   // sized for the cap: np + 1 <= 4 frames
  /* mul (longchain-r86, owner go 2026-10-31 — THE LONG CHAIN): the chain-growth pitch
   * factor 1 + trait.len·min(lenStep, LEN_STEPS). ONLY the hinge-to-hinge pitches stretch;
   * every segment carries its art AND its baked covering circles RIGIDLY (both read these
   * frames), so the art↔hitbox tie is frozen per segment and no re-bake exists to drift.
   * The eye offset (ch.j[0], part of the rigid haft) never scales. Chain weapons take no
   * LEN_LADDER row — the ladder is the rigid-weapon mechanism; the boot skips chain rows
   * and gates the factor against ch.growMax instead (past it the link art disconnects). */
  function chainFrames(fr, ch, u, mul) {
    const m = mul || 1;
    CF_X[0] = fr.ox; CF_Y[0] = fr.oy; CF_C[0] = fr.dx; CF_S[0] = fr.dy;
    let px = fr.ox + fr.dx * ch.j[0], py = fr.oy + fr.dy * ch.j[0];
    for (let k = 1; k <= ch.np; k++) {
      const ud = u[2 * k - 2], ul = u[2 * k - 1];
      const dx = ud * fr.dx - ul * fr.dy, dy = ud * fr.dy + ul * fr.dx;
      CF_X[k] = px; CF_Y[k] = py; CF_C[k] = dx; CF_S[k] = dy;
      if (k < ch.np) { px += dx * ch.len[k - 1] * m; py += dy * ch.len[k - 1] * m; }
    }
  }
  function chainGrow(wId, ls) {   // the ONE growth factor — sim (flailPose/flailStep), hitbox (bladeCircles) and art (drawWeaponChain) all read it, so the three can never disagree
    const t = WEAPONS[wId].trait;
    return t && t.len ? 1 + t.len * Math.min(ls || 0, LEN_STEPS) : 1;
  }
  /* Edge-leading flip (owner decision 2026-10-22 — the katana "spins backwards"
   * observation; extended to headLead the same day at the owner's javelin
   * word): directionally asymmetric art declares the side bearing its
   * business contour — `lead` = the spine-local L-side bearing the cutting
   * face (chisel blades, hook beaks), `headLead` = the chord D-end bearing
   * the head (javelin; pivots about the centred rim grip — tangential only,
   * never both traits, boot throws). Kinematics (proven at birth, 64 angles ×
   * both signs, both axes): wAngle += spin·dt makes the LOCAL +l SIDE LEAD
   * when spin > 0, and the chord head travels +d̂ (v·d̂ = bodyR·spin). When
   * the spin sign disagrees with the declaration, the placement layer mirrors
   * ART AND HITBOX TOGETHER on the declared axis — the contour always faces
   * the motion; a parry (law 5's sign flip) re-presents it, eased by the
   * renderer-side flip transition (CFG.flipMs — the view layer only; this
   * function stays the binary sim truth at every tick and in every event).
   * Radial-asymmetric art (bow belly, knives' outward blades, tome/scroll
   * pages) must NEVER declare — mirroring faces it inward, wrong at both
   * signs. ONE source: the sim's collision, the renderer, the stills and
   * every harness audit derive the flip from THIS function, so the drawing
   * cannot drift from the hitbox. */
  function leadFlip(wId, spin) {
    const W = WEAPONS[wId];
    const L = W.lead !== undefined ? W.lead : W.headLead;   // ONE factor, two declared axes: `lead` mirrors l (the cutting side faces the motion), `headLead` mirrors d about the centred grip (the head END points the way the grip travels — javelin, owner 2026-10-22). Never both (boot throw); bladeCircles/polyPath pick the axis off the same data.
    if (!L) return 1;
    const s = spin < 0 ? -1 : 1;   // spin is never 0 in a fight (law 5: zero-spin cannot occur); the guard keeps ghosts/reveal poses sane
    return s === L ? 1 : -1;
  }

  function bladeCircles(x, y, ang, wId, out, fl, fp, ls) {
    const fr = spineFrame(x, y, ang, wId);
    const ox = fr.ox, oy = fr.oy, dx = fr.dx, dy = fr.dy;
    out.length = 0;
    const W = WEAPONS[wId];
    if (W.chain && fl) {
      chainFrames(fr, W.chain, fl, chainGrow(wId, ls));
      for (const c of W.poly.circles) {
        const k = c.s, e = c.d - W.chain.dj[k];
        out.push(CF_X[k] + CF_C[k] * e - CF_S[k] * c.l, CF_Y[k] + CF_S[k] * e + CF_C[k] * c.l, c.r);
      }
      return out;
    }
    const m = fp === undefined ? 1 : fp;
    const hd = W.headLead !== undefined, h = hd ? W.len / 2 : 0;
    /* ls = the fighter's length-growth step (0 or undefined = the shipped geometry). The two
     * branches consume it by DIFFERENT mechanisms and never both: the rigid branch takes its
     * LEN_LADDER entry (per-step baked circles+polys); the chain branch scales ONLY the
     * pitches (chainGrow, longchain-r86) — rigid segment assemblies, frozen coverage, no
     * ladder row. A step on a weapon with no growth axis falls back to the base row. */
    const L = ls ? LEN_LADDER[wId] : null;
    const CIRC = L ? L.circles[ls] : W.poly.circles;
    for (const c of CIRC) {
      let d = c.d, l = c.l;
      if (m !== 1) {   // the placement mirror — ONE factor, the weapon's declared axis: lead scales l, headLead pivots d about the centred grip (the exact-1 fast path keeps every unflagged weapon byte-identical)
        if (hd) d = h + (d - h) * m;
        else l = c.l * m;
      }
      out.push(ox + dx * d - dy * l, oy + dy * d + dx * l, c.r);
    }
    return out;
  }

  function bladeBodyGap(circ, x, y) {
    // min(surface distance) from a body centre to the blade's circles;
    // < CFG.bodyR  <=>  damaging contact
    let best = Infinity;
    for (let i = 0; i < circ.length; i += 3) {
      const d = Math.hypot(x - circ[i], y - circ[i + 1]) - circ[i + 2];
      if (d < best) best = d;
    }
    return best;
  }

  const _pg = { gap: Infinity, x: 0, y: 0, nx: 0, ny: 0 };
  const _pA = { x: 0, y: 0, ang: 0, w: null, fl: null, fp: 1, ls: 0 }, _pB = { x: 0, y: 0, ang: 0, w: null, fl: null, fp: 1, ls: 0 };   // pose scratch for bladeVsBlade's parryGap call — the sim's hottest path allocates nothing per substep
  function parryGap(pA, pB) {
    // (pX = {x, y, ang, w, fl?, fp?, ls?} — fl added 2026-10-22 for the flail's chain pose; fp added 2026-10-22 for the edge-leading mirror; ls added 2026-10-28 for the length-growth step)
    // surface gap between two blades: min(dist - rA - rB) over inscribed
    // circle pairs; <= 0  <=>  touching (parry trigger / resolver). nx,ny =
    // unit normal of the deepest pair (A-circle -> B-circle): the direction
    // the solid resolver pushes along. Result object is reused: read it
    // before calling again.
    // body-distance prune: REACH is the drawn outer radius from the body
    // centre, so beyond this sum nothing can touch — most substeps cost O(1)
    const bd = Math.hypot(pB.x - pA.x, pB.y - pA.y);
    if (bd > REACH[pA.w] + REACH[pB.w] + CFG.parryPad) {
      _pg.gap = Infinity; _pg.x = 0; _pg.y = 0; _pg.nx = 0; _pg.ny = 0;
      return _pg;
    }
    bladeCircles(pA.x, pA.y, pA.ang, pA.w, C0, pA.fl, pA.fp, pA.ls);   // pX.fl: the chain pose (flail) — undefined for every rigid weapon; pX.fp: the edge-leading mirror; pX.ls: the length-growth step
    bladeCircles(pB.x, pB.y, pB.ang, pB.w, C1, pB.fl, pB.fp, pB.ls);
    let best = Infinity, bx = 0, by = 0, bnx = 0, bny = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < C0.length; i += 3) {
      for (let j = 0; j < C1.length; j += 3) {
        const dx = C1[j] - C0[i], dy = C1[j + 1] - C0[i + 1];
        const reach2 = C0[i + 2] + C1[j + 2] + CFG.parryPad;
        if (dx > reach2 || dx < -reach2 || dy > reach2 || dy < -reach2) continue;
        const dc = Math.hypot(dx, dy);
        const d = dc - C0[i + 2] - C1[j + 2];
        if (d < best) {
          best = d; bx = (C0[i] + C1[j]) / 2; by = (C0[i + 1] + C1[j + 1]) / 2;
          if (dc > 1e-9) { bnx = dx / dc; bny = dy / dc; }
          else {
            // degenerate concentric pair — fall back to the body line
            const ex = pB.x - pA.x, ey = pB.y - pA.y, ed = Math.hypot(ex, ey) || 1;
            bnx = ex / ed; bny = ey / ed;
          }
        }
      }
    }
    _pg.gap = best; _pg.x = bx; _pg.y = by; _pg.nx = bnx; _pg.ny = bny;
    return _pg;
  }

  /* harness surface — the FIVE functions every audit recomputes event and snapshot poses
   * through (same truth as sim and renderer). EXPORTED BY NAME, NOT BY USE: each harness
   * extracts this script body and appends `;return { …, geom }` — measure.mjs, ingest.mjs,
   * .qa/fingerprint.mjs, .qa/leadproof.mjs (list corrected 2026-10-28: it named eight, four retired
   * in the pre-skills cleanup) — so `geom` deliberately has NO in-file reference, re-verified that
   * same day by the whole-file canonical audit as the ONLY unreferenced top-level declaration here.
   * A dead-code scan must not remove it: that breaks all four at once, measure.mjs included. */
  const geom = {
    bladeCircles: bladeCircles, bladeBodyGap: bladeBodyGap,
    spineFrame: spineFrame, parryGap: parryGap, leadFlip: leadFlip,
  };

  /* ---- seeded RNG: splitmix32 seeding -> sfc32 stream (SPEC's PRNG) ---- */
  function splitmix32(a) {
    return function () {
      a |= 0; a = (a + 0x9e3779b9) | 0;
      let t = a ^ (a >>> 16);
      t = Math.imul(t, 0x21f0aaad);
      t = t ^ (t >>> 15);
      t = Math.imul(t, 0x735a2d97);
      return ((t = t ^ (t >>> 15)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
    };
  }
  function makeRng(seed) {
    const sm = splitmix32(seed >>> 0);
    let a = (sm() * 4294967296) >>> 0, b = (sm() * 4294967296) >>> 0,
        c = (sm() * 4294967296) >>> 0, d = (sm() * 4294967296) >>> 0;
    const sfc = function () {
      a |= 0; b |= 0; c |= 0; d |= 0;
      let t = (((a + b) | 0) + d) | 0;
      d = (d + 1) | 0;
      a = b ^ (b >>> 9);
      b = (c + (c << 3)) | 0;
      c = (c << 21) | (c >>> 11);
      c = (c + t) | 0;
      return (t >>> 0) / 4294967296;
    };
    for (let i = 0; i < 12; i++) sfc();
    return sfc;
  }

  const SPAWN = [{ x: 280, y: 380 }, { x: 720, y: 380 }];

  function emit(G, kind, data) {
    const e = data || {};
    e.kind = kind; e.tick = G.t;
    if (G.audit) e.sub = G.auditSub;   // substep index — perception audit correlation
    G.events.push(e);
  }

  /* `slot` is the SIDE (0 = the left spawn, 1 = the right spawn); `idx` is the CAST IDENTITY (the
   * row in FIGHTERS). They were ONE field while the only pairing was [0, 1]; the split is what lets
   * a match pick 2 of N cast members without touching a single law.
   *   SLOT-keyed (means "left/right" or "the other side"): SPAWN, the roll order ws[]/w0/w1, the
   *     launch direction sign, G.wins / G.winner / G.roundWinner, `1 - f.slot`, fs[0]/fs[1],
   *     view / flashV / flipAnim / koStill.pose, the C0/C1 circle scratch, `fs[st.o]`, and every
   *     event actor ref (by / to / o / winner / loser).
   *   IDX-keyed (means "who is this"): COLS, TINTS, SKILL_SHORT, FIGHTERS[idx].skill,
   *     meta.fighters (the roster table).
   * The two coincide exactly while cast is [0, 1], which is why the default pairing is inert. */
  function newFighter(castIdx, slot) {
    return {
      idx: castIdx, slot: slot, weapon: null, hp: CFG.hp, alive: true,
      pos: { x: SPAWN[slot].x, y: SPAWN[slot].y }, vel: { x: 0, y: 0 },
      wAngle: 0, spin: 0, dmg: 0,
      lenStep: 0,                          // length-growth ladder position (0..LEN_STEPS) — the spear's trait, capped UNIFORM for every holder since nocombo-r34; reset per round like spin/dmg (owner law)
      shotStep: 0,                         // shot-radius growth count — the staff's trait (shotgrow-r33): landings so far this round; the next born shot scales by (1+trait.shotR)^shotStep; UNCAPPED (the rim is the wall), reset per round (owner law)
      prev: { x: SPAWN[slot].x, y: SPAWN[slot].y }, pwAngle: 0,   // render-interpolation base (v0.8.2) — pose at this tick's start
      bladeStuck: false, wallCd: 0,
      bladeLatchTick: 0, bladeClearPeak: 0,   // deep-disengage gate state (law 4's re-arm extension, owner 2026-10-23): the tick the current blade latch fired + the peak body clearance (px) reached since — both written fresh at every latch and every round roll, never read while unstuck
      nudgeTick: -1,                         // last tick a pin-escape nudge was added to THIS fighter — one add per tick per fighter (the nudge's smoothness gate, owner 2026-10-21; per-fighter state — it once sat misfiled on newGame's G)
      deathSeq: 0,                         // death-order stamp — only read on a same-tick double K.O.
      fireAcc: 0,                          // projectile launcher: accumulated radians toward the next release (one shot per revolution)
      catchWait: 0,                        // chaosorbit-r54: seconds of hand-rest left after the returns flight ends (catchonly-r56: the catch is the only returns end) — the launch gate holds while it counts down; reset per round like every per-round state
      cycleIdx: 0,
      figT: 0, figWait: 0, figPoof: 0, figObj: null, figLive: 0,   // bloom-r73 — transfiguration state (the bloom, the immunity, the poof ring, the rotation pick; bloomfix-r76: figLive the arrival grace)                         // shot-kind cycle position (the row's `cycle`; strict rotation — the tome trio today, phase 3, 2026-10-25; renamed off spellIdx at the 2026-10-28 launcher consolidation, which made the cycle row data)
      skew: null,                          // SKEWER state (skewer-r46): null, or { phase 'carry'|'pin', t, dur, sx/sy, dx/dy, spinBase, bleedAcc, nx/ny, cutArm, anchor } — the javelin's impalement; reset every round (the LAW)
      /* CHAIN state (flail 2026-10-22, N-segment generic) — present on every fighter (inert unless the weapon has a
       * chain), reset by flailInit. FIXED SIZE for the cap np <= 3 (the boot throws past it):
       * u/pu = chain pose now / at tick start (6 numbers, spine-local unit directions of links S1..S3; slots past
       * 2*np stay at rest and are never read; pu feeds render blending),
       * x,y,vx,vy = world position + velocity of the np chain particles (flail: joint J1, joint J2, ball centre),
       * qx,qy = per-substep scratch, vmax = fastest particle at tick start (substep budget). */
      fl: { u: [1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0], pu: [1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0], x: [0, 0, 0], y: [0, 0, 0], vx: [0, 0, 0], vy: [0, 0, 0], qx: [0, 0, 0], qy: [0, 0, 0], vmax: 0 },
    };
  }

  /* PAIRING (pair-r31, owner go 2026-10-28): the CAST is the roster (FIGHTERS); the PAIRING is
   * which two of them play this match, and on which side. `cast` is [leftCastIdx, rightCastIdx] —
   * slot-ordered, so `G.cast[slot]` maps a side to its actor. The shipped default is the whole cast
   * in list order, which is what every battle so far has played, so the default pairing is
   * byte-identical in behaviour to the pre-pairing build (fingerprints prove it). A repeated entry
   * is a legal MIRROR pairing (the same bot on both sides) — nothing in the sim needs the two to
   * differ. Guarded at boot AND on every construction: a bad index would read undefined out of
   * FIGHTERS far from here. */
  const DEFAULT_CAST = [0, 1];
  function checkCast(cast) {
    if (!Array.isArray(cast) || cast.length !== 2) throw new Error(`cast must be an array of exactly 2 FIGHTERS indices (a pairing fills two slots), got ${JSON.stringify(cast)}`);
    for (const c of cast) {
      if (!Number.isInteger(c) || c < 0 || c >= FIGHTERS.length) throw new Error(`cast entry ${JSON.stringify(c)} is not an integer index into FIGHTERS (length ${FIGHTERS.length}) — a pairing picks cast members, it cannot invent one`);
    }
    return cast;
  }
  checkCast(DEFAULT_CAST);   // boot guard: the shipped pairing is validated at load, not on first use

  function newGame(seed, opts) {
    const o = opts || {};
    const cast = checkCast(o.cast || DEFAULT_CAST);
    return {
      seed: seed >>> 0,
      cast: cast.slice(),                  // [leftCastIdx, rightCastIdx] — slot -> cast identity; `G.cast[slot]` is the only slot->idx map
      weapons: o.weapons || null,          // [id|null, id|null] — curator force; viewer never knows
      rng: makeRng(seed),
      phase: 'reveal', phaseT: 0,
      round: 1, wins: [0, 0],
      t: 0, over: false, winner: null,
      roundWinner: null,                   // fighter checkKO just credited — the K.O. card reads it (a wins comparison misreads 1–1)
      fighters: [newFighter(cast[0], 0), newFighter(cast[1], 1)],   // fighters[] is SLOT-ordered: fighters[s].slot === s, so `1 - f.slot` and fs[0]/fs[1] both mean "the other side"
      clash: false,                        // blade-blade contact latch (hysteresis): one parry per fresh touch
      clinchT: 0,                          // clinch-spring ramp level in ticks (0 = no push); climbs while the latch stays shut, decays once the blades clear
      parryT: -999,                        // tick of the last fired parry — the flutter gate's re-arm clock (law 2's gate, owner option 1 2026-10-21)
      bounceT: -1,                         // last tick that emitted a bounce (once-per-tick throttle)
      rolls: [],
      events: [],
      shots: [], shotSid: 0,             // in-flight projectiles (sim-generic 'shot' — arrows/orbs/sparks/bolts/boomerangs/stars); sid = battle-unique id (audit accounting)
      pools: [],                         // emberpool-r79 — THE BURNING POOL: fire left on the floor by scroll hits ({x, y, r, t, acc, o, dmg, sid}), stepped in poolStep, cleared by the roll (round-reset LAW)
      embers: [], emberFx: [], emberSid: 0,           // kindling-r82 — THE EMBER SPILL: coals shed by the scroll's flight ({x, y, r, t, o, dmg, glow, eid}), popped in emberStep, cleared by the roll (round-reset LAW); emberFx = the pop bursts' visual timers ({x, y, t} — the figPoof precedent, kindlingfix-r83); emberSid = battle-unique art-phase ids (never reset, the shotSid precedent)
      deathSeq: 0,                         // death-order counter — stamps f.deathSeq so a same-tick double K.O. credits the survivor
      stats: { hits: 0, parries: 0, thrown: 0, landed: 0, swatted: 0, rim: 0, crossed: 0, pools: 0, poolBurns: 0, embers: 0, emberPops: 0 },   // battle-level counters (no effect on dynamics) — emberpool-r79: pools/poolBurns; kindling-r82: embers = coals shed, emberPops = bites dealt
      maxSpin: 0, maxDmg: 0,               // ridiculousness trackers (battle-level)
      audit: false, auditSub: 0, auditSubs: [], auditShots: [], auditK: [], auditFl: [],   // perception-audit instrumentation (harness-only; inert in the browser)
    };
  }

  function tick(G) {
    if (G.over) return;            // battle over: the clock is frozen — chrome's stats line reads G.t
    G.events.length = 0;
    if (G.audit) { G.auditSubs.length = 0; G.auditShots.length = 0; G.auditK.length = 0; G.auditFl.length = 0; }
    G.t++;
    if (G.phase === 'reveal') {
      if (G.phaseT === 0) rollWeapons(G);
      G.phaseT++;
      if (G.phaseT >= CFG.revealTicks) startFight(G);
    } else if (G.phase === 'fight') {
      G.phaseT++;                    // fight clock: weapon pop-in ramp + scorebug round seconds read it
      stepPhysics(G);
      checkKO(G);
    } else if (G.phase === 'ko') {
      G.phaseT++;
      if (G.phaseT >= CFG.koTicks) {
        if (G.wins[0] >= CFG.roundsToWin || G.wins[1] >= CFG.roundsToWin) {
          G.phase = 'over'; G.over = true;
          G.winner = G.wins[0] > G.wins[1] ? 0 : 1;
          emit(G, 'battleWin', { winner: G.winner, wins: G.wins.slice() });
        } else {
          G.round++;
          G.phase = 'reveal'; G.phaseT = 0;
        }
      }
    }
    /* phase 'over': idle — chrome holds the winner overlay */
  }

  function rollWeapons(G) {
    const r = G.rng;
    const rolled = [
      WEAPON_IDS[Math.floor(r() * WEAPON_IDS.length)],
      WEAPON_IDS[Math.floor(r() * WEAPON_IDS.length)],
    ];
    const forced = G.weapons || [null, null];
    const ws = [forced[0] || rolled[0], forced[1] || rolled[1]];
    G.rolls.push({ round: G.round, w: ws.slice() });
    for (const f of G.fighters) {
      const W = WEAPONS[ws[f.slot]];   // ws is the roll, SLOT-ordered (w0 = the left side's weapon, w1 = the right's)
      const s = SPAWN[f.slot];
      f.weapon = ws[f.slot];
      f.hp = CFG.hp; f.alive = true;
      f.pos.x = s.x; f.pos.y = s.y; f.vel.x = 0; f.vel.y = 0;
      f.wAngle = 0; f.spin = 0; f.dmg = W.dmg;
      f.lenStep = 0;                       // growth resets with the round — the round IS the cap (no lenCap constant)
      f.shotStep = 0;                      // shot-radius / cycle / rain growth resets with the round — same LAW, same place (the shared counter; the ricochet-budget feed retired with bouncegrow-r40)
      f.bladeStuck = false; f.wallCd = 0; f.fireAcc = 0; f.catchWait = 0; f.deathSeq = 0; f.cycleIdx = 0;
      f.bladeLatchTick = 0; f.bladeClearPeak = 0;   // teleport: the deep-disengage gate starts the new round fresh
      f.nudgeTick = -1;                    // teleport: no carried nudge gate into the new round
      f.skew = null;                       // skewer-r46: no impalement carried into the new round (the round-reset LAW) — anchors die with the roll's shot-clear
      f.dot = null; f.chill = null;        // affinity-r66: no venom, no chill carried over the roll — victim-side statuses obey the round-reset LAW like traits
      f.figT = 0; f.figWait = 0; f.figPoof = 0; f.figObj = null; f.figLive = 0;   // bloom-r73 — the joke resets every round (LAW); G.figIdx keeps the match-long rotation
      f.prev.x = f.pos.x; f.prev.y = f.pos.y; f.pwAngle = 0;   // teleport: snap the interpolation base — no slide from last round's pose
      flailInit(f);                        // flail chain: hang straight, at rest — reset per round like every other per-battle state
    }
    G.clash = false; G.parryT = -999; G.clinchT = 0;   // fresh round: fresh latch, gate clock reset, clinch spring unwound
    const clearedSids = G.shots.map(st => st.sid);     // shots frozen at the K.O. vanish with the round (audit accounting)
    G.shots.length = 0;
    G.pools.length = 0;                  // emberpool-r79 — every fire resets with the round (the round-reset LAW, same place as the shot clear)
    G.embers.length = 0; G.emberFx.length = 0;   // kindling-r82 — every coal (and every burst) resets with the round (round-reset LAW; emberSid keeps counting — battle-unique ids)
    emit(G, 'roll', { round: G.round, w0: ws[0], w1: ws[1], shotsCleared: clearedSids.length, clearedSids: clearedSids });
  }

  function startFight(G) {
    const r = G.rng;
    /* Core contact law rule 6: every round opens counter-rotating. ONE seeded
     * roll per round picks fighter 0's direction; fighter 1 always gets the
     * opposite. Rolled, not fixed per cast (owner decision, 2026-10-16 —
