     * "imagine in the future a roster of 50 bots, it annoying to keep track
     * of to keep it even"): stateless, self-balancing at any roster size,
     * and mirror duels cannot open same-direction. Draw order per round is
     * fixed: 2 weapon draws, 1 direction draw, 2 launch draws (one angle per
     * fighter). */
    const dir0 = r() < 0.5 ? -1 : 1;
    for (const f of G.fighters) {
      const a = r() * TAU;
      f.vel.x = Math.cos(a) * CFG.launchSpeed;
      f.vel.y = Math.sin(a) * CFG.launchSpeed;
      f.spin = (f.slot === 0 ? dir0 : -dir0) * WEAPONS[f.weapon].omega;   // rule 6 is about SIDES, not identities: the left slot takes the seeded direction
      f.wAngle = a;
      f.pwAngle = a;                       // teleport: snap the interpolation base — no first-frame sweep from the reveal angle
      flailInit(f);                        // flail chain: straight at the launch pose, carried at the launch velocity (no random draw)
    }
    G.phase = 'fight'; G.phaseT = 0;
    emit(G, 'roundStart', { round: G.round });
  }

  function checkKO(G) {
    const a = G.fighters[0], b = G.fighters[1];
    let dead;
    if (!a.alive && !b.alive) dead = a.deathSeq < b.deathSeq ? a : b;   // same-tick double K.O.: whoever fell first loses — the other survived longer
    else if (!a.alive) dead = a;
    else if (!b.alive) dead = b;
    else return;
    const w = 1 - dead.slot;   // the survivor is the OTHER SIDE; wins is slot-keyed (the scorebug prints left–right)
    G.wins[w]++;
    G.roundWinner = w;                 // the K.O. card reads this — a wins comparison misreads a 1–1 tie
    G.phase = 'ko'; G.phaseT = 0;
    emit(G, 'ko', { winner: w, loser: dead.slot, x: dead.pos.x, y: dead.pos.y, round: G.round, wins: G.wins.slice() });
  }

  /* ---- physics (circular bowl only) ---- */

  function stepPhysics(G) {
    const dt = 1 / CFG.tickHz;
    const fs = G.fighters;
    /* Render-interpolation base (v0.8.2, pattern from sumo_war (2).html):
     * save every actor's tick-start pose. The renderer blends prev→current by
     * the leftover tick fraction so motion stays even on displays whose refresh
     * is not an integer multiple of the 120 Hz tick (144/165/240 Hz showed
     * systematic dead frames — .qa/pacing.mjs, 2026-10-17). Pure copy: laws,
     * audits, and determinism never read these fields. */
    for (const f of fs) {
      f.prev.x = f.pos.x; f.prev.y = f.pos.y; f.pwAngle = f.wAngle;
      if (WEAPONS[f.weapon].chain) {                       // chain: pose base for render blending + the fastest particle for the substep budget
        const F = f.fl, np = WEAPONS[f.weapon].chain.np;
        for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) F.pu[i] = F.u[i];
        F.vmax = 0;
        for (let k = 0; k < np; k++) F.vmax = Math.max(F.vmax, Math.hypot(F.vx[k], F.vy[k]));
      }
    }
    for (const st of G.shots) { st.px = st.x; st.py = st.y; }
    /* Substep sizing (v0.5.1 tunneling bug -> v0.8-step1 rule): relative
     * travel per substep <= HALF the narrowest contact window (rA+rB of the
     * thinnest inscribed circles). The old formula carried +parryPad/2 of
     * slack: harmless while the thinnest circles were needle tips, fatal for
     * path coverings, where one leapfrogged step buries a contact cluster
     * deeper than the resolver can unwind. The velocity budget uses REACH =
     * the DRAWN outer radius from the body centre, so tip speed is never
     * under-budgeted. measure.mjs verifies the bound per substep and flags
     * any maxSub engagement. */
    const delta = (MINR[fs[0].weapon] + MINR[fs[1].weapon]) / 2;
    let relV = CFG.subMargin;
    for (const f of fs) {
      if (!f.alive) continue;
      const tipV = Math.abs(f.spin) * REACH[f.weapon];
      relV += Math.hypot(f.vel.x, f.vel.y) + (WEAPONS[f.weapon].chain && f.fl.vmax > tipV ? f.fl.vmax : tipV);   // flail: a whipped chain can outrun omega*REACH — budget its fastest particle
    }
    let k = Math.ceil((relV * dt) / delta);
    /* Projectile budget (v0.7): a shot is killed on contact, never resolved,
     * so its detection guarantee is the same shape as the blades' — relative
     * travel per substep <= HALF the narrowest shot window. The narrowest is
     * shot-vs-blade-swat (shot r + the foe weapon's thinnest inscribed
     * circle), and shot speed against the foe's blade tip is the largest
     * relative velocity in the sim (GAMES.md, law 3's projectile extension).
     * subMargin covers in-tick impulses exactly as the blade budget does. */
    let kProjF = 0;
    for (const f of fs) {
      if (!f.alive) continue;
      const W = WEAPONS[f.weapon];
      if (!W.shot) continue;
      const foe = fs[1 - f.slot];
      const foeV = foe.alive
        ? (WEAPONS[foe.weapon].chain ? Math.max(Math.abs(foe.spin) * REACH[foe.weapon], foe.fl.vmax) : Math.abs(foe.spin) * REACH[foe.weapon]) + Math.hypot(foe.vel.x, foe.vel.y)
        : 0;
      const win = W.shot.r + (foe.alive ? MINR[foe.weapon] : W.shot.r);
      /* cycle growth budgets the FASTEST birth speed this holder can launch — the row speed alone
       * would under-budget a grown boomerang and let it tunnel the swat/body/catch windows.
       * pow(x,0)===1 with the same CYCLE_STEPS read-time cap keeps every other launcher's budget
       * bit-identical. (returngrow-r37) */
      const bspd = W.shot.speed * Math.pow(1 + ((W.trait && W.trait.cycle) || 0), Math.min(f.shotStep, CYCLE_STEPS)) * (W.shot.returns && W.shot.orbit ? W.shot.orbit.peak : 1);   // touchorbit-r53: a returning shot's honest maximum world speed is the periapsis PEAK (speed·peak, birth-snapshot growth included) — the anchor's owner-velocity headroom (ANCHOR_V) retired with the anchor
      const req = ((bspd + foeV + CFG.subMargin) * dt) / (win / 2);
      if (req > kProjF) kProjF = req;
    }
    if (G.shots.length >= 2) {
      /* shot-vs-shot: worst PAIR, not shots[0] — mixed projectile speeds
       * since v1.0 (spark 800 vs orb 430 …) made the old single-speed formula
       * under-budget the relative travel; window = rA + rB, half = (rA+rB)/2.
       * O(n²) on a handful of in-flight shots. */
      for (let i = 0; i < G.shots.length; i++) {
        for (let j = i + 1; j < G.shots.length; j++) {
          const A = G.shots[i], B = G.shots[j];
          const req = ((A.speed + B.speed + CFG.subMargin) * dt) / ((A.r + B.r) / 2);
          if (req > kProjF) kProjF = req;
        }
      }
    }
    const kProj = Math.ceil(kProjF);
    if (kProj > k) k = kProj;
    if (k < 1) k = 1;
    if (k > CFG.maxSub) k = CFG.maxSub;
    const sdt = dt / k;
    const maxV2 = CFG.maxSpeed * CFG.maxSpeed;
    if (G.audit) {
      G.auditK.push(k, Math.ceil((relV * dt) / delta), kProj);   // [chosen, blade-required, projectile-required]
      snapAudit(G, fs, -1);                                      // tick-entry pose: displacement baseline
      G.auditShots.push(G.shots.length);                       // rendered-frame shot poses (law 3, shot variant)
      for (const st of G.shots) G.auditShots.push(st.sid, st.x, st.y, st.o, st.r);
    }
    for (let s = 0; s < k; s++) {
      for (const f of fs) if (f.alive) clinchForce(G, f, sdt);   // clinch spring: ramped separation while the latch holds, per substep like every other force
      for (const f of fs) if (f.alive) integrate(f, sdt);
      for (const f of fs) if (f.alive) boundary(G, f);
      bodyCollide(G, fs[0], fs[1]);
      for (const f of fs) {
        f.wAngle += f.spin * chillMul(f) * bloomMul(f) * sdt;   // affinity-r66: the chill sags the sweep; bloomfix-r77: the bloom sags it harder (FIG.slow) so the joke object orbits slow enough to read
        if (f.wallCd > 0) f.wallCd = Math.max(0, f.wallCd - sdt);
      }
      for (const f of fs) if (f.alive && WEAPONS[f.weapon].chain) flailStep(f, sdt);   // FLAIL: the chain swings under the same pose the contact tests below see
      if (G.audit) { G.auditSub = s; snapAudit(G, fs, s); G.auditFl.push(s, ...fs[0].fl.u, ...fs[1].fl.u); }   // the exact poses the contact tests below see (+ chain poses, stride 13: sub, 6 + 6)
      for (const f of fs) bladeVsBody(G, f);
      bladeVsBlade(G);
      for (const f of fs) if (f.alive && f.skew) skewStep(G, f, sdt);   // skewer-r46 + impale-r48 order law: the impaled foe's position lock is the LAST fighter-pos writer in the substep — after integrate, boundary, bodyCollide's resolver AND bladeVsBlade's parry shove (the smoke caught each in turn nudging the pinned victim off the wall while the spear held its rim point): the skewer owns the body absolutely until it is cut free
      for (const f of fs) if (f.alive && WEAPONS[f.weapon].chain) flailSync(f);   // FLAIL: the resolver may have moved/turned the body — the chain rode rigidly, carry its particles along
      fireShots(G, fs, sdt);      // launcher release — one shot per revolution, per the launch-point doctrine (fireShots header)
      shotStep(G, fs, sdt);       // shot flight + rim/body/swat/cross resolutions
      for (const f of fs) {
        const sp = Math.abs(f.spin);
        if (sp > G.maxSpin) G.maxSpin = sp;
        if (f.dmg > G.maxDmg) G.maxDmg = f.dmg;
        // chaos ceiling (CFG.maxSpeed, owner option 1 2026-10-21 — it began as the TEMPORARY observer
        // cap 1100 and was ratified at 1200): clamp travel so the sim stays inside the ceiling
        const v2 = f.vel.x * f.vel.x + f.vel.y * f.vel.y;
        if (v2 > maxV2) {
          const k2 = CFG.maxSpeed / Math.sqrt(v2);
          f.vel.x *= k2; f.vel.y *= k2;
        }
      }
    }
    for (const f of fs) if (f.alive && f.skew) skewBleed(G, f);
    for (const f of fs) if (f.alive && (f.dot || f.chill)) dotStep(G, f);   // affinity-r66: the trio statuses pulse per TICK like the bleed (a beat, not a physics rate)   // skewer-r46: bleed pulses — per TICK, not per substep (a pulse is a readable beat)
    for (const f of fs) if (f.alive && (f.figT > 0 || f.figWait > 0 || f.figPoof > 0)) figStep(G, f);   // bloom-r73: the joke counts down to its poof
    poolStep(G, fs);                                   // emberpool-r79 — the pools tick down and burn whoever stands in the fire (per TICK, a readable beat like the bleed)
    emberStep(G, fs);                                  // kindling-r82 — the coals tick down and POP (one bite, consumed) under whoever steps on them
    G.clinchT = G.clash ? Math.min(G.clinchT + 1, CFG.clinchRamp) : Math.max(0, G.clinchT - CFG.clinchDecay);   // clinch spring ramp level: climbs while the latch holds, decays once the blades clear
  }

  function snapAudit(G, fs, s) {
    // stride 13: [sub, then per fighter: x, y, wAngle, bladeStuck,
    // spin (SIGNED — the spin-recoil law is audited off these), alive]
    const a = fs[0], b = fs[1];
    G.auditSubs.push(
      s,
      a.pos.x, a.pos.y, a.wAngle, a.bladeStuck ? 1 : 0, a.spin, a.alive ? 1 : 0,
      b.pos.x, b.pos.y, b.wAngle, b.bladeStuck ? 1 : 0, b.spin, b.alive ? 1 : 0
    );
  }

  function integrate(f, sdt) {
    f.vel.y += CFG.gravity * sdt;
    f.pos.x += f.vel.x * sdt;   // chillfix-r71 (owner ruling: "freeze/slow effect should only apply to the weapon… i dont want the bot to fall to the floor"): the chill NEVER touches the body — no drag, no sagged jumps, no floor-fall; the slow lives in the weapon swing alone
    f.pos.y += f.vel.y * sdt;
  }

  /* ---- CHAIN weapons (flail 2026-10-22, N-segment generic): a taut jointed chain under the game's own physics ----
   * np = ch.np point particles hang off the eye (j[0], fixed to the weapon); flail: Q1 = joint J1, Q2 = joint J2,
   * B = ball centre. Per substep, in world space, exactly like the bodies: gravity + the same integrator, then a
   * position-based solve of np rigid rods (pitches ch.len) with the eye as the only anchor, then velocity =
   * displacement / dt (so every impulse the bodies get — wall bounce, floor trampoline, parry shove, hit knock,
   * the spin flip — reaches the chain as a real whip, no scripted lag). Gravity cancels while the bot is in free
   * fall, so a steady spin leaves the chain streaming outward with a small drag lean (CFG.flailDrag); a parry
   * flip throws the head through. The head particle is heavier than the links (ch.iw, boot). The chain never
   * pushes the body (one-way coupling, like every weapon) and never enters the own disc: every chord is kept
   * clear of it, so the tuck clip never hides a hitbox. Pure arithmetic on fighter state — no random draw, no
   * allocation. Contact stays honest: the hit/parry/swat laws read the chain through bladeCircles(…, f.fl.u),
   * and the chain pose rides rigidly through the resolver (flailSync) — blades stay solids to each other, head
   * included. */
  function flailPose(f) {                // chain particles at the chain pose f.fl.u on the current weapon pose
    const W = WEAPONS[f.weapon], ch = W.chain, F = f.fl;
    const mul = chainGrow(f.weapon, f.lenStep);   // longchain-r86: the SAME factor chainFrames reads — the sim pose can never disagree with the drawn/hitbox frames
    const fr = spineFrame(f.pos.x, f.pos.y, f.wAngle, f.weapon);
    let px = fr.ox + fr.dx * ch.j[0], py = fr.oy + fr.dy * ch.j[0];
    for (let k = 0; k < ch.np; k++) {
      const ud = F.u[2 * k], ul = F.u[2 * k + 1];
      const L = ch.len[k] * mul;
      px += (ud * fr.dx - ul * fr.dy) * L; py += (ud * fr.dy + ul * fr.dx) * L;
      F.x[k] = px; F.y[k] = py;
    }
  }
  function flailInit(f) {                     // straight chain at the current pose, carried at the weapon's own velocity (rigid) — no history
    const F = f.fl;
    F.u[0] = 1; F.u[1] = 0; F.u[2] = 1; F.u[3] = 0; F.u[4] = 1; F.u[5] = 0;   // all 6 slots to rest (fixed-size state; slots past 2*np are never read)
    for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) F.pu[i] = F.u[i];
    F.vmax = 0;
    if (!f.weapon || !WEAPONS[f.weapon].chain) return;
    const np = WEAPONS[f.weapon].chain.np;
    flailPose(f);
    for (let k = 0; k < np; k++) {
      F.vx[k] = f.vel.x - f.spin * (F.y[k] - f.pos.y);
      F.vy[k] = f.vel.y + f.spin * (F.x[k] - f.pos.x);
      F.vmax = Math.max(F.vmax, Math.hypot(F.vx[k], F.vy[k]));
    }
  }
  function flailSync(f) {                     // after the resolver: particles re-seated on the (possibly moved) pose, velocities untouched
    flailPose(f);
  }
  function flailRod(X, Y, a, b, L, iw) {      // keep particles a,b exactly L apart (a = -1: the fixed eye is passed via X[3],Y[3]; iw = the chain's inverse masses)
    const ax = a < 0 ? X[3] : X[a], ay = a < 0 ? Y[3] : Y[a];
    let dx = X[b] - ax, dy = Y[b] - ay;
    const d = Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
    if (d < 1e-9) return;
    const k = (d - L) / d;
    if (a < 0) { X[b] -= dx * k; Y[b] -= dy * k; return; }
    const wa = iw[a], wb = iw[b], sw = wa + wb;
    X[a] += dx * k * wa / sw; Y[a] += dy * k * wa / sw;
    X[b] -= dx * k * wb / sw; Y[b] -= dy * k * wb / sw;
  }
  const FL_X = [0, 0, 0, 0], FL_Y = [0, 0, 0, 0];   // solver scratch: particles 0..np-1, then the FIXED EYE at slot 3 (the cap np <= 3 keeps the eye clear of every particle slot)
  function flailClear(f, a, b, margin) {      // push the chord a->b out of the own disc (a = -1: the fixed eye)
    const cx = f.pos.x, cy = f.pos.y;
    const ax = a < 0 ? FL_X[3] : FL_X[a], ay = a < 0 ? FL_Y[3] : FL_Y[a];
    const ex = FL_X[b] - ax, ey = FL_Y[b] - ay, e2 = ex * ex + ey * ey;
    let t = e2 > 1e-9 ? ((cx - ax) * ex + (cy - ay) * ey) / e2 : 0;
    t = t < 0 ? 0 : t > 1 ? 1 : t;
    const qx = ax + ex * t - cx, qy = ay + ey * t - cy;
    const d = Math.sqrt(qx * qx + qy * qy), deficit = CFG.bodyR + margin - d;
    if (deficit <= 0) return;
    const nx = d > 1e-9 ? qx / d : 1, ny = d > 1e-9 ? qy / d : 0;
    if (a < 0) {
      if (t < 0.2) return;
      FL_X[b] += nx * deficit / t; FL_Y[b] += ny * deficit / t; return;
    }
    const s2 = (1 - t) * (1 - t) + t * t;
    FL_X[a] += nx * deficit * (1 - t) / s2; FL_Y[a] += ny * deficit * (1 - t) / s2;
    FL_X[b] += nx * deficit * t / s2; FL_Y[b] += ny * deficit * t / s2;
  }
  function flailStep(f, sdt) {
    const W = WEAPONS[f.weapon], ch = W.chain, F = f.fl, np = ch.np;
    const mul = chainGrow(f.weapon, f.lenStep);   // longchain-r86: grown pitches — the rods solve to exactly what the pose and the frames read
    const fr = spineFrame(f.pos.x, f.pos.y, f.wAngle, f.weapon);
    FL_X[3] = fr.ox + fr.dx * ch.j[0]; FL_Y[3] = fr.oy + fr.dy * ch.j[0];            // the eye, on the current pose
    const g = CFG.gravity * sdt, damp = Math.max(0, 1 - CFG.flailDrag * sdt);
    for (let i = 0; i < np; i++) {
      F.qx[i] = F.x[i]; F.qy[i] = F.y[i];
      F.vy[i] += g;
      FL_X[i] = F.x[i] + F.vx[i] * sdt; FL_Y[i] = F.y[i] + F.vy[i] * sdt;
    }
    const rB = 19;                                                                   // the head keeps its own radius clear of the disc (margin on the centre distance; the old `CFG.bodyR + 19 - CFG.bodyR` self-cancelled — written as the plain margin it is)
    for (let it = 0; it < 8; it++) {
      for (let k = 0; k < np; k++) flailRod(FL_X, FL_Y, k - 1, k, ch.len[k] * mul, ch.iw);
      for (let k = 0; k < np; k++) flailClear(f, k - 1, k, k === np - 1 ? rB : 12);  // the head chord keeps the fat margin, inner chords 12
    }
    for (let k = 0; k < np; k++) flailRod(FL_X, FL_Y, k - 1, k, ch.len[k] * mul, ch.iw);   // final exact pass: every pitch is rigid on the drawn frame (at the grown length)
    const jd = Math.max(0, 1 - CFG.flailJoint * sdt);
    for (let i = 0; i < np; i++) {
      F.x[i] = FL_X[i]; F.y[i] = FL_Y[i];
      const vx = (FL_X[i] - F.qx[i]) / sdt, vy = (FL_Y[i] - F.qy[i]) / sdt;
      const rx = f.vel.x - f.spin * (FL_Y[i] - f.pos.y), ry = f.vel.y + f.spin * (FL_X[i] - f.pos.x);   // where this particle would be if the chain rode the spinning weapon rigidly
      F.vx[i] = (rx + (vx - rx) * jd) * damp;                  // hinge friction: motion RELATIVE to the weapon frame bleeds off (the chain re-streams after a whip) …
      F.vy[i] = (ry + (vy - ry) * jd) * damp;                  // … air drag on top: the small steady trailing lean
    }
    // chain pose in SPINE-LOCAL unit directions: what bladeCircles, the renderer and the events carry
    let ax = FL_X[3], ay = FL_Y[3];
    for (let k = 0; k < np; k++) {
      const dx = F.x[k] - ax, dy = F.y[k] - ay, d = Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) || 1;
      const wx = dx / d, wy = dy / d;
      F.u[2 * k] = wx * fr.dx + wy * fr.dy;                // d component
      F.u[2 * k + 1] = -wx * fr.dy + wy * fr.dx;           // l component
      ax = F.x[k]; ay = F.y[k];
    }
  }

  function wallHit(G, f, iv, x, y) {
    if (f.wallCd > 0) return;
    f.wallCd = CFG.wallEventCd;
    emit(G, 'wall', { by: f.slot, x: x, y: y, intensity: Math.min(1, iv / 1600) });
  }

  function boundary(G, f) {
    const half = CFG.size / 2, r = CFG.bodyR;
    const dx = f.pos.x - half, dy = f.pos.y - half;
    const d = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1e-9;
    if (d + r <= half) return;
    const nx = dx / d, ny = dy / d;
    f.pos.x = half + nx * (half - r);
    f.pos.y = half + ny * (half - r);
    const vn = f.vel.x * nx + f.vel.y * ny;
    if (vn > 0) {
      f.vel.x -= (1 + CFG.wallRest) * vn * nx;
      f.vel.y -= (1 + CFG.wallRest) * vn * ny;
      wallHit(G, f, vn, f.pos.x, f.pos.y);
    }
    if (ny > 0.5 && f.vel.y > -CFG.floorMinBounce) f.vel.y = -CFG.floorMinBounce;
  }

  function bodyCollide(G, a, b) {
    if (!a.alive || !b.alive) return;
    const dx = b.pos.x - a.pos.x, dy = b.pos.y - a.pos.y;
    const d = Math.hypot(dx, dy);
    const rr = CFG.bodyR * 2;
    if (d <= 0 || d >= rr) return;
    const nx = dx / d, ny = dy / d, ov = (rr - d) / 2;
    a.pos.x -= nx * ov; a.pos.y -= ny * ov;
    b.pos.x += nx * ov; b.pos.y += ny * ov;
    const rv = (a.vel.x - b.vel.x) * nx + (a.vel.y - b.vel.y) * ny;
    if (rv <= 0) return;
    a.vel.x -= rv * nx; a.vel.y -= rv * ny;
    b.vel.x += rv * nx; b.vel.y += rv * ny;
    if (rv > 60 && G.bounceT !== G.t) { G.bounceT = G.t; emit(G, 'bounce', { x: a.pos.x + nx * CFG.bodyR, y: a.pos.y + ny * CFG.bodyR, intensity: Math.min(1, rv / 1600) }); }   // v0.8-step1b: once per tick (was per substep: event churn fed GC pauses that read as slow-motion in the preview)
  }

  /* growth: fighter skill + weapon trait, both on every damaging hit — one shared block
   * for blade hits and shot landings alike. Spin is bounded by CFG.omegaCap (dormant
   * today); damage is uncapped; length advances one pre-baked ladder step and stops at
   * the UNIFORM ladder top (LEN_STEPS — per-fighter caps were retired with skill.lenSteps
   * at nocombo-r34, owner no-combos ruling), which is the de facto ceiling; there is no
   * lenCap constant. All three axes reset with the round, by owner law. */
  function grow(G, f) {
    const sk = FIGHTERS[f.idx].skill, ab = WEAPONS[f.weapon].trait;
    const spinGain = sk.spin + ab.spin;
    const dmgGain = sk.dmg + ab.dmg;
    if (spinGain) {
      const dir = f.spin < 0 ? -1 : 1;
      f.spin = dir * Math.min(CFG.omegaCap, Math.abs(f.spin) + spinGain);
      if (f.skew) f.skew.spinBase = (f.skew.spinBase < 0 ? -1 : 1) * Math.min(CFG.omegaCap, Math.abs(f.skew.spinBase) + spinGain);   // skewer-r46: growth landed while impaled goes to the RESTORED spin, not to the crawl
    }
    if (dmgGain) f.dmg += dmgGain;
    /* length growth (the spear's trait, owner 2026-10-28). The RATE is a weapon-row field, so
     * under M2 that half is data and needs no hook. The CAP is UNIFORM (LEN_STEPS) since
     * nocombo-r34 (2026-10-31): the per-fighter cap from `skill.lenSteps` was retired with the
     * owner's no-combos ruling — a skill may add on a shared axis, never reach into a trait's
     * mechanics. Clamped at the ladder top because past it there is no baked geometry, and the
     * inscription-gate proof only covers the ladder's range. */
    if (ab.len && f.lenStep < LEN_STEPS) f.lenStep++;
    /* shot-radius growth (the staff's trait, shotgrow-r33, owner pick 2026-10-31). UNCAPPED by
     * design: growth-uncapped is the doctrine, the arena rim is the physical wall (rim death
     * reads dr + st.r) and the per-round reset in rollWeapons is the balance bound — the same
     * philosophy as the spear's "no lenCap". For every row without shotR this never fires, so
     * f.shotStep stays 0 and the birth radius is exactly W.shot.r (pow(x, 0) === 1). For the
     * staff the trigger was born as the orb landing alone (under the retired projectile rule a
     * launcher's shot landings were its only damaging hits); since allcut-r62 EVERY damaging hit
     * — spine touches included — advances the shared counter, which is exactly the owner's aim:
     * launchers gain growth in the early melee they used to only survive. */
    if (ab.shotR || ab.cycle || ab.mult || ab.fan || (WEAPONS[f.weapon].shot && WEAPONS[f.weapon].shot.hex)) f.shotStep++;   // returngrow-r37: the shared counter serves every shot-growth axis (bendspark-r61: the wand's bend joins it) — hexfam-r68: the gate's ab.turn term RETIRES with the axis and shot.hex takes its place: the FAMILY FLIGHT LAW is itself a growth axis (the hex deepens off this counter), so every spell row feeds it — for the wand the gate opens on exactly the same hits as before (bit-identical counter timeline); the scroll joins the counter for the first time (its hex must deepen too). cycle caps at READ time (CYCLE_STEPS), shotR stays uncapped (the rim is its wall)
    G.stats.hits++;
  }

  function bladeVsBody(G, a) {
    if (!a.alive || a.figT > 0) return;   // bloom-r73 — a bloomed weapon cuts nothing
    const b = G.fighters[1 - a.slot];
    if (!b.alive) return;
    const gap = bladeBodyGap(bladeCircles(a.pos.x, a.pos.y, a.wAngle, a.weapon, a.slot === 0 ? C0 : C1, a.fl.u, leadFlip(a.weapon, a.spin), a.lenStep), b.pos.x, b.pos.y);
    if (a.bladeStuck) {
      /* DEEP-DISENGAGE GATE (law 4's re-arm-side sanctioned extension, owner
       * option 1 2026-10-23 "do 1"; the trigger side — one damage per touch —
       * is unchanged). reArmPad clearance alone let a rocked blade machine-gun
       * fresh legal hits (seed 24267: 3 hits in 95 ticks — "looks very ugly").
       * Re-arm now needs pad clearance AND either a genuine disengagement
       * (peak clearance since the latch >= reArmDeep 85px — above the whole
       * middle band: the episode rocks 69–79px peaks, naturals' genuine
       * re-hits clear >=91px fast / >=120px typical) or reArmWait 90 ticks out
       * (a rocked or hovering blade re-hits at most once per 0.75s — a poke
       * rhythm, never a buzzsaw). Peak is updated BEFORE the check so a
       * single-substep exit that blows straight through the band still re-arms
       * on the spot. A buried blade can never re-arm (clear > pad fails), so a
       * latched touch stays exactly one touch. The damage gate rode the latch —
       * even the knock-only contacts of the retired projectile rule (allcut-r62:
       * every touch cuts now) obeyed it identically; solidity is untouched — the resolver runs every substep
       * regardless, this gates EVENTS only, the same division of labour as law
       * 2's parryGate. measure.mjs's law-4 replica mirrors this exact block. */
      const clear = gap - CFG.bodyR;
      if (clear > a.bladeClearPeak) a.bladeClearPeak = clear;
      if (clear > CFG.reArmPad && (a.bladeClearPeak >= CFG.reArmDeep || G.t - a.bladeLatchTick >= CFG.reArmWait)) a.bladeStuck = false;
      return;
    }
    if (gap >= CFG.bodyR) return;
    a.bladeStuck = true;
    a.bladeLatchTick = G.t; a.bladeClearPeak = 0;

    /* ALLCUT — EVERY weapon cuts on body touch (owner ruling 2026-11-02: "all
     * weapons from now on deals damage if they touch the opponets body… i
     * realized launchers are boring to watch in the beginning as they have a
     * hard time hitting the opponents and gaining growth"). This RETIRES the
     * PROJECTILE-WEAPON rule (owner decision 2026-10-19: "ranged weapons
     * (shooting projectiles), their weapons do not damage, only their
     * projetiles" — which restated and widened the v0.7.2 tangential-only rule
     * of 2026-10-17) AND its last remnant, the shield's tangential no-damage
     * clause ("parries only" — open question 4 answered in mechanism; its
     * balance question stays open). The knock-only contact class is GONE: every
     * fresh latched touch is a damaging hit — HP, knock, hitstop, flash, the
     * hit event and grow() — for launchers and the shield exactly as for melee.
     * The contact stays solid on the same re-arm latch as ever (law 3's
     * solidity — bodies cannot walk through the spine). The projectile remains
     * the launcher's growth ENGINE but is no longer its only damage. Disclosed,
     * not balanced (#674): launcher spines chip at the base WDEF dmg 1 in
     * close, waking every dormant launcher-side trigger — the shield's
     * trait.dmg 0.7 fires for the first time ever, the wand's bend deepens on
     * spine touches too, and shield+shield loses its cannot-KO stall. Blade-vs-
     * blade parries and swats are untouched. measure.mjs law 4's replica
     * mirrors the gate-free law; its law 7s is RETIRED with the rule (edited
     * per the owner-go rule, never run here). */
    const kx = b.pos.x - a.pos.x, ky = b.pos.y - a.pos.y;
    const kd = Math.hypot(kx, ky) || 1;
    b.vel.x += (kx / kd) * CFG.hitKnock;
    b.vel.y += (ky / kd) * CFG.hitKnock;
    const dealt = a.dmg;
    b.hp = Math.max(0, b.hp - dealt);
    grow(G, a);
    if (a.weapon === 'wand' && WEAPONS.wand.trait.fig > 0) tryFig(G, WEAPONS.wand, a, b);   // bloom-r73 — the spine touch blooms too (allcut: every touch is a wand hit)

    const kill = b.hp <= 0;
    if (kill) { b.alive = false; b.deathSeq = ++G.deathSeq; }
    const hev = {
      by: a.slot, to: b.slot, dealt: dealt, kill: kill,
      x: b.pos.x, y: b.pos.y,                                   // victim at the contact instant
      aFl: a.fl.u.slice(),                                      // chain pose of the attacker (flail; harmless 6-array for rigid weapons) — the audit passes it to bladeCircles
      ax: a.pos.x, ay: a.pos.y, aAng: a.wAngle, aW: a.weapon,   // contact pose: the renderer re-draws this exact pose as the flash silhouette; the audit proves the blade touches (x, y) in it
      spin: Math.abs(a.spin), dmg: a.dmg,
    };
    if (WEAPONS[a.weapon].lead || WEAPONS[a.weapon].headLead) hev.aSp = a.spin;               // edge-leading (owner 2026-10-22): the SIGNED spin at contact — audits and stills derive the mirror via leadFlip(aW, aSp). Flagged weapons only, so unflagged event JSON stays byte-identical (surgical fingerprints)
    emit(G, 'hit', hev);
  }

  /* ---- blade-vs-blade: the core contact law's solid pair (2026-10-16) ----
   * Runs EVERY substep — no cooldown may skip it (the v0.5.1 cooldown skip
   * was the tunneling ghost window: 100% of measured interpenetration lived
   * inside it). Three jobs per substep, in order:
   *   1. latch release — once the blades clear parryPad AND the flutter gate
   *      (law 2's named re-arm gate, owner option 1 2026-10-21) has expired,
   *      the next touch is fresh again (hysteresis; same pattern as
   *      bladeStuck/reArmPad);
   *   2. resolver — any overlap is pushed out along the TRUE contact normal
   *      (bodies move, weapons ride rigidly), then body-vs-body and arena
   *      are re-honoured position-only, and the approaching velocity is
   *      killed: rendered frames never show interpenetration;
   *   3. parry — a fresh exact touch (entry gap <= 0, rising edge of the
   *      latch) flips BOTH spins (rule 5), shoves the bodies apart and emits
   *      the event with the ENTRY poses, so the audit can recompute the touch
   *      from exactly what triggered it. Every fresh contact is one parry;
   *      the latch — not a timer — prevents re-fires during a sustained
   *      press; the only other gate is the flutter gate on the RE-ARM (a
   *      named law-2 extension: inside it the pair stays solid, no parry). */
  /* Clinch spring (bind-prevention 2026-10-27, owner eyes-first): while the
   * blade latch stays shut — blades inside the pad, a sustained interlock —
   * a separation force ramps zero->full over CFG.clinchRamp ticks
   * (smoothstep: no onset jerk) and pushes the two bodies apart along their
   * own axis; it fades over clinchDecay once the blades clear. A force,
   * never an impulse: the bind pushes itself apart for exactly as long as
   * it exists, and open-space play (latch open, clinchT 0) feels nothing.
   * The locked blades are the visible cause of the push — attributable,
   * same ramp every time, no snapping, no warping. */
  function clinchForce(G, f, sdt) {
    const L = G.clinchT / CFG.clinchRamp;
    if (L <= 0) return;
    const o = G.fighters[1 - f.slot];
    if (!o.alive) return;
    const dx = f.pos.x - o.pos.x, dy = f.pos.y - o.pos.y;
    const d = Math.hypot(dx, dy);
    if (d < 1e-9) return;
    const sm = L * L * (3 - 2 * L);
    /* bindfix-r35: while the latch is shut the spring never starts from ~zero —
     * the floor is what makes a fresh vertical/rim stack push out in ~10-15
     * ticks instead of waiting for the ramp to mature past the press. Once the
     * latch releases this reads the pure ramp again, so the fade is unchanged. */
    const a = G.clash ? Math.max(CFG.clinchAcc * sm, CFG.clinchFloor) : CFG.clinchAcc * sm;
    f.vel.x += (dx / d) * a * sdt; f.vel.y += (dy / d) * a * sdt;
  }
  function clampToArenaPos(f) {
    const half = CFG.size / 2, r = CFG.bodyR;
    const dx = f.pos.x - half, dy = f.pos.y - half;
    const d = Math.hypot(dx, dy);
    if (d > 1e-9 && d + r > half) {
      const s = (half - r) / d;
      f.pos.x = half + dx * s; f.pos.y = half + dy * s;
    }
  }
  function separateBodiesPos(a, b) {
    const dx = b.pos.x - a.pos.x, dy = b.pos.y - a.pos.y;
    const d = Math.hypot(dx, dy);
    if (d > 1e-9 && d < CFG.bodyR * 2) {
      const ov = (CFG.bodyR * 2 - d) / 2, ux = dx / d, uy = dy / d;
      a.pos.x -= ux * ov; a.pos.y -= uy * ov;
      b.pos.x += ux * ov; b.pos.y += uy * ov;
    }
  }
  function bladeVsBlade(G) {
    const a = G.fighters[0], b = G.fighters[1];
    if (!a.alive || !b.alive) return;
    if (a.figT > 0 || b.figT > 0) return;   // bloom-r73 — a joke object parries nothing and is parried by nothing (the pair goes solid-free: no latch, no clinch)
    _pA.x = a.pos.x; _pA.y = a.pos.y; _pA.ang = a.wAngle; _pA.w = a.weapon; _pA.fl = a.fl.u; _pA.fp = leadFlip(a.weapon, a.spin); _pA.ls = a.lenStep;
    _pB.x = b.pos.x; _pB.y = b.pos.y; _pB.ang = b.wAngle; _pB.w = b.weapon; _pB.fl = b.fl.u; _pB.fp = leadFlip(b.weapon, b.spin); _pB.ls = b.lenStep;
    const pg = parryGap(_pA, _pB);
    const egap = pg.gap;                      // entry (pre-resolution) gap — the trigger's truth
    /* Latch release: blades clear of the pad AND the flutter gate expired.
     * Inside the gate (16 ticks from the last fired parry, owner option 1
     * 2026-10-21 — law 2's named re-arm gate) the latch stays shut: the pair
     * remains fully solid below (resolver + approach-velocity kill) but no
     * parry fires — the vibrato burst becomes clang-bind-separate. Legit
     * re-clangs sit at p10 81 ticks, five times above the gate. */
    if (egap > CFG.parryPad && G.t - G.parryT >= CFG.parryGate) { G.clash = false; return; }   // clear of the latch margin (prune returns Infinity)
    // entry poses + contact point, captured before the resolver moves anything
    const eax = a.pos.x, eay = a.pos.y, ebx = b.pos.x, eby = b.pos.y, ex = pg.x, ey = pg.y;
    const eaa = a.wAngle, eba = b.wAngle;   // entry ANGLES, pre-resolver: the pin nudge must not rewrite the pose the audit recomputes
    const eas = a.spin, ebs = b.spin;       // entry SPINS, signed and pre-flip: the edge-leading mirror the audit recomputes is the ENTRY one (the parry's recoil flips them after this capture)

    if (egap < 0) {
      /* resolver, v0.8-step1: MULTI-CONTACT accumulation. A single deepest
       * pair jams whenever two contacts carry opposing normals — a blade
       * wedged in a concave mouth, or two wide heads crossing in an X (the
       * axe's failure mode at the step-1 baseline: 9.9px rendered depth,
       * seeds 7/8). Each iteration pushes along the overlap-weighted sum of
       * ALL contacting circle pairs; opposed laterals cancel and the axial
       * components add, which is exactly the direction that opens scissors.
       * Single-contact cases reduce to the old behaviour (sum = deepest).
       * Iteration cap stays for the pathological wall-pin (GAMES.md caveat). */
      /* v0.8-step1b perf: one prefiltered sequential-impulse loop. The old
       * loop re-ran parryGap (a second full circle-pair scan) every iteration
       * — during a sustained clash at high spin that made clash ticks the
       * hottest code in the sim and the browser frame budget slipped into
       * slow-motion (owner report, seed 69737). The sequential pass already
       * knows its deepest contact; it IS the gap. Axis prefilter skips the
       * hypot for every pair that cannot reach. */
      let gap = egap, nx = pg.nx, ny = pg.ny, gapPrev = egap, nudged = false;
      /* adaptive iterations (v0.8-step1d; stall test corrected 2026-10-28):
       * progress is `deep` RISING toward 0, so a stall is `deep - gapPrev <
       * 0.02`; the old `> -0.02` fired on convergence, always exiting after two
       * passes. A stall is NOT an infeasible pin but this translation-only
       * loop's fixed point (~10px); the nudge adds the rotation it lacks. */
      for (let iter = 0; iter < 16 && gap < 0; iter++) {
        bladeCircles(a.pos.x, a.pos.y, a.wAngle, a.weapon, D0, a.fl.u, leadFlip(a.weapon, a.spin), a.lenStep);
        bladeCircles(b.pos.x, b.pos.y, b.wAngle, b.weapon, D1, b.fl.u, leadFlip(b.weapon, b.spin), b.lenStep);
        let daX = 0, daY = 0, dbX = 0, dbY = 0, deep = 0, tqA = 0, tqB = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < D0.length; i += 3) {
          const ra = D0[i + 2];
          for (let j = 0; j < D1.length; j += 3) {
            const sum = ra + D1[j + 2];
            const dx0 = D1[j] - D0[i], dy0 = D1[j + 1] - D0[i + 1];
            if (dx0 > sum || dx0 < -sum || dy0 > sum || dy0 < -sum) continue;
            const ax = D0[i] + daX, ay = D0[i + 1] + daY;
            const bx = D1[j] + dbX, by = D1[j + 1] + dbY;
            const dx = bx - ax, dy = by - ay;
            const dc = Math.hypot(dx, dy);
            const d = dc - sum;
            if (d >= 0) continue;
            const ux = dc > 1e-9 ? dx / dc : 0, uy = dc > 1e-9 ? dy / dc : -1;
            const ov = -d * 0.4;
            daX -= ux * ov; daY -= uy * ov;
            dbX += ux * ov; dbY += uy * ov;
            // contact torque about each body: the rotation the push demands
            tqA += (ax - a.pos.x) * -uy - (ay - a.pos.y) * -ux;
            tqB += (bx - b.pos.x) * uy - (by - b.pos.y) * ux;
            if (d < deep) { deep = d; nx = ux; ny = uy; }
          }
        }
        a.pos.x += daX; a.pos.y += daY;
        b.pos.x += dbX; b.pos.y += dbY;
        separateBodiesPos(a, b);
        clampToArenaPos(a); clampToArenaPos(b);
        gap = deep;
        if (deep === 0) { nx = pg.nx; ny = pg.ny; break; }
        if (deep - gapPrev < 0.02) {
          if (!nudged && deep < -1) {
            nudged = true;
            // pin escape along the contact torque's own direction (disclosed):
            // rotation is the only free DOF while both bodies stay solid.
            // bindfix-r35: inside a LATCHED bind the escape rotates WITH each
            // weapon's own orbit (sign of its spin), never against it. The live
            // torque sign sawtooths in a symmetric X-cross (crossbow bow-arms ×
            // a shaft: the deepest contacting pair alternates sides tick to tick
            // — measured ±0.046 rad/tick against a spin·dt of 0.046, net rotation
            // ZERO, the crossed weapons visibly freeze and vibrate: owner seed
            // 32542), and a torque sign captured ONCE per episode can latch the
            // WRONG scissor direction and hold a bind for 384 ticks (measured in
            // the variant sweep). Spin-aligned, the nudge ADDS to the orbit so
            // the cross rotates open at up to twice the orbit rate. Unlatched
            // deep wedges (transient pins; the knock-only class retired
            // at allcut-r62) keep the physical torque sign.
            let sa = tqA !== 0 ? Math.sign(tqA) : (a.spin > 0 ? 1 : -1);
            let sb = tqB !== 0 ? Math.sign(tqB) : (b.spin > 0 ? 1 : -1);
            if (G.clash) { sa = a.spin > 0 ? 1 : -1; sb = b.spin > 0 ? 1 : -1; }
            // depth-scaled: a 25px burial needs a bigger rotational kick than a
            // 2px one; capped in px-at-the-head (nudgePx / REACH) and gated to
            // ONE add per tick per fighter (owner 2026-10-21): the old uncapped
            // teleport read as a ~36px one-frame warp, so cap+gate spread the
            // escape over ~3-12 ticks. It does NOT hold burial sub-ink — measured
            // 20.754px / 14.673px, both visible past the 3px outline (2026-10-28):
            // the nudge rotates but a translation-only loop cannot pull crossed
            // blades apart. Stalls only, so no grapple feed (reverted whip).
            const nzBase = 0.15 + (-deep) * 0.02;
            if (a.nudgeTick !== G.t) { a.nudgeTick = G.t; a.wAngle += sa * Math.min(0.6, nzBase, CFG.nudgePx / REACH[a.weapon]); }
            if (b.nudgeTick !== G.t) { b.nudgeTick = G.t; b.wAngle += sb * Math.min(0.6, nzBase, CFG.nudgePx / REACH[b.weapon]); }
            gapPrev = deep;
            continue;
          }
          break;
        }
        gapPrev = deep;
      }
      // kill the approaching velocity along the contact normal (equal masses)
      const rv = (a.vel.x - b.vel.x) * nx + (a.vel.y - b.vel.y) * ny;
      if (rv > 0) {
        a.vel.x -= rv * 0.5 * nx; a.vel.y -= rv * 0.5 * ny;
        b.vel.x += rv * 0.5 * nx; b.vel.y += rv * 0.5 * ny;
      }
    }

    if (G.clash || egap > 0) return;          // sustained press or near-miss inside the margin: solid, but no parry
    G.clash = true;                           // fresh exact touch — this IS the parry
    G.parryT = G.t;                           // flutter gate: the re-arm clock starts now (law 2's named gate)
    a.spin = -a.spin; b.spin = -b.spin;       // rule 5: both weapons recoil
    const nx = b.pos.x - a.pos.x, ny = b.pos.y - a.pos.y;
    const nd = Math.hypot(nx, ny) || 1;
    const keep = 1 - CFG.parryCarryKill;                 // the clang absorbs the flight: what leaves the clang is shove + reversed orbit, legible at the clang
    a.vel.x *= keep; a.vel.y *= keep; b.vel.x *= keep; b.vel.y *= keep;
    a.vel.x -= (nx / nd) * CFG.parryPush; a.vel.y -= (ny / nd) * CFG.parryPush;
    b.vel.x += (nx / nd) * CFG.parryPush; b.vel.y += (ny / nd) * CFG.parryPush;
    G.stats.parries++;
    const pev = {
      x: ex, y: ey,                                            // true contact point (deepest circle pair) at the touch frame
      ax: eax, ay: eay, aAng: eaa, aW: a.weapon,          // ENTRY poses of both blades — the audit recomputes gap <= 0 from exactly these
      bx: ebx, by: eby, bAng: eba, bW: b.weapon,
      aFl: a.fl.u.slice(), bFl: b.fl.u.slice(),                // entry chain poses (flail): the resolver never changes them, only the bodies move
      spin0: a.spin, spin1: b.spin,                            // signed post-flip spins — the spin-law audit reads the recoil off the event itself
    };
    if (WEAPONS[a.weapon].lead || WEAPONS[a.weapon].headLead) pev.aSp = eas;                 // entry spin signs for the edge-leading mirror (flagged weapons only — unflagged event JSON byte-identical). ENTRY, not spin0: the audit recomputes the touch the blades made BEFORE the recoil flipped them
    if (WEAPONS[b.weapon].lead || WEAPONS[b.weapon].headLead) pev.bSp = ebs;
    emit(G, 'parry', pev);
  }

  /* ---- projectiles (v0.7 as the sling's shot; generalised v0.9–v1.0 into
   * the shot system; owner decisions 2026-10-16/17/19) ----
   * Firing: one release per full revolution — spin rate IS fire rate, no
   * cooldown and no ammo stat.
   * LAUNCH-POINT doctrine (owner decision 2026-10-19: "when the weapon is
   * radial, shoot from the tip, when it is the opposite, shoot from the
   * middle, like bow and crossbow"): a RADIAL-hold launcher releases at the
   * spine TIP (t = 1, staff/wand — 'tip'); a TANGENTIAL-hold launcher
   * releases at the spine MIDDLE (t = 0.5, the grip point on the rim). There
   * the DIRECTION splits per weapon: shooting weapons (bow, crossbow —
   * 'radial') send the shot radially OUT of the grip, offset by shot.off so
   * the head starts at the belly (the nocked arrow's tail on the string) — a
   * bow shoots where its belly faces, not along its limbs; thrown weapons
   * (boomerang, shuriken — no flag) leave tangentially in the spin direction.
   * Every shot carries the thrower's CURRENT dmg at launch (one damage number
   * per fighter) and flies without gravity or drag; the boomerang alone ORBITS, and the spell
   * rows curve on the FAMILY FLIGHT LAW (hexfam-r68 — bornBend derives the bend off shot.hex +
   * the row's speed). Per-shot contact rules (GAMES.md "Projectile weapons"):
   *   - vs enemy body: a damaging hit (law 1); the shot is consumed by it,
   *     so one-damage-per-touch (law 4) is automatic;
   *   - vs enemy blade: SWAT — destroyed, nothing else happens: no parry
   *     event, no spin flip on either fighter (the named rule-5 exception;
   *     readable on the reveal card and in the legend); catchonly-r56: the
   *     returning boomerang is EXEMPT — the loop is immune to swats (owner:
   *     "i want the boomerang to be immune to swats"), blades pass through it;
   *   - vs rim: dies (law 1 — walls never damage); the sanctioned exceptions
   *     are the shuriken star's ETERNAL RICOCHET (shot.ricochet, ricolaw-r41 —
   *     the rim never kills a star; it mirrors forever at row speed), the
   *     boomerang's pierce (shot.returns, freeloop-r38 — it flies past the
   *     wall and loops home back through it), and the crossbow's NAIL
   *     (shot.pin, pinlaw-r44 — the bolt sticks just inside the rim as a shot
   *     AT REST: the foe's body touch is the law-4 hit that consumes it, the
   *     foe's blade swats it off, an enemy shot crosses it out, the OWNER
   *     walks through his own nails, and the roll clears them);
   *   - vs another shot: both cancel — ENEMY shots only (multgrow-r42, owner
   *     ruling 2026-11-01, option A): owner-blindness is game-wide — a shot
   *     never crosses its OWN side's shots, period; friendly fire does not
   *     exist; the returning boomerang is the standing exemption, one-sided
   *     since snapfix-r57 (owner: "i want other projectiles hitting the
   *     boomerang to be destroyed, but not the boomerang"): an enemy
   *     projectile that touches the loop DIES on it while the loop flies on;
   *     loop vs loop is a normal BOTH-DIE cross again (catchghost-r58, owner:
   *     "what happens if both bots have boomerang and they collide? i want them
   *     to both get destroyed" — r56's mutual pass reversed), triggered arc
   *     against arc; blades still pass through the loop with no effect at
   *     all (the swat test skips it). (History: ricolaw-r41 exempted own-star pairs for the swarm;
   *     multgrow-r42 generalized the exemption when the bow's rain made
   *     same-owner crossings a self-annihilation pathology);
   *   - vs its OWNER (returning shots only): catchonly-r56 — the catch is
   *     BACK (nocatch-r55 reverted at the owner's eye: "no it look bad,
   *     revert it") and it is now the ONLY thing that ends a returning
   *     flight: PURE TOUCH on the drawn arc (touchorbit-r53 window,
   *     chaosorbit-r54 arc read), armed once the throw has cleared the body
   *     with BOTH the pivot disc and the arc by CATCH_ARM — the arc-aware arm
   *     is what killed the departure-tick self-catch the owner caught by eye
   *     ("the boomerang was immediately consumed when it was thrown"). The
   *     cycle-growth step rides the catch again; the banked spin rethrows
   *     instantly after it (RETHROW_WAIT 0, instantthrow-r59 — the r54
   *     hand-rest dormant in the constant);
   *   - no friendly fire: a shot is never tested against its owner's body,
   *     blade or SHOTS (owner-blindness, the last extended by multgrow-r42),
   *     so it can never self-destruct, self-swat or self-cross —
   *     the catch above is the sanctioned exception, and it deals nothing;
   *   - law 3 turns asymmetric: a shot has no body behind it to push, so it
   *     LOSES every collision (destroyed, never separated) and never overlaps
   *     blade, body, rim or another shot on a rendered frame — detection
   *     guaranteed by the projectile substep budget in stepPhysics.
   * Drawn shape vs hitbox: disc-shaped shots are drawn at exactly shot.r;
   * arrows/bolts (shot.len, kept as fingerprint-hashed flight state) trail behind the
   * hitbox circle, which sits at the head. The returning boomerang is the third case
   * (chaosorbit-r54): the copy art's OWN covering circles (boomCircles) are the hitbox —
   * body, blade, cross and catch all read the drawn arc, so what the eye sees is what touches.
   * VOCABULARY (renamed 2026-10-28 at owner word "renmae now"; the old generic
   * was 'stone', a legacy of the removed sling): the sim-level name for any
   * projectile is 'shot' — G.shots, G.shotSid, G.auditShots, the
   * shotFire/shotRim/shotCross events, W.shot data, the hit event's shot:true
   * flag — which now MATCHES the audience word, so one concept carries one name
   * through every layer. Per-shot on-screen names stay (arrow, bolt, knife, orb,
   * spark, boomerang, star, javelin, page, scroll) via shot.what. The old
   * 'stone' vocabulary survives only in dated records (CHRONICLE-archive.md, the
   * 2026-10-28 chainlaw output, GAMES.md's dated entries) and in the frozen bench
   * page's snapshots — that page left the tree at the 2026-10-28 checkpoint clean
   * (the owner holds a copy; its generator and smoke stay, dormant) and it was
   * never hand-edited. Behaviour-identical: no stamp bump; the
   * fingerprints re-baselined (.qa/fp-pause-after.json -> .qa/fp-shotvocab.json)
   * because event keys are hash inputs, with neutrality proven by identical
   * cellscan/natscan/projectile-fix numbers. */
  const CS = [];          // foe-blade circle scratch for shot tests

  /* LAUNCHER CONSOLIDATION (2026-10-28, owner-approved pre-skills cleanup): KNIFE_VOLLEY,
   * SPELL_CYCLE and COPYW are gone, and with them the last four `f.weapon === ...` tests in
   * fireShots. The launcher is now data-driven through W.shot: `revs` (revolutions per
   * volley, default 1), `volley` ([d, l, degrees] anchors, WORLD px — see the knives row:
   * deliberately outside the weaponScale loop), `cycle` (kind rotation, state f.cycleIdx)
   * and `copy` (spawn at the art centre). Per-weapon shot behaviour now lives on the row
   * next to its trait, which is where the skills pass will read it. Behaviour-identical:
   * fingerprints 8/8 unchanged, and cellscan / natscan / projectile-fix numbers unchanged. */
  /* fan-r43 (the knives' GROWING FAN, owner rulings 2026-11-01: "the knives sounds good, try and
   * do that first" + eye-approve of the rate-0.5 probe, "it looks good already implement it"): the
   * row's static 3-anchor volley is the tier-0 form; each fan tier adds ONE knife per side,
   * launched from that side's outer anchor, spread ±(22 + k*FAN_SPREAD) degrees. Tier
   * t = min(floor(shotStep * trait.fan), FAN_STEPS) — quantized so every growth is a visible step.
   * Rows without trait.fan get the row array ITSELF back — bit-identical; the volley branch is
   * knives-only, so no other launcher's cadence, geometry or hashes are touched. The row's three
   * anchors are never mutated (the static fan identity — the bow owns the stream, the knives the fan). */
  /* bendspark-r61 → hexfam-r68 — THE BEND's ONE consumer site: the birth turn of a spell. THE
   * FAMILY FLIGHT LAW (owner ruling 2026-11-02: "from now on all magic/spell users should adopt
   * the same mechanig as wand currently have, it looks good"): the bend is no longer the wand's
   * trait — it is what MAGIC DOES. Every shot.hex row derives the SAME ladder off its own speed:
   * (HEXFAM.base + HEXFAM.grow × min(f.shotStep, TURN_STEPS)) × speed ÷ HEXFAM.ref — the wand's
   * blessed r62/r65 numbers ARE the standard (ref = the wand's 800 ⇒ the wand stays
   * BIT-IDENTICAL, k = 1 exactly), and the radius language is speed-independent: every spell
   * births on the ~889px arc and hunts down to the ~333px floor. The SIGN is a fresh G.rng roll
   * PER THROW — the pure-chaos doctrine: magic never aims. Non-hex rows (every steel launcher)
   * take the falsy branch: zero turn AND ZERO rng draws, so their streams stay byte-identical
   * (the r61 law, now gated on the family flag). Birth snapshot only — in-flight shots never
   * re-bend (the effR doctrine); the dormant curve branch in shotStep does the rest, and the
   * r65 hex seek splits its authority exactly as before (row-generic since it was written). */
  function bornBend(G, W, f) {
    if (!W.shot.hex) return 0;   // the family gate: steel flies straight; only hexed rows are born bent
    const bend = (HEXFAM.base + HEXFAM.grow * Math.min(f.shotStep, TURN_STEPS)) * (W.shot.speed / HEXFAM.ref);
    return bend * (G.rng() < 0.5 ? -1 : 1);
  }
  /* emberpool-r79 — THE BURNING POOL's clock (per TICK, in the fight step, so the KO freeze holds
   * the fire like every world beat): the pool ticks down; while the foe's centre stands within
   * r + half a body the acc counts to POOL.tick and deals one burn beat (the snapshot dmg), an
   * honest damage beat that can kill — but it is a ZONE, not a hit: no grow, no hex deepening,
   * no slow-mo beat (the poolBurn event is its own punctuation). Expired fires drop in place. */
  function poolStep(G, fs) {
    if (!G.pools.length) return;
    let w = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < G.pools.length; i++) {
      const pl = G.pools[i];
      pl.t -= 1;
      if (pl.t > 0) {
        const foe = fs[1 - pl.o];
        const inside = foe.alive && Math.hypot(foe.pos.x - pl.x, foe.pos.y - pl.y) <= pl.r + CFG.bodyR * POOL.reach;
        if (inside) {
          // burnfix-r84 — THE TOUCH BITE: the damage starts the VERY TICK the body touches the fire (owner: "he starts taking
          // damage as soon as he touches it"); the beat continues every POOL.tick after; leaving re-arms the entry edge, so a
          // re-step is a fresh touch bite. A pool spawned ON the victim by the hit bites its own victim on the spawn tick.
          const fresh = !pl.in;
          pl.in = true;
          if (fresh) pl.acc = 0; else pl.acc += 1;
          if (fresh || pl.acc >= POOL.tick) {
            if (!fresh) pl.acc = 0;
            foe.hp = Math.max(0, foe.hp - pl.dmg);
            G.stats.poolBurns++;
            const kill = foe.hp <= 0;
            if (kill) { foe.alive = false; foe.deathSeq = ++G.deathSeq; }   // a pool kill is an honest kill
            emit(G, 'poolBurn', { by: pl.o, to: foe.slot, x: pl.x, y: pl.y, dealt: pl.dmg, kill: kill });   // emberfix-r85 — the kill flag feeds the KO beat (every kill freezes)
          }
        } else { pl.in = false; pl.acc = 0; }
        G.pools[w++] = pl;
      }
    }
    G.pools.length = w;
  }
  /* kindling-r82 — KINDLING / THE EMBER SPILL's machinery. The spell SHEDS coals in flight:
   * fireShots stamps the birth-snapshot cadence (st.eiv — the effR doctrine: the stacks at the
   * CAST), shotStep counts and calls spawnEmber; each coal snapshots its life/r/dmg AT THE DROP.
   * emberStep ticks the coals down; the foe's centre within r + half a body POPS one — a single
   * honest bite that CONSUMES the coal. THE GROWTH BRAKE (owner law): a pop is a zone event like
   * the pool's burn beat — no grow, no hex deepening, no slow-mo, no counter but its own (the
   * emberPop event is its own punctuation); growth rides the METEOR's hit alone, "otherwise i
   * think it is going to snowball very quickly". Expired coals die in place. */
  function spawnEmber(G, fs, st) {
    const f = fs[st.o];
    const gl = Math.min(f.shotStep, EMBER.steps);
    const an = G.rng() * TAU, sr = EMBER.scatter * Math.sqrt(G.rng());   // kindlingfix-r83 — the coal lands on a RANDOM DISC around the flight point, not in a tail behind it (two row-owned draws at the drop — the bornBend precedent; the sqrt keeps the disc uniform)
    let ex = st.x + Math.cos(an) * sr, ey = st.y + Math.sin(an) * sr;
    const dc = Math.hypot(ex - CFG.size / 2, ey - CFG.size / 2);
    if (dc > CFG.size / 2 - 10) { const k = (CFG.size / 2 - 10) / dc; ex = CFG.size / 2 + (ex - CFG.size / 2) * k; ey = CFG.size / 2 + (ey - CFG.size / 2) * k; }   // rim clamp: no coal may burn off the floor
    G.embers.push({ x: ex, y: ey, r: EMBER.r + EMBER.rAdd * gl, t: EMBER.life + EMBER.lifeAdd * gl, o: f.slot, dmg: Math.max(0.3, f.dmg * POOL.rate * EMBER.rate), glow: gl, eid: ++G.emberSid });
    if (G.embers.length > EMBER.cap) { const out = G.embers.shift(); G.emberFx.push({ x: out.x, y: out.y, t: EMBER.wisp, k: 1 }); }   // the lace guard: oldest coal dies young — and emberfix-r85 makes that death READABLE (the diagnostic: ~85–92% of coals died THIS way, silently, 14–28× per cell under a standing body — his "fell through 3, took 2")
    G.stats.embers++;
    emit(G, 'ember', { by: f.slot, eid: G.emberSid, x: ex, y: ey });
  }
  function emberStep(G, fs) {
    for (let i = G.emberFx.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (--G.emberFx[i].t <= 0) G.emberFx.splice(i, 1);   // kindlingfix-r83 — the pop bursts tick down (visual timers, the figPoof precedent)
    if (!G.embers.length) return;
    let w = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < G.embers.length; i++) {
      const em = G.embers[i];
      const foe = fs[1 - em.o];
      if (foe.alive && Math.hypot(foe.pos.x - em.x, foe.pos.y - em.y) <= em.r + CFG.bodyR * POOL.reach) {
        // emberfix-r85 — THE POP TEST RUNS FIRST, on EVERY tick of the coal's life including its last: the old order
        // decremented before testing, so a coal could expire silently under a standing body on its final tick — a
        // 1-tick hole in "stepping on these does damage" (the diagnostic never caught it firing; the law is the law)
        foe.hp = Math.max(0, foe.hp - em.dmg);
        G.stats.emberPops++;
        const kill = foe.hp <= 0;
        if (kill) { foe.alive = false; foe.deathSeq = ++G.deathSeq; }   // an ember kill is an honest kill
        G.emberFx.push({ x: em.x, y: em.y, t: EMBER.popFx, k: 0 });   // THE BURST — a bite is a VISIBLE event even on a fading coal
        emit(G, 'emberPop', { by: em.o, to: foe.slot, x: em.x, y: em.y, dealt: em.dmg, kill: kill });   // emberfix-r85 — the kill flag feeds the KO beat
        continue;                                   // THE POP consumes the coal — one honest bite and it is gone
      }
      em.t -= 1;
      if (em.t > 0) G.embers[w++] = em;
      else G.emberFx.push({ x: em.x, y: em.y, t: EMBER.wisp, k: 1 });   // emberfix-r85 — THE WISP: died of age, and the death is READABLE (BURST = it bit, WISP = it died)
    }
    G.embers.length = w;
  }
  /* affinity-r66 — the FIRE payload's ONE consumer: the vortex page's birth radius. Linear off the
   * shared counter and CAPPED at TRIO.steps (unlike the staff's uncapped compounding — the trio's wall
   * is the uniform cap, house pattern). Birth snapshot only, like every size axis (the effR doctrine). */
  function trioRadius(W, f, kind) {
    if (AFFINITY[kind] !== 'fire' || !TRIO.fireSwell) return W.shot.r;   // spellform-r69: the FIRE swell sleeps at the owner's shape grammar — all three pages are born the SAME size, colour = which; the rate waits in TRIO.fireGrow behind the fireSwell switch
    return W.shot.r * (1 + TRIO.fireGrow * Math.min(f.shotStep, TRIO.steps));
  }
  function grudgeBirth() { return {}; }   // chillfix-r71: THE LONG GRUDGE reverted whole at the owner's eye (read as tome-like linger); the birth-state helper stays as an empty spread so both spawn sites keep their shape and the revert stays surgical
  function grownVolley(W, f) {
    const rate = W.trait && W.trait.fan;
    if (!rate) return W.shot.volley;
    const t = Math.min(Math.floor(f.shotStep * rate), FAN_STEPS);
    if (t <= 0) return W.shot.volley;
    const v = W.shot.volley.slice();
    const outNeg = W.shot.volley[1], outPos = W.shot.volley[2];   // the ±22° anchors: d-heel and d-tip
    for (let k = 1; k <= t; k++) {
      const deg = 22 + k * FAN_SPREAD;
      v.push([outNeg[0], outNeg[1], -deg], [outPos[0], outPos[1], deg]);
    }
    return v;
  }
  /* touchorbit-r53 — THE THROW SOLVE (the owner's solo prototype, ported near-verbatim): the
   * boomerang's flight is an ARENA-CENTRED ELLIPSE through the release point. a is forced past
   * the release radius (the orbit always reaches beyond the throw — and past the rim on its far
   * arc), b is forced inside it, and of the four (orientation × traversal sense) solutions
   * chaosorbit-r54 draws one AT RANDOM (owner: "i dont want ai aiming, it should be pure
   * randomness, pure chaos" — the touchorbit-r53 best-tangent aim at the foe is retired whole).
   * The per-throw jitter rides G.rng (the sim never touches Math.random) ⇒ an orbit FAMILY,
   * deterministic per seed. The returned spread also overrides vx/vy (the true release tangent)
   * and speed (the honest periapsis maximum speed·peak — the number the law-3 budget, the knock
   * and om all read). */
  function orbitThrow(G, W, x, y, cyc) {
    const half = CFG.size / 2, ob = W.shot.orbit, rng = G.rng;
    const px = x - half, py = y - half;
    const r = Math.max(8, Math.hypot(px, py)), th = Math.atan2(py, px);
    const ea = Math.max(ob.a * (0.92 + 0.08 * rng()), r * 1.04);   // the prototype's jitter bands, verbatim
    const eb = Math.min(ob.b * (0.8 + 0.4 * rng()), r * 0.97);
    const s2 = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (1 / (r * r) - 1 / (ea * ea)) / (1 / (eb * eb) - 1 / (ea * ea))));
    const d0 = Math.asin(Math.sqrt(s2));
    /* chaosorbit-r54 PURE CHAOS: the four solutions (orientation sign × traversal sense) are
     * EQUIPROBABLE on G.rng — the throw never reads the foe. Deterministic per seed like every
     * other draw in the sim. */
    const sg = rng() < 0.5 ? -1 : 1, sense = rng() < 0.5 ? -1 : 1;
    const del = sg * d0, phi = th - del, t0 = Math.atan2(r * Math.sin(del) / eb, r * Math.cos(del) / ea);
    const speed = W.shot.speed * cyc * ob.peak;            // the birth-snapshot growth lands here: the cycle counter scales the whole orbit's rate (om = speed/ea)
    const om = speed / ea;
    const cs = Math.cos(phi), sn = Math.sin(phi);
    const tvx = -ea * Math.sin(t0), tvy = eb * Math.cos(t0);
    return {
      returns: true, arc: 0, age: 0, armed: 0, latch: 0, peak: 0,   // the r38c flight-state family (latch/peak are the pass-through deep-clearance machinery — untouched)
      oa: ea, ob: eb, oph: phi, ot: t0, osn: sense,   // the ORBIT, FROZEN at the throw — the world-anchored path the pure-touch catch intercepts
      vx: (tvx * cs - tvy * sn) * sense * om, vy: (tvx * sn + tvy * cs) * sense * om,
      speed: speed,
    };
  }

  /* chaosorbit-r54 — THE DRAWN ARC IS THE HITBOX. The flying boomerang is a COPY of the weapon art
   * (the copy rule): a ~100px arc pivoted at copyCtr and oriented along its velocity — while its
   * hitbox was the bare r=10 pivot disc. The eye watched the arc sit INSIDE a body for a quarter
   * second with nothing dealt (owner catch, seed 3593: "the boomerang is clearly inside speedy but
   * no damage is dealt"), and every later pass of a latched throw read dead for the same reason.
   * The weapon-poly doctrine (draw and hitbox cannot drift apart) extended to the copy flight:
   * these are the row's OWN covering circles, transformed exactly as drawPolySet's copy path
   * transforms the art (offset by -copyCtr, rotated by the velocity heading). Body, blade, cross
   * and catch tests all read them — what the eye sees is what touches. */
  const BOOM_CS = [];
  const BOOM_CS2 = [];   // second scratch bank (catchghost-r58): the loop-pair cross tests arc against arc
  function boomCircles(G, st, out) {
    const w = G.fighters[st.o].weapon, ctr = copyCtr(w);
    /* snapfix-r57 — THE HITBOX FOLLOWS THE DRAWN TUMBLE (owner screenshot: Speedy flashing from a
     * hit while the drawn arc visibly sat away from him, "there is a gap between"): drawShot's copy
     * path orients the flying arc by COPYSPIN (phaseT·0.05 — the countable tumble), NOT by the
     * velocity heading; the chaosorbit-r54 hitbox read the heading, so the invisible arc could
     * touch a body while the drawn arc pointed somewhere else — damage with a gap. The hitbox now
     * reads the EXACT angle the renderer reads: what flashes is what touches. */
    const ang = COPYSPIN.boom ? G.phaseT * COPYSPIN.boom : Math.atan2(st.vy, st.vx);
    const c = Math.cos(ang), s = Math.sin(ang);
    out.length = 0;
    for (const ci of WEAPONS[w].poly.circles) {
      const qd = ci.d - ctr[0], ql = ci.l - ctr[1];
      out.push(st.x + qd * c - ql * s, st.y + qd * s + ql * c, ci.r);
    }
    return out;
  }
  function boomGap(G, st, px, py, pr) {   // true surface gap from a point-circle (px, py, pr) to the drawn arc — negative on contact
    const BC = boomCircles(G, st, BOOM_CS);
    let g = Infinity;
    for (let ci = 0; ci < BC.length; ci += 3) { const d = Math.hypot(px - BC[ci], py - BC[ci + 1]) - BC[ci + 2] - pr; if (d < g) g = d; }
    return g;
  }
  /* shotGap (chaosorbit-r54's generic shot-vs-shot arc-side helper) stays retired since
   * catchonly-r56 — but this note's "the plain disc distance is the whole law" went stale at
   * snapfix-r57/catchghost-r58: the cross test DOES have an arc side again, inline in its two
   * returns branches (the one-sided test via boomGap, the pair test arc-against-arc through
   * BOOM_CS/BOOM_CS2). The plain-disc distance is the whole law for every OTHER pair.
   * (review-r60 comment correction; no code moved.) */

  function fireShots(G, fs, sdt) {
    for (const f of fs) {
      if (!f.alive) continue;
      const W = WEAPONS[f.weapon];
      if (!W.shot) continue;
      if (f.catchWait > 0) f.catchWait = Math.max(0, f.catchWait - sdt);   // chaosorbit-r54: the hand-rest countdown (seconds, substep-stepped like every clock) — the accumulator KEEPS BANKING under it, so the rethrow leaves exactly when the wait expires
      f.fireAcc += Math.abs(f.spin) * chillMul(f) * bloomMul(f) * sdt;   // affinity-r66 → chillfix-r71: fireAcc counts the ACTUAL swung revolutions — bloomfix-r77: a bloomed swing is a slow swing, the bank follows honestlyUAL swept angle (wAngle advances by spin×chill), so the cast cadence slows only as the swing slows — per-rev honesty, not a second slow on the body
      /* SHOT-CADENCE MULTIPLIER SEAM (seam-r30, owner-authorized hook target). The weapon row and
       * the fighter's skill BOTH contribute and they ADD (owner ruling: stacking adds); the result
       * divides the accumulator's `need`, so an effective 2 fires the same volley twice as often.
       * Cadence rather than extra projectiles per release, because `revs` already owns "how much
       * spin per volley" and a fan already exists as `shot.volley` — a third way to mean "more
       * shots" would be one too many. Guarded positive at boot. NO ROW DECLARES IT YET: this is the
       * seam, not a carrier, so the sim is behaviour-identical until something uses it. */
      const smul = 1 + (W.shot.mult || 0) + ((FIGHTERS[f.idx].skill && FIGHTERS[f.idx].skill.shotMult) || 0) + ((W.trait && W.trait.mult) || 0) * Math.min(f.shotStep, MULT_STEPS);   // multgrow-r42: the capped rain term — additive on the seam's axis per the stacking doctrine; shotStep serves the launchers like shotR/cycle serve melee
      const need = TAU * (W.shot.revs || 1) / (smul > 0 ? smul : 1);   // revolutions of accumulated spin per volley (knives 3, everyone else 1), scaled by the multiplier
      /* the birth radius (shotgrow-r33) — trait.shotR's ONE consumer site. A row without shotR
       * gets exactly W.shot.r (Math.pow(1, n) === 1 and x * 1 === x, bit-identical); the staff's
       * orb compounds (1 + rate)^f.shotStep over the holder's landings this round. Birth
       * snapshot only — in-flight shots never resize (the `dmg: f.dmg` precedent), so the hit
       * audit's stored `sr` and the rim/swat/cross tests all read one constant radius per shot. */
      const effR = W.shot.r * Math.pow(1 + ((W.trait && W.trait.shotR) || 0), f.shotStep);
      /* the loop CYCLE growth (the boomerang's Return trait, returngrow-r37): speed and turn scale
       * TOGETHER, so the loop radius (speed/turn) stays LOCKED while the period (2π/turn) shrinks —
       * the throw reaches just as far and comes home sooner. Capped at CYCLE_STEPS at read time
       * (the first capped growth axis: a faster loop has no physical wall — see the const).
       * pow(x, 0) === 1 keeps every non-cycle row bit-identical. Birth snapshot only — the effR
       * doctrine: in-flight shots never change. */
      const cyc = W.trait && W.trait.cycle ? Math.pow(1 + W.trait.cycle, Math.min(f.shotStep, CYCLE_STEPS)) : 1;
    /* r38 SINGLETON (owner: "only 1 boomerang flying" — REAFFIRMED 2026-11-01, r59: "i know there
     * is only one boomerang at a time from the same bot, but maybe when balancing we introduce
     * more"): one returning shot per owner at a time — while it is out the gate holds and the
     * accumulator KEEPS BANKING. The chaosorbit-r54 hand-rest gate (f.catchWait) is DORMANT since
     * instantthrow-r59 (RETHROW_WAIT 0 — the owner reversed his r54 eye: "just instantly throw
     * it"); the gate stays wired so the beat is one constant away.
     * Non-returns rows short-circuit on the falsy flag — bit-identical. */
      if (f.figT > 0 && f.weapon === 'wand') f.fireAcc = Math.min(f.fireAcc, need);   // bloom-r73 — the bloomed wand banks exactly ONE comet; the poof instant answers with a single honest throw
      while (f.figT <= 0 && f.fireAcc >= need && !(W.shot.returns && (f.catchWait > 0 || G.shots.some(s => s.o === f.slot && s.returns)))) {   // the singleton gate plus the (dormant, RETHROW_WAIT 0) hand-rest gate — instantthrow-r59: the banked revolution fires on the substep after the catch
        f.fireAcc -= need;
        const c = Math.cos(f.wAngle), s = Math.sin(f.wAngle);
        const fr = spineFrame(f.pos.x, f.pos.y, f.wAngle, f.weapon);
        let x = fr.ox + fr.dx * fr.span * 0.5, y = fr.oy + fr.dy * fr.span * 0.5;   // spine t = 0.5: the weapon's middle (v0.7.2) — for the tangential hold, the grip point on the rim
        const dir = f.spin > 0 ? 1 : -1;                 // tangential release in the spin direction
        const tipF = W.shot.fire === 'tip';              // radial-hold launchers (staff, wand): leave the TIP, along the spine (launch doctrine, owner 2026-10-19)
        const rad = W.shot.fire === 'radial' || tipF;    // 'radial': out of the grip along the belly's facing, whatever the spin sign (bow, crossbow)
        if (tipF) { x = fr.ox + fr.dx * fr.span; y = fr.oy + fr.dy * fr.span; }
        else if (rad) { x += c * W.shot.off; y += s * W.shot.off; }   // head starts at the bow's belly, the nocked arrow's tail on the string
        if (W.shot.copy) {   // copy rule: the throw IS the weapon — spawn at the art centre (owner catch 2026-10-25: grip spawns made the copy orbit/snap). Row-declared since the 2026-10-28 consolidation, so there is no keying left to get wrong (COPYW was weapon-id keyed; canonical COPYKIND is kind-keyed — javelin's id/kind coincidence hid that for one weapon)
          const ctr = copyCtr(f.weapon);
          x = fr.ox + ctr[0] * fr.dx - ctr[1] * fr.dy;
          y = fr.oy + ctr[0] * fr.dy + ctr[1] * fr.dx;
        }
        /* `kind`: rows with a `cycle` advance it on every launch (state f.cycleIdx);
         * everyone else uses the row's single kind. Hoisted above the branch so both
         * paths share one expression — no row declares both today, and for a row that
         * did, the cycle would advance once per VOLLEY (not per projectile), which is
         * the reading the pre-consolidation code gave the tome. */
        const kinds = W.shot.cycle;
        const kind = kinds ? kinds[f.cycleIdx = (f.cycleIdx + 1) % kinds.length] : (W.shot.kind || null);
        const pR = kinds ? trioRadius(W, f, kind) : effR;   // affinity-r66: cycle rows take the element-gated birth radius (spellform-r69: FIRE's swell sleeps at the owner's shape grammar — all pages born at the row r); every non-cycle row keeps shotgrow-r33's effR BIT-IDENTICAL
        if (W.shot.volley) {   // fan: one projectile per anchor, each along its own blade-local axis
          for (const ka of grownVolley(W, f)) {   // fan-r43: grown anchors for the knives; the static row array for every other volley row (there is none today)
            const a2 = ka[2] * Math.PI / 180, vd = Math.sin(a2), vl = -Math.cos(a2);   // blade-local axis: out along -l, fanned toward ±d
            const wx = fr.ox + ka[0] * fr.dx - ka[1] * fr.dy, wy = fr.oy + ka[0] * fr.dy + ka[1] * fr.dx;   // SPINE-FRAME axes, never wAngle trig
            let sx2 = wx, sy2 = wy;
            { const dxc = sx2 - CFG.size / 2, dyc = sy2 - CFG.size / 2, dr = Math.hypot(dxc, dyc);   // rim clamp: a tip outside the arena would die on its spawn tick (owner-visible pop)
              if (dr + effR > CFG.size / 2 - 0.5) { const k2 = (CFG.size / 2 - 0.5 - effR) / dr; sx2 = CFG.size / 2 + dxc * k2; sy2 = CFG.size / 2 + dyc * k2; } }
            const vcx = vd * fr.dx - vl * fr.dy, vcy = vd * fr.dy + vl * fr.dx;
            const vsid = ++G.shotSid;
            const bvx = vcx * W.shot.speed * cyc, bvy = vcy * W.shot.speed * cyc;   // r38c: hoisted so the returns spread can lock the oval's long axis to the launch heading
            G.shots.push({
              sid: vsid, o: f.slot, x: sx2, y: sy2, px: sx2, py: sy2,
              vx: bvx, vy: bvy,
              r: pR, speed: W.shot.speed * cyc, len: W.shot.len || 0,
              kind: kind, turn: bornBend(G, W, f) * cyc, bounce: W.shot.bounce || 0,   // bendspark-r61: the birth turn now comes off bornBend (row base + shared-counter growth, per-throw rng sign) — the old expression multiplied the row base by the SPIN SIGN (the retired pre-orbit boomerang semantics); no other row declares shot.turn, so every non-wand spawn stays exactly 0
              ...(W.shot.ricochet ? { ricochet: true } : null), ...(W.shot.pin ? { pin: true } : null), ...(W.shot.skewer ? { skewer: true } : null), ...(W.shot.hex ? { hex: true } : null),   // hexspark-r65: the hex flag rides the restored flagfix line — and per the r64 STANDING LAW a spawn-line edit re-runs the whole flag battery (smoke-r64) with this landing. ricolaw-r41: `bounce` is a FROZEN HASH FIELD (fingerprint.mjs hashes it by name — always 0 since the budget law retired); the ricochet flag is row-owned flight state like the returns spread. flagfix-r64: these three spreads were COMMENT TEXT from r61 to r63 — the bendspark-r61 edit's new_text ran the comment marker past them, swallowing the flag law for the shuriken's eternal ricochet, the crossbow's nails and the javelin's skewer; restored as code on their own line (found at the owner's eye: "looks like all our pin logic doesnt work anymore")
              ...(W.shot.returns ? orbitThrow(G, W, sx2, sy2, cyc) : null),   // touchorbit-r53 flight state ONLY on returning rows — every other shot's hashed fields stay byte-identical; chaosorbit-r54: the solve reads no foe (pure chaos)
              dmg: f.dmg, born: G.t, x0: sx2, y0: sy2,
            });
            G.stats.thrown++;
            emit(G, 'shotFire', {
              by: f.slot, sid: vsid, x: sx2, y: sy2, dmg: f.dmg,
              fx: f.pos.x, fy: f.pos.y, fAng: f.wAngle,
            });
          }
        } else {
                  const sid = ++G.shotSid;
                  const svx = (rad ? c : -s * dir) * W.shot.speed * cyc, svy = (rad ? s : c * dir) * W.shot.speed * cyc;   // r38c: hoisted so the returns spread can lock the oval's long axis to the launch heading
                  G.shots.push({
                    sid: sid, o: f.slot, x: x, y: y, px: x, py: y,   // px/py: interpolation base, snapped at birth — shots fade in from their own launch point, never from (0,0)
                    vx: svx, vy: svy,
                    r: pR, speed: W.shot.speed * cyc, len: W.shot.len || 0,
                    kind: kind, turn: bornBend(G, W, f) * cyc, bounce: W.shot.bounce || 0,   // bendspark-r61: the birth turn now comes off bornBend (row base + shared-counter growth, per-throw rng sign) — the old expression multiplied the row base by the SPIN SIGN (the retired pre-orbit boomerang semantics); no other row declares shot.turn, so every non-wand spawn stays exactly 0
              ...(W.shot.ricochet ? { ricochet: true } : null), ...(W.shot.pin ? { pin: true } : null), ...(W.shot.skewer ? { skewer: true } : null), ...(W.shot.hex ? { hex: true } : null),   // hexspark-r65: the hex flag rides the restored flagfix line — and per the r64 STANDING LAW a spawn-line edit re-runs the whole flag battery (smoke-r64) with this landing. ricolaw-r41: `bounce` is a FROZEN HASH FIELD (fingerprint.mjs hashes it by name — always 0 since the budget law retired); the ricochet flag is row-owned flight state like the returns spread. flagfix-r64: these three spreads were COMMENT TEXT from r61 to r63 — the bendspark-r61 edit's new_text ran the comment marker past them, swallowing the flag law for the shuriken's eternal ricochet, the crossbow's nails and the javelin's skewer; restored as code on their own line (found at the owner's eye: "looks like all our pin logic doesnt work anymore")
                    ...(W.shot.returns ? orbitThrow(G, W, x, y, cyc) : null),   // touchorbit-r53 flight state ONLY on returning rows — every other shot's hashed fields stay byte-identical; chaosorbit-r54: the solve reads no foe (pure chaos)
                    dmg: f.dmg, born: G.t, x0: x, y0: y,          // launched with the thrower's current damage
                  });
                  if (W.trait && W.trait.ember) { const ns = G.shots[G.shots.length - 1]; ns.eiv = Math.max(EMBER.dropMin, EMBER.drop - EMBER.dropCut * Math.min(f.shotStep, EMBER.steps)); ns.emb = 0; }   // kindling-r82 — an ember row's flight is BORN with its shed cadence (the effR doctrine: the stacks at the cast, not at the drop)
                  G.stats.thrown++;
